items.summary: We study the hyperbolic $p$-barycenters $C_p$, $0\le p\le\infty$, of $n$ points $α_1,\ldots,α_n$ in the hyperbolic plane. For $0<p<\infty$, $C_p$ minimizes the sum of the $p$th powers of the hyperbolic cosines of the distances to the points. At the endpoints, $C_0$ minimizes the product of these cosines and $C_\infty$ their maximum. The center map $p\mapsto C_p$ is real analytic at every finite parameter. A point $P$ is the center for every parameter exactly when, at each positive distance from $P$, the unit directions to the points at that distance sum to zero. If the map is nonconstant, the equation $C_p=P$ has at most $n-2$ solutions in $[0,\infty]$ for each $P$, and at most $\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor$ when the points lie on a geodesic. Finite solutions are counted with multiplicity, and the endpoint contributes one if $C_\infty=P$. Each bound is attained in arbitrarily small disks, with prescribed finite parameters and multiplicities, and with or without the endpoint. The proofs use exponential sums over distance shells, a variation-diminishing property of the radial-weight kernel, and the Hobby--Rice theorem. For the upper-half-plane roots of a totally complex real binary form, $C_0$ is Julia's zero and $C_1$ is the hyperbolic zero. Their coincidence forces the center map to be constant in degrees at most six, but counterexamples exist in every even degree at least eight. We obtain the same bounds on the number of distinct parameters for Riemannian $L^q$ centers, the minimizers of $\sum_i d(P,α_i)^q$ on Hadamard manifolds for $1<q<\infty$.

items.title: ab-indices for lattice path matroids
items.summary: The base polytopes of connected lattice path matroids admit subdivisions into snakes. We use these to obtain an explicit positive combinatorial description of their ab-indices, their Chow polynomials and their chain polynomials. We finally apply this description to the particular case of the ab-index of Schubert matroids.

items.title: Extension of results on generalized Pólya's urns for polynomially self-repelling walks
items.summary: This is a technical note which extends the results of Kosygina, Mountford and Peterson (Ann. Probab., 51(5):1684-1728, 2023, Section 4) about generalized Pólya's urns from a specific weight function $w(n) = (n+1)^{-α}$ to a general family of weight functions satisfying $(w(n))^{-1}=n^α\left(1+2Bn^{-1}+O\left(n^{-2}\right)\right)$ as $n \to \infty$. The latter was considered by Tóth (Ann. Probab., 24(3):1324-1367, 1996) as a part of his study of polynomially self-repelling walks. This extension is used in the study of scaling limits of these walks and related processes; see arXiv:2610.28935 and arXiv:2610.38591.

items.title: Minimality of $T_z^*$-Invariant Subspaces of $H^2(\mathbb D^2)$
items.summary: In this paper, we establish necessary conditions for the minimality of infinite-dimensional $T_z^*$-invariant subspaces of $H^2(\mathbb D^2)$. More precisely, we prove that if $M\subset H^2(\mathbb D^2)$ is an infinite-dimensional, minimal $T_z^*$-invariant subspace, then, for every $n\in\mathbb N_0$, either $\overline{P_n(M)}=H^2(\mathbb D)$ or $\overline{P_n(M)}^\perp =φ_{a,θ}H^2(\mathbb D)$ where $φ_{a,θ}$ is an atomic singular inner function and $P_n$ denotes the orthogonal projection of $H^2(\mathbb D^2)$ onto $H^2(z)w^n$. As $T_z^*$ is a universal operator on $H^2(\mathbb D^2)$, this result reduces the Invariant Subspace Problem to the analysis of these two alternatives for infinite-dimensional minimal $T_z^*$-invariant subspaces.

items.title: Formulation-dependent linearized buckling of stiffened shell panels: role of the stress stiffness operator
items.summary: Linearized buckling loads of stiffened panels can diverge across commercial shell formulations because six-degree-of-freedom elements treat drilling rotations and director kinematics differently in the stress stiffness operator. We derive three analytical stress stiffness operators (membrane-only, uncoupled rotational-block, and shear-coupled full second-variation forms), verified against an exact second-difference energy identity. Using direct matrix extraction in ANSYS (SHELL181, SHELL281) and modal and strain-energy benchmarks in Abaqus (S4, S8R), we classify these commercial elements across twelve configurations. On the finest cantilevered shear-panel mesh (in-plane bending and shear), the SHELL181 perturbation and classic procedures predict load factors 11.3% and 28.5% above an independent 3D continuum reference. By contrast, Abaqus S4 and ANSYS SHELL281 lie 5.2% and 5.8% below this reference and remain indistinguishable from the analytical full form within the junction-idealization uncertainty, while Abaqus S8R lies 20.1% below the reference. The tested cases indicate that substantial divergence occurs only when non-coplanar junctions carry pre-stress bending or transverse shear and the buckling mode involves junction drilling rotations. Under pure axial compression or uniform membrane shear flow, the analytical operators coincide and within-element procedures agree within 0.06%. Because buckling under in-plane bending and shear is formulation-dependent, stability design and layout optimization of built-up panels require cross-verification across shell elements or continuum models.

items.title: Directed acyclic graph-type distributed ledgers via young-age preferential attachment
items.summary: Distributed Ledger Technologies provide a mechanism to achieve ordering among transactions that are scattered on multiple participants with no prerequisite trust relations. This mechanism is essentially based on the idea of new transactions referencing older ones in a chain structure. Recently, DAG-type Distributed Ledgers that are based on directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) were proposed to increase the system scalability through sacrificing the total order of transactions. In this paper, we develop a mathematical model to study the process that governs the addition of new transactions to the DAG-type Distributed Ledger. We propose a simple model for DAG-type Distributed Ledgers that are obtained from a recursive Young-age Preferential Attachment scheme, i.e. new connections are made preferably to transactions that have not been in the system for very long. We determine the asymptotic degree structure of the resulting graph and show that a forward component of linear size arises if the edge density is chosen sufficiently large in relation to the `young-age preference' that tunes how quickly old transactions become unattractive.

items.title: Patterson-Sullivan Theory for Approximate Groups
items.summary: In this paper we consider the limit set of a uniformly discrete approximate subgroup acting on a negatively curved manifold, and prove several properties comparable to that of the classical case of discrete groups, including a version of the dichotomy between elementary and non-elementary groups. Furthermore, we adapt the Patterson-Sullivan construction for discrete groups to obtain asymptotic counting results for the orbits of infinite uniformly discrete approximate groups acting on a negatively curved manifold.

items.title: An approach to topology via lattices of names
items.summary: Synthetic topology encompasses various alternatives to the classical definition of a topological space by Hausdorff. In particular, Abstract Stone Duality (ASD) develops the theory of locally compact spaces directly from logic. This study introduces a semi-formal theory of synthetic topology using a first-order version of the intuitionistic modal logic iS4, inspired by a nominalist, dynamic interpretation of the specialization order. The remarkable similarities to ASD include a constructive interpretation of the open-closed duality, overtness of the line, compactness of the unit interval and the nuclei that define closed and open subspaces.

items.title: Even Quartets and the Maximum Density of a Simplical 3-Cocycle
items.summary: Colour the triples of an $n$-element set red or blue, and call a four-set even if it contains an even number of red triples. We prove that the minimum number of even four-sets is $\frac5{16}\binom n4-Θ(n^3)$. In particular, the maximum asymptotic density of a simplicial $3$-cocycle over the field of two elements is $11/16$. The classical two-part matrix construction attains the limiting bound. We prove that it also determines the unique limiting distribution of quartet parities on every fixed number of vertices. Writing $m_n$ for the minimum density, we bound the limit inferior and limit superior of $n(5/16-m_n)$ between $0.75$ and $0.752427$. The lower bound on even quartets follows from an exact rational inequality on eight vertices. A perturbation of the construction explains all $72$ cases of equality in this finite inequality, of which only $22$ survive in an extremal limit.

items.title: Multivariable Alexander polynomials of twisted torus links via Dehn surgery
items.summary: Let $T(p,q;r,s)$ be the twisted torus link obtained from the torus link $T(p,q)$ by adding $s$ full twists to $r$ adjacent strands, and let $C$ be an unknotted circle encircling those strands. For all $p$, $q$, and $r$ we compute the multivariable Alexander polynomial of $T(p,q)\cup C$ in closed form. A relation of Silver and Williams between the Alexander polynomials of a link and of its $1/n$ Dehn fillings then gives a closed formula for the multivariable Alexander polynomial of every twisted torus link $T(p,q;r,s)$, answering a question of Adnan and Park. When $\gcd(p,q)=1$, so that $T(p,q;r,s)$ is a knot, the formula is a sum of $pr$ monomials with coefficient $+1$, divided by cyclotomic factors, and its exponents are governed by an elementary counting function on the orbit of $q$ modulo $p$. Because the numerator has no cancellation, we are able to give the degree for all $s$ and simple non-fiberedness and non-L-space criteria for infinite families of twisted torus knots.

items.title: On Hecke algebras at exceptional Eisenstein primes
items.summary: We study the structure over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ of the Hecke algebra acting on ordinary cusp forms in the Eisenstein, non-$p$-distinguished case. Our results and methods draw on four complementary approaches: deformation theory, through $R=\mathbf{T}$ theorems; Iwasawa theory, through connections to Sharifi's conjecture; $p$-adic $L$-functions, through an exceptional zero formula; and computational experiments using Magma. We also obtain new results regarding the Coleman--Greenberg conjecture.

items.title: The word problem in verbal products of groups
items.summary: We prove that nilpotent and metabelian products of groups with decidable word problem have decidable word problem. In contrast, we exhibit families of groups with decidable word problem for which their solvable product has undecidable word problem. In doing so, we exhibit hyperbolic groups with undecidable membership problem in their derived subgroups.

items.title: Sharp variational estimates for Schrödinger equation in higher dimensions
items.summary: We study strong $r$-variation estimates for the free Schrödinger equation on $\mathbb R^n$, $n\geq3$. Combining fractal and weighted restriction estimates with mixed space--time estimates, we determine the sharp Sobolev regularity, up to endpoints, in several ranges of the spatial exponent $p$ and the variation exponent $r$. In particular, our results give a sharp $L^2(\mathbb R^n)$ variational extension of the Schrödinger maximal estimate of Du and Zhang [\emph{Ann. of Math.}, \textbf{189}, 837--861 (2019)].

items.title: Positive recurrence of weakly reversible stochastic reaction networks with mass-action kinetics
items.summary: We study finite stochastic reaction networks with mass-action kinetics. A network is weakly reversible if every reaction lies on a directed cycle of complexes. We prove that, for arbitrary positive rate constants, the Markov chain of every such network is non-explosive and positive recurrent on each communicating class. This settles the long-standing chemical recurrence conjecture. The proof is by construction of a Lyapunov function. For a fixed choice of weights on the species, the function is the exponential of a weighted count of the molecules, adjusted by a bounded quantity which is defined through the paths of reactions leading back to a reference population, and which accounts for the species that are absent or scarce. Before the adjusted count can decrease, several preparatory steps may be needed. We count faster and slower steps separately, giving priority to paths that require fewer slow steps. Weak reversibility controls how competing reactions can change these counts. Finitely many choices of weights are then combined, and a minimization over a scale parameter gives a single function on each communicating class.

items.title: The integer group determinants for the abelian groups of order 27
items.summary: We completely determine the integer group determinants for $\mathbb Z_3 \times \mathbb Z_9$ by resolving the allowable multiples of $3$. This completes the Taussky-Todd integer group determinant problem for the abelian groups of order $27$.

items.title: Hybridizable Discontinuous Galerkin methods for the Keller-Segel model
items.summary: We propose a hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) finite element method to approximate the solution of the time-dependent Keller-Segel model, a drift-diffusion system describing chemotactic cell movement. We develop and analyze the corresponding HDG scheme, and establish theoretical convergence results for the proposed discretization. Finally, we present numerical experiments that confirm the theoretical findings.

items.title: Higher Order Unfitted Discontinuous Galerkin Methods in Space and Time
items.summary: We present and analyse an unfitted space-time discontinuous Galerkin (DG) method of arbitrary order for convection-diffusion problems on moving domains in up to three space dimensions. The method is discontinuous in space and time and uses upwind fluxes, so that convection is stabilised without additional terms and a Ghost penalty is needed only in the vicinity of the moving boundary. We prove inf-sup stability in a problem-specific norm, which in addition to the coercive part controls the time derivative in the diffusion-dominated regime and the material derivative in the convection-dominated regime. From this we derive a priori error estimates of high order in space and time for both regimes, including vanishing diffusion. Numerical experiments confirm the convergence rates and the robustness with respect to the diffusion coefficient.

items.title: Spanning cyclability of split graphs
items.summary: For a positive integer $k$, a graph $G$ is called $k$-spanning cyclable (resp. $k$-edge spanning cyclable) if, given any $k$ distinct vertices $v_1, v_2, \ldots, v_k$ (resp. $k$ independent edges $e_1, e_2, \ldots, e_k$) of $G$, there exist $k$ vertex-disjoint cycles $C_1, C_2, \ldots, C_k$ in $G$ such that $v_i \in V(C_i)$ (resp. $e_i \in E(C_i)$) for each $i$ and $V(C_1) \cup \cdots \cup V(C_k) = V(G)$. In particular, the notion of 1-spanning cyclable coincides with the existence of a Hamiltonian cycle, and a Hamilton-connected graph is necessarily 1-edge spanning cyclable. For a positive integer $r \ge 3$, a graph $G$ is $K_{1,r}$-free if $G$ does not have an induced subgraph isomorphic to $K_{1,r}$, and $K_{1,4} + e$ denotes the graph obtained by adding an edge $e$ between two nonadjacent vertices of $K_{1,4}$. There are several interesting conjectures and sparse results relative to these conjectures on Hamiltonian properties of $K_{1,r}$-free split graphs, whose vertex set can be partitioned into a maximum clique $W$ and an independent set $J$. In this paper, we extend some of these results by proving the following: (1) every $(k+1)$-connected $K_{1,3}$-free split graph of order at least $4k-1$ is $k$-spanning cyclable for $k \ge 1$; in particular, every 2-connected $K_{1,3}$-free split graph of order at least 3 is Hamiltonian; (2) every $2k$-connected $K_{1,3}$-free split graph is $k$-edge spanning cyclable for $k \ge 2$; (3) every $(k+1)$-connected $\{K_{1,4}, K_{1,4}+e\}$-free split graph with $|W| \ge |J| \ge 3k+5$ is $k$-spanning cyclable for $k \ge 1$; in particular, every 2-connected $\{K_{1,4}, K_{1,4}+e\}$-free split graph with $|W| \ge |J| \ge 8$ is Hamiltonian; (4) every $2k$-connected $\{K_{1,4}, K_{1,4}+e\}$-free split graph with order at least $4k+9$ is $k$-edge spanning cyclable for $k \ge 2$.

items.title: Glauber dynamics for random field Ising models on bounded degree graphs and MLSI
items.summary: We study the ferromagnetic random field Ising model (RFIM) on a graph $G=(V,E)$ having maximal degree $Δ$, where the external field at each vertex is an i.i.d. random variable. When the random field distribution is sufficiently anti-concentrated, we prove that with high probability over the quenched randomness of the external field, the Glauber dynamics of this RFIM mixes in polynomial time as a consequence of a Poincaré inequality. This model is relevant to the Griffiths phase where the correlations decay exponentially fast in expectation over the quenched random field, but contraction does not hold point-wise due to the existence of weak fields that lead to low-temperature behavior. Previously, fast mixing of Glauber dynamics under large disorder was only proven on the integer lattice, and for RFIM on general graphs, only a sampling algorithm based on self-avoiding walks was known. Under a further technical condition that the random fields are bounded, we prove a modified log-Sobolev inequality for the Glauber dynamics. When the random field is weaker but still satisfies weak spatial mixing (exponential decay of correlations from boundary to bulk) in expectation, and the graph has $α$-stretched-exponential growth for some $α<1$, we prove a weak Poincaré inequality. If weak spatial mixing holds uniformly along a given sequence of growing induced subgraphs, we further obtain a polynomial-time sampling algorithm based on Glauber dynamics with warm starts. These results extend the corresponding weak Poincaré and sampling results from the integer lattice to graphs with $α$-stretched-exponential growth.

items.title: Universality for persistence exponents of local times of self-similar processes with stationary increments
items.summary: We show that $\mathbb{P} ( \ell_X(0,T] \leq 1)=(c_X+o(1))T^{-(1-H)}$, where $\ell_X$ is the local time measure at $0$ of any recurrent $H$-self-similar real-valued process $X$ with stationary increments that admits a sufficiently regular local time and $c_X$ is some constant depending only on $X$. A special case is the Gaussian setting, i.e. when the underlying process is fractional Brownian motion, in which our result settles a conjecture by Molchan [Commun. Math. Phys. 205, 97-111 (1999)] who obtained the upper bound $1-H$ on the decay exponent of $\mathbb{P} ( \ell_X(0,T] \leq 1)$. Our approach establishes a new connection between persistence probabilities and Palm theory for self-similar random measures, thereby providing a general framework which extends far beyond the Gaussian case.

items.title: Subword enumeration up to stack-sorting equivalence
items.summary: Defant and Kravitz introduced generalizations of West's stack-sorting map $s$ from permutations to finite words. This raises questions as to how such generalizations could be applied in the field of combinatorics on words. The Defant-Kravitz generalizations of $s$ depend on how repeated occurrences of the same character within a word may be repositioned, according to their $\textsf{tortoise}$ and $\textsf{hare}$ operations. As demonstrated in this paper, these operations provide a natural way of extending abelian complexity functions for infinite sequences, in a way that gives light to structural properties associated with infinite words. We apply these new ideas to two famous infinite words: the paperfolding word and the Thue-Morse word. In the case of the Thue-Morse word, we discover an interesting connection to the previous work of several authors, such as de Luca and Varricchio, on the ``special'' factors of the Thue-Morse word. This may be seen as providing a basis for a new and interdisciplinary area linking the combinatorics about the stack-sorting of permutations with the field of combinatorics on words.

items.title: Mirror flow for semimartingale optimal transport
items.summary: Semimartingale optimal transport arises in a wide range of applications, including mathematical finance and flow-based generative models. A recurring computational challenge is that the dual energy functional is often poorly conditioned with respect to the dual potential, leading to slow convergence of gradient descent algorithms. To address this issue, we investigate a mirror flow approach that effectively preconditions the dual energy functional. We establish the geometric convergence of the mirror descent sequence. To obtain a practical numerical algorithm, we introduce a feasible discrete-time scheme based on first-order linearization. We prove that the scheme is well-defined and establish a uniform-in-time error bound for the accumulated linearization error, under a suitable smallness condition on the initial error. Finally, we apply the proposed mirror flow scheme to the specific-entropic martingale optimal transport (SEMOT) problem \cite{BuetGolfouseEtAl2026SEMOT} and observe a substantial improvement in computational efficiency.

items.title: Convergence of Implicit Particle Methods for Wasserstein Gradient Flows
items.summary: In this paper, we establish the convergence of implicit particle methods for Wasserstein gradient flows as the number of particles tends to infinity, with the time step held fixed. The schemes combine the Jordan--Kinderlehrer--Otto (JKO) variational time discretization with particle approximations of the evolving probability measure. The main challenge lies in approximating the internal energy, which depends nonlinearly on the probability density and cannot, in general, be evaluated directly on empirical measures. We consider three approaches: a one-dimensional density reconstruction based on the spacings between ordered particles; a blob method using kernel-based density reconstruction; and a transport-map formulation in which the density is recovered from the pushforward relation through the change-of-variables formula. The latter two approaches apply in arbitrary spatial dimensions without requiring the spatial domain to be compact. For the blob method, we also establish simultaneous convergence as the particle number tends to infinity and the regularization parameter vanishes, under the scaling $N\varepsilon_N^d\to\infty$. Our analysis combines $Γ$-convergence and compactness arguments to establish convergence of the discrete variational problems and their minimizers. These results complement classical dynamical mean-field theory by providing a variational particle-to-continuum limit for implicit JKO schemes involving nonlinear internal energies.

items.title: On a conjecture of Velani
items.summary: We investigate the approximation of elements of the middle-third Cantor set by dyadic rationals, and natural extensions. We prove a conjecture of Velani, completing the metric theory for the Cantor measure. Our key method enables a quantitative study of the incommensurability of binary and ternary expansions of integers, initiated by Furstenberg. The method has other applications, e.g. $\sum_{k} |\hatμ(2^k)|^σ< \infty$ for any $σ> 0$, where $μ$ is the Cantor measure.

items.title: Discrete unique continuation for Schrödinger equations
items.summary: We study discrete unique continuation for one-dimensional Schrödinger equations. We prove that if a solution vanishes at the points $\pm n^α$ at time $0$ and at the points $\pm n^β$ at time $1$, it must vanish identically in two main cases: the case of a Schrödinger equation with a real potential that is uniformly of Gevrey class $σ\ge 0$ in space, provided that $\max\{1,σ\}\big(α/(1-α)+β/(1-β)\big)<1$, and in the case of the cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation, provided that $α/(1-α)+β/(1-β)<1$. Unlike previous results for logarithmically spaced zeros, our methods do not rely on complex analysis. We first show that, whenever $α+β<1$, the zeros force the solution to lie in the Schwartz class at all times. We then convert the zeros into gaussian decay at the two times, by combining energy estimates for iterations of the vector field $Γ=x+2it\partial_x$ with techniques from Fourier uniqueness problems, and conclude with the Morgan-type uncertainty principle of Escauriaza, Kenig, Ponce and Vega.

items.title: NABLA: A Noise-Adaptive Blockwise Left-Right Preconditioning Algorithm for Stochastic Optimization
items.summary: We propose NABLA, a noise-adaptive blockwise left-right preconditioning algorithm for mini-batch stochastic nonconvex optimization. NABLA combines an exponential moving average of stochastic gradients with block-diagonal row and column preconditioners constructed from matrix-valued second-moment statistics. Unlike conventional matrix-preconditioned methods that use fixed decay parameters, NABLA adjusts the second-moment averaging coefficient through a closed-loop feedback rule determined by the cumulative stochastic-gradient energy and its running average. The first-moment coefficient remains fixed, allowing the trajectory-dependent adaptation to act directly on the structured preconditioners. The resulting method is horizon-free, requires no prior knowledge of the noise level, and automatically adjusts the memory of its second-moment estimators to the observed optimization dynamics. Under standard lower boundedness, smoothness, unbiasedness, bounded-variance, and spectral-boundedness assumptions, we establish uniform stability and variation bounds for the time-varying block preconditioners and control their interaction with momentum estimation and parameter updates. These results yield the noise-adaptive stationarity guarantee $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(T^{-1/2}+σ^{1/2}T^{-1/4})$, which automatically reduces to the nearly deterministic $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(T^{-1/2})$ rate when the stochastic-gradient noise vanishes. NABLA therefore provides a principled approach to combining closed-loop trajectory feedback with memory-efficient structured matrix preconditioning.

items.title: Mixed local and fractional laplacian problems with $(α,β)$-Neumann conditions
items.summary: The existence of non-constant solutions to a mixed local-nonlocal elliptic problem with $(α,β)$-Neumann conditions, critical exponent, and parameter $λ>0$ is established for any $λ$ large enough. Proofs exploit both mountain-pass-type arguments and appropriate boundary Sobolev inequalities patterned after those of [19].

items.title: A Unified Heat-Ball Framework for Fokker--Planck Equations: Mean-Value Identities, Exact Sampling, and Error Analysis
items.summary: Diffusion-based generative models with nonlinear or learned forward drifts raise questions that stay hidden for Gaussian forward processes: how the divergence-free and gradient parts of the drift shape the evolving density, whether sampling can draw on local rather than global information, and how to treat low-density regions, where $u$ carries a weak signal while $\log u$ diverges and the entropy density $u\log u$ falls between the two. These questions motivate the present study of local representations for Fokker--Planck equations with general, possibly nonlinear and time-dependent drift. We derive inhomogeneous heat-ball identities for the density $u$, the log-density $\log u$, the entropy density $u\log u$, and the score $\nabla\log u$, keeping the source terms generated by the drift; their unscaled residuals recover the corresponding differential residuals at leading order in the squared heat-ball radius. The weights appearing in the identities, the source integrals, and the integration-by-parts formulas all belong to a single Beta--Gamma family of measures on the heat ball, which gives exact rejection-free sampling, product quadrature, and unbiased Monte Carlo estimators with variance and cost bounds that are explicit in the dimension and the radius. Experiments with Gaussian-mixture and nonlinear-drift references, in dimensions up to $1024$ where applicable, confirm the sampling laws, the identities, and the residual behavior. In particular, log-density and score evaluations remain accurate where direct density estimation breaks down, and the heat-ball residuals provide local consistency tests for learned score models. A study of gauge-based heat-ball walks illustrates a recursive use of the density identity.

items.title: Quadratic Wasserstein transport for elliptical distributions
items.summary: The quadratic Wasserstein distance between Gaussian distributions is given by the classical Bures-Wasserstein formula, which depends only on the means, the covariance matrices $Σ_0$ and $Σ_1$, and their interaction $K=(Σ_0^{1/2}Σ_1Σ_0^{1/2})^{1/2}$. The same formula holds for elliptical distributions with a common radial law. In this paper, we extend this representation to general elliptical distributions by identifying an additional transport cost $Γ$ that depends on the radial laws and the spectrum of $K$. We describe $Γ$ via a weighted quadratic transport problem involving Dirichlet distributions and show that optimal couplings preserve directions within the eigenspaces of $K$. When $K$ has a single eigenvalue, we obtain an explicit cost formula and an optimal Monge map. For general spectra, we derive remarkably tight lower and upper bounds for $Γ$ using nested spectral projections and Knothe-Rosenblatt couplings. The lower bound is based on one-dimensional integrals and can be computed fast. For Gaussian, Student-$t$, uniform ball, and uniform sphere distributions, the upper bound also admits computationally efficient representations via dynamic programming. Numerical experiments demonstrate that we reduce the gap between the previously known bounds by more than 80% in many settings, and by over 99.9% in certain scenarios, even in dimension $10^6$. These improvements are particularly valuable in high-dimensional or heavy-tailed settings, where accurate numerical computation of quadratic Wasserstein distances is challenging.

items.title: Twisted $L^2$-torsion functions obstruct fibring over the circle
items.summary: The vanishing of the L^2-Betti numbers of the universal covering of a closed manifold is an obstruction to fibring over the circle. When the L^2-Betti numbers vanish we introduce a secondary obstruction based on the asymptotic behaviour of the twisted L^2-torsion function at 0 and infinity. We provide a number of examples showing the invariant is indeed non-trivial.

items.title: A $2$-adic Kida-type formula for chromatic Selmer groups of elliptic curves and applications to quadratic twists
items.summary: Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ with good supersingular reduction at $2$. We study the chromatic ($\sharp/\flat$) Selmer groups of $E$ over the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_2$-extension of $\mathbb{Q}$, defined using Sprung's chromatic Coleman maps. We show that at least one of these Selmer groups is $Λ$-cotorsion and, assuming the vanishing of the corresponding $μ$-invariant, establish a $2$-adic Kida-type formula describing the change in the Iwasawa $λ$-invariants under base change from $\mathbb{Q}$ to a real quadratic field $F$ in which $2$ is unramified. When $E$ has square-free conductor, applying this formula to $E$ and its quadratic twist $E^D$ yields an explicit formula describing the variation of the chromatic $λ$-invariants under twists by positive square-free integers $D\equiv1\pmod4$. As an application, under suitable hypotheses on the root number and chromatic Iwasawa invariants of $E$, we construct explicit sets of primes $\ell$ such that the $2^{\infty}$-Selmer group of $E^{\ell}$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ has $\mathbb{Z}_2$-corank one, and determine their positive natural densities.

items.title: A disproof of the van Emde Boas--Kruyswijk conjecture on the Davenport constant
items.summary: The Davenport constant $D(G)$ of a finite abelian group $G$ is the smallest positive integer $\ell$ such that every sequence $S$ with terms from $G$ and with length $|S| \ge \ell$ has a nontrivial zero-sum subsequence. A long-standing conjecture, first proposed by van Emde Boas and Kruyswijk in 1969, states that $D(C_n^r)=r(n-1)+1$ for all positive integers $n$ and $r$. We disprove this conjecture for every exponent $n=2k$ with $k\ge3$ odd. For each such $n$, we prove that $D(C_n^r)>r(n-1)+1$ for every $r\ge \frac{5n}{2}$. For rank $r=3$, we prove that the equality $D(C_n^3)=3n-2$ holds for all sufficiently large integers $n$.

items.title: A Barsotti-Weil isomorphism for Taelman units
items.summary: The positive-characteristic analogue of motivic cohomology with coefficients in an Anderson A-motive M over a function field of transcendence degree one was introduced in an earlier work of the author. In this paper, we prove that, when M arises as the dual of the A-motive of an Anderson module E that is abelian, uniformizable, and has everywhere good reduction, the corresponding A-motivic cohomology coincides with the module of Taelman units of E, up to a twist by the module of Kähler differentials of A. To this end, we recast the theory of Anderson generating functions in the spirit of earlier work of Maurischat and the author on special functions.

items.title: Ordering Information in Multispecies Long-Range Swap Processes
items.summary: We measure how much the left-to-right species order $W_t$ of interacting particles on the integer lattice reveals about their initial configuration. For distinct species under long-range swaps, deleting stronger particles gives coordinates with independent Poisson increments. For a finitely supported initial law, the mutual information between any function $U$ of the initial configuration and $W_t$ is $C_U/t+O(t^{-3/2})$ as $t\to\infty$, where $C_U$, which may vanish, is determined by the means of Gaussian order statistics and the conditional means of the initial compressed coordinates given $U$. On consecutive sites with a uniform initial order, we compute the coefficient of the $t\log(1/t)$ term in the short-time information loss for arbitrary species counts. For three particles in this setting, repeating the weaker rather than the stronger species triples the long-time $t^{-1}$ coefficient, although both compositions have the same composition entropy and initial-order entropy. These long-time coefficients are the same whether equal particles block or push each other, but the nonuniform limiting output law is reversed. In the ordinary multispecies totally asymmetric simple exclusion process (TASEP), two distinct particles at fixed sites with a uniform initial order instead give $t^{-1/2}$ decay.

items.title: Large deviation principle of error of Euler--Maruyama method for stochastic differential equations
items.summary: We study large deviations for the error of the Euler--Maruyama method applied to a one-dimensional stochastic differential equation with $C_b^3$ coefficients and a uniformly elliptic diffusion coefficient. We prove that the error at the terminal time, without rescaling, satisfies a large deviation principle (LDP) at speed $n$, where $n$ is the number of steps, with a good rate function that vanishes only at the origin. In particular, the probability that the error exceeds a fixed level decays exponentially in $n$. Two effects determine the rate function. A single Brownian increment of fixed nonzero size has finite cost at speed $n$, and the cumulative effect of smaller Brownian increments depends on the states at which their squares accumulate. To capture both effects, we introduce, for a cutoff $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$, an empirical enhanced control that records the state-dependent quadratic variation of the small increments together with the time, state and size of each increment exceeding $\varepsilon$. We prove an LDP for the empirical enhanced control for every fixed $\varepsilon$, and deduce the LDP for the error by the contraction principle and an exponentially good approximation as $\varepsilon\to0$.

items.title: An Asymptotically Sharp Form of the Overfull Conjecture
items.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph with maximum degree $Δ$. A subgraph $H$ of $G$ is \emph{$Δ$-overfull} if $|E(H)|>Δ\lfloor |V(H)|/2\rfloor$. The Overfull Conjecture, proposed by Chetwynd and Hilton in 1986, states that a graph $G$ with $Δ>|V(G)|/3$ is of class~2 if and only if it contains a $Δ$-overfull subgraph. This conjecture would give a polynomial-time algorithm for determining the chromatic index in this degree range and would imply several longstanding conjectures on critical graphs. In this paper, we prove that, for every $\varepsilon>0$, a sufficiently large graph $G$ with $Δ\ge(1/4+\varepsilon)|V(G)|$ is of class~2 if and only if it contains a $Δ$-overfull subgraph. Consequently, the chromatic index can be determined in polynomial time in this range. We also obtain the Just-overfull and Vertex-splitting Conjectures for large graphs, and Vizing's Independence Number, Average Degree, and $2$-Factor Conjectures in the same degree range. The coefficient $1/4$ is asymptotically best possible: for every odd integer $Δ\ge3$, we construct a connected class~2 graph on $4Δ+5$ vertices with maximum degree $Δ$ and no $Δ$-overfull subgraph.

items.title: SGD with Large Learning Rates: General Analysis & Improved Rates
items.summary: Stochastic Gradient Descent lies at the core of modern machine learning. However its classical analysis typically restricts the stepsize to be below a curvature-dependent stability threshold. Recent developments in deterministic optimization have challenged this paradigm, showing that suitably chosen large stepsizes can not only preserve convergence, but also accelerate Gradient Descent (GD). Whether this phenomenon persists in the presence of stochastic gradient noise has remained an open question (Wu et al., 2024). In this work, we answer this question affirmatively for the cross-entropy loss with linear predictors and two-layer neural networks, establishing an accelerated $\mathcal{O}(T^{-2})$ convergence rate. At the core of our analysis is a fine-grained characterization of the stochastic large-stepsize dynamics. This sharper control of the trajectory further yields tight convergence guarantees within the stable regime, improving existing bounds even in the deterministic setting. Taken together, our results show that the acceleration mechanism induced by large stepsizes survives stochasticity and extends beyond linear models. Numerical experiments demonstrate the benefits of large learning rates in practice.

items.title: Risk-Informed Path Planning: Collision and Grounding Avoidance Application for Autonomous Surface Vessels
items.summary: Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS) must demonstrate safety before and during operations, necessitating online risk assessment to guide decision-making at sea. This paper presents a risk-informed Rapidly Exploring Random Tree Star (RRT*) path planner that integrates a Bayesian Belief Network (BBN) as an online risk model. The BBN evaluates the probability and severity distribution of hazardous events, which are aggregated into a bounded scalar risk index. During the search, this risk index is evaluated at sample points along candidate edges. The planner optimizes a composite cost function comprising path distance, heading change penalties, and accumulated risk, subject to a hard constraint enforcing a risk acceptance limit. Each search tree vertex stores the BBN posterior at its state, enabling the tree to function as an explainable risk map for individual hazards. We define design requirements for the BBN to serve as the risk model in this context and introduce a runtime model that translates replanning deadlines into strict limits on single risk calculation times. The planner is demonstrated in a simulated harbor entry scenario involving collision and grounding hazards. Measured run times validate that the planner operates within the computational bounds predicted by the runtime model for a single replanning cycle.

items.title: Elliptic Monotonicity Formulas for $p$-Green Functions
items.summary: In this paper, we derive $p$-Laplace analogues of Colding's three monotonicity formulas in the original metric on complete noncompact $n$-dimensional manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature, for $n\geq3$ and $1<p<n$. We assume a normalized positive minimal $p$-Green function vanishing at infinity with Euclidean pole asymptotics. Two complementary linearizations and the $p$-Bochner formula yield exact derivative identities with a common nonnegative defect involving an anisotropic trace-free Hessian and Ricci curvature. These identities give exterior cone rigidity and integral defect estimates, and recover the sharp gradient estimate and Euclidean rigidity of Mari--Rigoli--Setti. A one-parameter extension of Colding--Minicozzi type connects the formulas with known monotonicity and convexity identities for $p$-capacitary potentials.

items.title: Cospan contexts and higher categories
items.summary: Motivated by the desire to turn the cobordism hypothesis (a statement about the universal property of some $n$-category of bordisms) into a $1$-categorical statement, we prove that all $n$-categories can be modeled by \emph{$n$-cospan contexts}: these are $1$-categories equipped with a collection of iterated cospans that satisfy a composition property in terms of pushouts. In particular, we construct an adjunction from $\mathsf{Cat}_n$ to the category of $n$-cospan contexts which simultaneously generalizes the $n$-fold span construction of Haugseng and the twisted arrow category construction (when $n = 1$).

items.title: Line bundles on regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties
items.summary: Let $G$ be a connected simply-connected simple algebraic group over $\mathbb{C}$ and $B$ be a Borel subgroup of $G$. Let $Y$ be an irreducible regular semisimple Hessenberg variety in $G/B$. In this article, we give a necessary and sufficient condition for the natural restriction map $\mathrm{res}: \mathrm{Pic}(G/B)\longrightarrow \mathrm{Pic}(Y)$ of Picard groups induced by the inclusion $Y\subseteq G/B$ to be an isomorphism.

items.title: Variance Reduction Note 5: The Convergence of Loopless SVRG
items.summary: A snapshot in loopless SVRG has no prescribed lifetime. At each step the algorithm may keep using an old full gradient or compute a new one. How does this choice enter the convergence proof, and how often is a new full gradient worth its cost? For a strongly convex finite sum we follow the age and objective gap of the snapshot. Its expected gap is a geometrically weighted average of earlier iterate gaps. This identity determines a weight for the snapshot in a one-step contraction argument and gives an objective bound for the last iterate. A two-component quadratic makes the estimator variance explicit, including on the step immediately after a refresh. We also evaluate the work bound as a function of the refresh probability and compare its minimizer with the condition-number-independent choice $p=1/n$.

items.title: An elliptic Lehmer bound of exponent one at a supersingular prime
items.summary: Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over a number field $K$ with good supersingular reduction at a prime $\p$. We prove that the Néron--Tate height of every non-torsion $P\in E(\Kbar)$ satisfies $\hh_E(P)\ge c\,D^{-1}(\log3D)^{-1}\exp(-c'\sqrt{\log3D})$, where $D=[K(x(P)):K]$ and $c,c'>0$ depend only on $E$, $K$ and $\p$; so $\hh_E(P)\ge D^{-1-o(1)}$. By a result of Elkies this applies to every elliptic curve over $\QQ$, and it improves the exponents of Masser and of Hindry and Silverman.

items.title: Convex computation of cost bounds for data-driven nonlinear optimal control
items.summary: The paper addresses the optimal control problem of an input-affine polynomial system with an unknown (state-dependent) input matrix affecting the control effectiveness. Under assumptions on the existence of a data set and the Lipschitz continuity of the unknown part {of the dynamics}, an uncertainty set is constructed and used to adapt the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation towards a data-driven formulation. We solve it for the best-case scenario, thus giving a lower bound on the best cost achievable by means of a feedback control policy. After relaxing it into a moment-SoS hierarchy of semidefinite programs, a control law is extracted from the primal on moments and compared with other benchmark methods in a numerical application.

items.title: The majority game chromatic number for dense random graphs
items.summary: We show that for every fixed $2/3<p<1$ the majority game chromatic number of the Erdős--Rényi random graph $G_{n,p}$ is $3$ with high probability.

items.title: Baker-Akhiezer functions for Koornwinder-van Diejen integrable system
items.summary: The Koornwinder-van Diejen integrable system is a counterpart of the trigonometric Ruijsenaars integrable system (associated with the root system $A_n$) for the root system $(C_n^\vee, C_n)$. It depends on the standard Macdonald parameters $q$ and $t$ as well as the Koornwinder (Askey-Wilson) parameters $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$. Different specializations of the parameters connect it to the other classical root systems from the $(C_n^\vee, C_n)$ family. The eigenfunctions of the Koornwinder-van Diejen integrable system are the symmetric Koornwinder polynomials; for certain values of the parameters $t$, $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$ they coincide with the sum over the Weyl group of the Baker-Akhiezer functions introduced by O.A.\,Chalykh for the classical root system $BC_n$. The main idea behind this paper is to elucidate Chalykh's formalism and apply it to other affine root systems. We define Baker-Akhiezer functions for all root systems in the $(C_n^\vee, C_n)$ family. We also present some explicit expressions for Baker-Akhiezer functions.

items.title: Fluctuations in the k-cut numbers of random recursive trees
items.summary: We consider the k-cut procedure introduced by Cai et al. [EJP, 2018] on random recursive trees. Our main result identifies the fluctuations in the number of cuts required to isolate the root as the tree size tends to infinity. This extends the results by Drmota et al. [RSA, 2009] and Iksanov et al. [ECP, 2007] for the classical cutting procedure.

items.title: On the generalized foliated cone theorem of rank one
items.summary: We prove the cone theorem for generalized foliated quadruples of rank one in arbitrary dimension. As an application, we prove the uniqueness of MMP outputs for log canonical generalized foliated quadruples of rank one.

items.title: Timelike conjugate points in Lorentzian length spaces
items.summary: We study notions of conjugate points along timelike geodesics in the synthetic setting of Lorentzian (pre-)length spaces, inspired by earlier work for metric spaces by Shankar--Sormani. After preliminary considerations on convergence of timelike and causal geodesics, we introduce and compare one-sided, symmetric, unreachable and ultimate conjugate points along timelike geodesics. We show that all such notions are compatible with the usual one in the smooth (strongly causal) spacetime setting. As applications, we prove a timelike Rauch comparison theorem, as well as a result closely related to the recently established Lorentzian Cartan--Hadamard theorem by Erös--Gieger. In the appendix, we give a detailed treatment of the Fréchet distance on the space of non-stopping curves up to reparametrization, a technical tool used throughout the paper.

items.title: A degree-sum condition for paths through prescribed vertices
items.summary: Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$ and let $S\subseteq V(G)$. Denote by $κ(S)$ the minimum size of a vertex set separating two vertices of $S$, and by $σ_p(S)$ the minimum degree sum over all independent sets of $p$ vertices in $S$. We prove that if $κ(S)\ge k\ge2$ and $σ_p(S)\ge n+(p-1)^2$ for every integer $p\ge k$, then any two distinct vertices of $S$ are joined by a path containing all vertices of $S$. This gives a path version of Ota's theorem on cycles containing a prescribed set of vertices. As an application, we prove a conjecture of Faudree, Faudree, Gould, Jacobson and Magnant: for $k\ge3$, every $k$-connected graph $G$ of order $n$ satisfying $δ(G)>(n+k^2-2k)/k$ and $δ(G)\geα(G)+k-2$ is hamiltonian-connected.

items.title: A sufficient criterion for ballistic behavior of forced geometric motions in random environment
items.summary: We introduce a sufficient criterion for ballistic motion of interface evolutions in random environments. More precisely, we consider interfaces moving by forced mean curvature flow in dimension $d=2$ with a spatially fluctuating (possibly negative) driving force. Such models arise e.g. from the motions of dislocation lines or magnetic domain walls in a material with impurities. We show that the evolution admits an `effective minimum speed on large scales' if for a sample of the random environment in some long and thin box there is a sufficiently large probability that an interface initialized in the bottom of the box evolves to reach its top. The concept of an `effective minimum speed on large scales' was introduced and is required for the quantitative stochastic homogenization result in the companion paper ``Quantitative homogenization of forced geometric motions through random fields of obstacles''. We show that our criterion and hence the requirements for the homogenization result in the companion paper are satisfied for compactly supported obstacle shapes distributed according to a Poisson point process with sufficiently low intensity.

items.title: Graph-Induced Rotational Twisted States in Systems of Identical Oscillators
items.summary: In this article, we study a new class of collective motion for identical coupled Stuart-Landau oscillators on graphs. This model was previously known to converge to the synchronized state for a certain class of initial data. Here, we show that when the interaction matrix is circulant, there exists another class of attractors, in which the particles are uniformly distributed on a circle, reminiscent of the \textit{twisted states} known for the Kuramoto model, but which rotate around the origin. However, contrary to the classical Kuramoto case, here the rotation is caused by the asymmetry of the graph structure, and not by the natural frequencies. We identify conditions for the existence and local stability of the \textit{rotational twisted states}, both in the Stuart-Landau model and in the Kuramoto model. We also provide sufficient conditions for the existence and stability of the synchronized state, which can co-exist with the rotational twisted state in a certain parameter region. We provide a generalization of the class of interaction matrices able to generate rotational twisted states via leader-follower interaction matrices. We show that heterogeneous rotational twisted states can also exist for a system of heterogeneous oscillators, attracted to different individual target amplitudes. This study is accompanied by numerical simulations that illustrate the possible behaviors of the system, which also include metastable dynamics and a chimera state.

items.title: Quasifibrations in étale homotopy theory
items.summary: We study quasifibrations in étale homotopy theory and prove a criterion for a morphism of schemes to be a quasifibration in terms of its (higher) direct images for sheaves of sets and (possibly non-abelian) groups. This allows to generalise Friedlander's formula for the homotopy fibre of geometric fibrations to the case of an arbitrary qcqs base scheme that is not necessarily normal. Among the applications to geometric fibrations are (1) specialisation is an equivalence on the pro-$Σ$ completed profinite étale homotopy types of geometric fibres, (2) a long exact sequence of étale homotopy groups in characteristic 0, and (3) a partially $Σ$-completed exact sequence of étale homotopy groups in low degree terms in general.

items.title: Convergence analysis of generalized modified splitting methods using multi-index series
items.summary: We consider splitting methods for partial differential equations involving unbounded operators. For non-time-reversible dynamics, such as dissipative systems, negative splitting coefficients are generally not admissible because they require stepping backward in time, leading to an order barrier when all coefficients are required to be positive. We introduce generalized modified splitting methods that overcome this algebraic order barrier while retaining nonnegative splitting coefficients. To analyze their convergence, we develop a decorated multi-index series formalism and establish a substitution law that provides a systematic framework for deriving order conditions. This law also yields an order-raising procedure based on canceling the leading error through a modification of a single stage. We also derive an explicit composition law for extended multi-index series allowing the composition of methods with independently scaled time steps common in composition and processed methods. We illustrate the construction with two sixth-order methods that use different sets of commutator corrections. Python scripts automate the computation and verification of order conditions and the construction of the methods. Finally, we discuss connections with word series, Lie-Butcher series, and multi-index Butcher series.

items.title: Minimal log discrepancies are lower semicontinuous and bounded
items.summary: We prove Ambro's conjecture stating that the minimal log discrepancies are lower semicontinuous. As a consequence, minimal log discrepancies are bounded from above by the dimension of the variety, proving a conjecture of Shokurov.

items.title: Spectral and arithmetic classifications of mixed-power difference factor absorbing ideals
items.summary: For integers $n\ge2$ and $k\ge1$, a proper ideal $I$ is $(kn,n)$-mixed-power difference factor absorbing if $a^{kn}-b^n\in I$ implies that $a^k-b$ or the complementary geometric-sum factor lies in $I$. Extending the cubic spectral criterion, we classify radical ideals for all exponents via roots of unity in the fraction fields of their minimal-prime quotients, with no finiteness or comaximality assumptions; for radical ideals the condition is independent of $k$. We extend the finite comaximal-prime criterion for quartic pair absorption to all radical ideals and identify its three-component obstruction. Requiring one factor to lie in the radical is equivalent to the radical satisfying the condition for every multiplier, yielding radical descent and extending cubic primary descent. For radical ideals, the condition is equivalent under polynomial and power series extension. Applications include pullbacks of domains and, when the characteristic does not divide $n$, a characterization of geometric integrality of geometrically reduced algebras by stability under field extension; for $n\ge3$, a square-zero extension of such an algebra is stable precisely when the quotient is geometrically integral and the kernel is torsion-free. If the characteristic $p$ divides $n$, the condition depends only on the $p$-part of $n$ and is equivalent to a power-closure condition. We classify square-zero extensions of domains, including nonsplit extensions and idealization ideals with prime projection. For homogeneous idealizations over $P$-primary bases with $2\notin P$, a related quartic criterion

items.title: Temporal Inhomogeneous Random Graphs
items.summary: Motivated by the study of time-dependent propagation processes in inhomogeneous populations, we extend Burova, Lugosi and Perarnau's results on the temporal stochastic block model to graphon-based random graphs with a continuous and strictly positive kernel. We consider such a graph in the regime where connection probabilities are of the order of $\log n/n$, and equip its edges with a uniformly random ordering, interpreted as timestamps. We study the size of reachable sets via increasing paths (that is, paths whose edge timestamps are strictly increasing). We establish tight first-order asymptotics for the size of the reachable set from a fixed vertex, and also determine the first-order asymptotics of the lengths of the longest and shortest increasing paths with one or two fixed endpoints.

items.title: Polynomial valuations on plane polygons
items.summary: Scissors congruence problems involving translations have prompted the study of translation invariant simple valuations. We review this classical theory from a naive and consistent viewpoint: starting from a description of all simple valuations on polygons, we characterize the effect of translation invariance. A description of all polynomial simple valuations is obtained as a bi-product of the adopted approach and as a direct generalization of the translation invariant theory; it appears to be new.

items.title: Dobrowolski-type lower bounds for canonical heights of polynomials of Frobenius type
items.summary: Let $K$ be a number field and let $f\in\OK[x]$ be a monic polynomial of degree $d=p^r$ with $f\equiv x^d+c\pmod p$, such as $x^2+c$. We prove that every $α\in\Kbar$ of degree $D$ over $K$ with infinite orbit under $f$ satisfies $$\hh_f(α)\ \ge\ \frac{c_1}{D\log3D}\exp\bigl(-c_2\sqrt{\log3D}\bigr),$$ where $c_1,c_2>0$ depend only on $f$ and $K$. This implies $\hh_f(α)\ge D^{-1-o(1)}$, making progress towards the dynamical Lehmer conjecture. The polynomial $f$ need not be postcritically finite. For such polynomials, for instance $x^2+1$, no lower bound of polynomial decay in $D$ was previously known. For postcritically finite polynomials such as $x^2-1$, it improves the recent quadratic bound of Habegger and Schmidt. The method is motivated by Dobrowolski's proof on Lehmer's problem.

items.title: A Classification of Trees Without Unique Subgraphs
items.summary: We study trees without unique subgraphs, in both the induced and non-induced settings. Graphs without unique induced subgraphs, called anchor-free graphs, form a natural candidate class for counterexamples to the Graph Reconstruction Conjecture, but their structure remains poorly understood. We develop a framework for studying anchor-free graphs based on a covering lemma that characterizes anchor-freeness via induced subgraph coverings of vertices. Using this framework, we prove that a tree is anchor-free if and only if it is a path with one less vertex than a prime. We also introduce the related notion of unique-subgraph-freeness, which acts as an edge-based analogue of anchor-freeness. We show that the line graph of every unique-subgraph-free graph is anchor-free and obtain a complete classification of unique-subgraph-free trees as either prime paths, stars, or extended stars. Together, these results provide a classification of trees without unique subgraphs and suggest a general approach for extending the theory beyond trees.

items.title: Transmission and Reflection coefficients for Schrödinger Operators with Truncated Periodic Potentials that support defect states
items.summary: We consider scattering waves through truncated periodic potentials with perturbations that support localized gap eigenstates. In a small complex neighborhood around an assumed positive bound state of the model operator, we prove the existence of a distinct zero reflection state, or transmission resonance. We compare its location to a previously found scattering resonance and use the properties of solutions near these interesting points to analyze the behavior of transmission and reflection coefficients of scattering solutions near the assumed bound state. By example, we also discuss the truncated simple harmonic oscillator and compare the analysis to the crystalline case.

items.title: Formality of finite abelian covers and Jordan blocks of the monodromy
items.summary: Let $X$ be a connected finite-type CW-complex with a map to the circle that is surjective on fundamental groups. If $X$ is formal, the algebraic monodromy of the associated infinite cyclic cover has no Jordan block of size greater than one at the eigenvalue 1, over the rationals; formality of the $d$-fold cyclic cover rules out such blocks at the $d$-th roots of unity. We study how formality of finite abelian covers and Jordan blocks of the monodromy constrain each other. We call $X$ Alexander formal if there are no such blocks at any root of unity, rationally, nor at the eigenvalue 1 modulo any prime; this is a formality property of cochains, as DG modules over the cohomology of the circle. The complement of a central hyperplane arrangement, with its Milnor fibration, is Alexander formal exactly when the numbers of hyperplanes in its irreducible factors have no common divisor greater than 1. We also show that a CDGA graded by an abelian group, over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, is formal if and only if it is formal as a graded CDGA. Hence the strong formality of Kohno and Pajitnov implies formality of every finite abelian cover of $X$, but not conversely. Modulo $p$, eigenvalues of $p$-power order collide with 1, producing Jordan blocks that strong formality allows; the two conditions are incomparable, and all four resulting classes contain arrangement complements.

items.title: Pyoframe: A Python Library to Easily and Efficiently Construct Large Optimization Models
items.summary: Researchers and industry practitioners are constructing increasingly large optimization models to tackle problems in fields such as manufacturing, logistics, and energy systems planning. As the performance of solvers like Gurobi keeps improving, the performance of modeling frameworks like gurobipy which let users interact with solvers is increasingly becoming a bottleneck. We present Pyoframe, an open-source Python modeling framework to construct optimization models of various types (LPs, MIPs, QPs, and QCQPs). Pyoframe adopts a novel DataFrame-based software architecture that enables parallelized computations while also offering a legible syntax and a friendly user experience. We benchmark Pyoframe against other modeling frameworks (AMPL, CVXPY, Gurobipy, JuMP, Linopy, PuLP, Pyomo, and PyOptInterface) and find that Pyoframe is faster on every large or complex benchmark, while almost always using less memory and fewer lines of code. Switching to Pyoframe reduces the total time, memory, and code needed to solve these benchmark problems by up to 83%, 68%, and 64%, respectively, demonstrating the significant impact that modeling frameworks, not only solvers, can have in applied optimization. Overall, Pyoframe makes it easier and faster to develop and run large linear or quadratic optimization models.

items.title: Dubrovin duality for open Hurwitz flat F-manifolds
items.summary: We prove that the Dubrovin dual of a Hurwitz Frobenius manifold extends naturally to an F-manifold with compatible flat connection on the universal curve, in the sense of the open WDVV equations. A similar result is proven for the Frobenius manifold itself in arXiv:2503.09258 . This equips the universal curve with two F-manifolds with compatible flat structure, and we study their duality. We show that they combine into a bi-flat F-manifold. Conditions on open WDVV solutions imposed in previous work are retrieved in this setting, thus providing them with a geometrical meaning. Finally, explicit examples are computed. For Saito Frobenius manifolds of types $A$ and $D$, the extended prepotentials coincide with open WDVV solutions computed independently, whereas even the existence of the solution in type $E$ had not been previously discussed. On the other hand, new non-homogeneous solutions are constructed by duality.

items.title: Rotational Chaos in the Driven Pendulum
items.summary: Building on recent developments in the topological theory of surface dynamics, we develop readily applicable criteria for computer-assisted proofs of the existence of rotational horseshoes and apply them to the Driven Pendulum. These tools also allow us to localize the resulting instability region, and to compute a lower bound for the length of their rotation sets. This, in turn, implies the existence of periodic points realizing a wide range of rational rotation numbers. The obtained results correspond to physically meaningful parameter values of the Driven Pendulum. The method also applies to periodically forced Hamiltonian systems whenever the stated conditions are satisfied.

items.title: Syzygies of general projections of canonical and paracanonical curves
items.summary: Let $X\subset\mathbb{P}^r$ be an integral linearly normal variety and $R=k[x_0,\cdots,x_r]$ the coordinate ring of $\mathbb{P}^r$. It is known that the syzygies of $X$ contain some geometric information. In recent years the syzygies of non-projectively normal varieties or in other words, the projection $X'$ of $X$ away from a linear subspace $W\subset\mathbb{P}^r$, were taken into considerations. Assuming that the coordinate ring of the ambient space that $X'$ lives in is $S$, there are two types of vanishing properties of the Betti diagrams of the projected varieties, the so-called $N_{d,p}^S$ and $\widetilde{N}_{d,p}$. The former one have been widely discussed for general varieties, for example by S. Kwak, Y. Choi and E. Park, while the latter one was discussed by W. Lee and E. Park for curves of very large degree. In this paper I will discuss about the $\widetilde{N}_{d,p}$ properties of the projection of a generic canonical and paracanonical curve away from a generic point and in particular whether they are cut out by quadrics. Some conjectures will be claimed based on the tests on Macaulay2.

items.title: Two-Scale Diffusion Approximations for Many-Server Queues with Overdispersed Arrivals
items.summary: We study steady-state diffusion approximations for a many-server queue driven by overdispersed arrivals from a doubly stochastic Poisson process. Its arrival intensity follows a generalized Cox--Ingersoll--Ross (CIR) process, where $α\in [0, 1)$ governs how the arrival-count variance scales as $λ^{1+α}$ with the baseline arrival rate $λ$ under Taylor's law. For $α> 0$, arrival-intensity fluctuations grow faster with $λ$ than counting fluctuations from arrivals and departures, so normalizing by $λ^{(1+α)/2}$ pairs a nonvanishing intensity volatility with a vanishing queue-length volatility. This two-scale formulation differs critically from conventional diffusion approximations, which either apply a single $λ^{1/2}$ scaling with nonvanishing volatilities or drop the vanishing queue-length noise in the heavy-traffic limit. Retaining both scales, we compare two diffusions: one replaces the scaled intensity with its limiting Ornstein--Uhlenbeck (OU) process, and the other preserves the exact CIR intensity. Using Stein's method, we establish steady-state error bounds for smooth test functions of arbitrary polynomial growth that depend on $α$ in opposite directions. Both diffusions achieve the classical $O(λ^{-1/2})$ rate at $α= 0$. For $α\in (0, 1)$, however, the OU rate degrades to the sharp order $O(λ^{-(1-α)/2})$, whereas preserving the CIR intensity improves the rate to $O(λ^{-(2+α)/4})$. Our proofs establish new derivative bounds for the associated Poisson equations that remain valid when the diffusion has vanishing volatility and nonsmooth drift.

items.title: Schnyder Woods and the Chromatic Polynomial
items.summary: Let $χ_G(q)$ be the chromatic polynomial of a graph $G$. Analogous to the classical results of Greene and Zaslavsky interpreting $(-1)^{n-1}χ_G'(0)$ and $(-1)^nχ_G'(1)$ as counting certain orientations of $G$, we show that if $G$ is a triangulation, $\frac{1}{2}(-1)^{n-1}χ_G'(2)$ counts the number of Schnyder woods on a plane embedding of $G$. We also generalise this result to graphs obtained by removing certain edges of $G$.

items.title: Bicriteria Traffic Assignment
items.summary: The classical traffic assignment problem determines the equilibrium flows on a congested network with many infinitesimal users who choose paths to minimize their own travel times. Travelers care about cost (including tolls) as well as time, and different travelers put different weights on these two criteria. We study a bicriteria traffic assignment problem in which travelers differ in their tradeoff between a flow-independent cost, such as tolls, and a flow-dependent cost, such as travel time. Existing formulations require either finitely many user classes or positive preference densities, including formulations for positive preference densities that are either infinite-dimensional or nonconvex. We formulate a finite-dimensional convex optimization problem for arbitrary preference distributions with bounded support, including distributions with a mixture of atoms, densities, and gaps in their support, and we show how to convert an optimal solution to an equilibrium of the bicriteria traffic assignment problem. We propose an algorithm that alternates between solving a convex problem for a (typically small) number of paths, and solving a parametric shortest-path problem. Computational experiments on benchmark networks illustrate the performance of the algorithm relative to existing methods.

items.title: A Learning-Based Numerical Method for Biharmonic boundary value problems via the Almansi Decomposition
items.summary: We extend the learning-based numerical method (LbNM) to two-dimensional biharmonic boundary value problems, combining high accuracy with efficient repeated solves for different boundary data on a fixed domain. The method reconstructs a discrete boundary-to-solution operator from explicit biharmonic samples generated by the Almansi decomposition, using their boundary values and normal derivatives through Tikhonov regularization. Once constructed at prescribed evaluation points, the operator provides solutions for new boundary inputs by a single matrix-vector multiplication. Moreover, additional sample solutions can be incorporated through rank-one updates without rebuilding the operator. We establish a quantitative convergence estimate under a biharmonic continuation assumption. Numerical experiments on nonconvex domains demonstrate accuracy close to the double-precision limit for a smooth benchmark and high accuracy for solutions induced by nearby exterior singularities.

items.title: Free abelian group actions on projective fibered varieties
items.summary: Let $X$ be an $n$-dimensional normal projective variety of Kodaira dimension $κ$ and $G$ an abelian subgroup of automorphisms such that all elements of $G\backslash \{\mathrm{id}\}$ are of positive entropy. Dinh and Sibony showed that $G$ is actually free abelian of rank $\le n-κ-1$. In this paper, we show that after replacing $G$ by a finite-index subgroup, there exists a G-Equivariant Minimal Model Program for the pair $(X, G)$ when $\mathrm{rank}(G)=n-κ-1$ and $κ>0$, and the very general fiber of the final model is a klt Calabi-Yau surface or a $Q$-abelian variety provided that the termination of flips holds in this setting.

items.title: Unbounded GHZ dimension from fixed-order multiphoton sources
items.summary: We study the local dimension of Greenberger--Horne--Zeilinger (GHZ) states obtained by selecting events with one photon per output path. Each coherent source emits photons with a fixed internal label into a distinct set of paths, and the sets for each label partition the outputs. For two-photon sources, the maximum local dimension is 2 for every even number of paths greater than 4. However, we show that three-photon sources can produce GHZ states of arbitrarily large local dimension. To prove this, we view the three paths fed by each source as an edge of a $3$-uniform hypergraph, so that accepted emission patterns correspond exactly to perfect matchings. We construct such hypergraphs with arbitrarily many edge-disjoint perfect matchings, one per label, and no others. The construction extends to $r$-uniform hypergraphs for every fixed $r\ge3$, yielding a GHZ dimension that grows at least polynomially as the number of paths ranges over the positive multiples of $r$.

items.title: Erdős Distance Results for $k$-Degenerate Graphs with $m$ Edges
items.summary: The Erdős distinct distances problem asks how many distinct distances $N$ points must determine. In the plane, Guth and Katz determined the optimal power of $N$. A natural generalization fixes a finite graph $G$ with $m$ edges and records, over all injective embeddings of $G$ into a finite point set $P \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, the vectors of edge-lengths realized; we write $Δ_G^\circ(P)$ for this set of edge-distance vectors. Taking $G$ to be a single edge recovers the classical problem. In the plane, the exponent $|V(G)|-1$ is known up to an arbitrarily small loss for every connected graph. A graph is $k$-degenerate if its vertices can be ordered so that each has at most $k$ neighbors among those preceding it. We show that if $G$ is $k$-degenerate, then for every $d \ge \max(2k,3)$ and every $\varepsilon > 0$, $|Δ_G^\circ(P)| \gtrsim_{G,d,\varepsilon} N^{m/(d-1)-\varepsilon}$ for $|P|=N\ge |V(G)|$. For a connected graph with $m/(|V(G)|-1)>2(d-1)/d$, the exponent $m/(d-1)$ exceeds the spanning-tree exponent predicted by the pinned-distance conjecture. Our result is motivated by the threshold $\frac{d+k}{2}$ obtained by Borges, Foster, Ou, Palsson, and Romero Acosta for edge lengths of $k$-degenerate graphs in fractal sets. The proof combines a bisector-energy estimate for pinned $k$-stars with an entropy argument of Katz--Tardos type, applied along a construction order of $G$ and combined with an induction on the dimension.

items.title: A Systematic Construction of High-Corank Kac--Moody Algebras
items.summary: We form a hexagonal prism from two six-cycles and iterate a doubling construction with a fixed positive integer edge multiplicity, producing a family of indefinite Kac--Moody algebras. The prism's spectrum determines the exact corank of every algebra in the family. Along each nonvanishing parity class, the corank grows exponentially, while its ratio to the matrix size tends to zero. For the twelve-node algebra we identify the two central directions, describe the first two graded levels, and characterize the integral central charges of its unitary highest-weight modules.

items.title: One monoid to realize them all: a master monoid for homotopy types
items.summary: Homotopy theory has traditionally been approached either through topological spaces or through categories of presheaves on suitable combinatorial categories, a perspective subsumed by Grothendieck's theory of test categories. In this paper, we develop a more algebraic viewpoint: homotopy types can be represented by actions of a single monoid on sets. This monoid is obtained by identifying all the objects of the semisimplicial category while retaining its face operators. Every CW homotopy type is the classifying space of the translation category of one of its actions, and its truncation at dimension n is finitely presented and realizes exactly the homotopy types of dimension at most n. The construction rests on a general result: every set-valued functor on a small category freely generates an action of its universal monoid, and its category of elements is a full coreflective subcategory of the resulting translation category. Hence every weak test category gives rise to a monoid whose actions realize all homotopy types; when the category has more than one object, however, this monoid is not itself a weak test category, so that a single monoid may realize all homotopy types without modelling homotopy theory as a localization. The obstruction lies in identifying objects, not in having a single one: there are strict test categories with a single object, such as the monoid of all self-maps of an infinite set and a countable monoid of primitive recursive functions.

items.title: Uniformly bounded representations of discrete measured groupoids into finite Von Neumann algebras
items.summary: Let $(\mathcal{G},ν)$ be a $t$-discrete ergodic groupoid. Consider a finite Von Neumann algebra $\mathcal{M}$ with separable predual. We prove that every uniformly bounded measurable representation $ρ:\mathcal{G} \rightarrow \mathrm{GL}(\mathcal{M})$ into the invertible elements of $\mathcal{M}$ is similar to a unitary representation.

items.title: Unlikely intersections with CM abelian varieties in a family and explicit bounds for canonical heights under endomorphisms
items.summary: Let $\mathcal{A} \rightarrow S$ be a non-isotrivial abelian scheme over a smooth irreducible curve and let $\mathcal{C} \subseteq \mathcal{A}$ be an irreducible curve, all defined over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$. In 2020, Barroero and Capuano proved that, if $\mathcal{C}$ is not contained in a proper subgroup scheme, then its intersection with the union of the flat subgroup schemes of $\mathcal{A}$ of codimension at least $2$ is finite. We complement this result by proving that, if $\mathcal{C}$ is contained neither in a fixed fiber nor in a proper flat subgroup scheme, even after a finite base change, then only finitely many points of $\mathcal{C}$ lie in a proper algebraic subgroup of a CM fiber of $\mathcal{A}$. This generalizes a previous result of Barroero for fibered powers of elliptic schemes. A key ingredient of the proof is an explicit control of canonical heights under endomorphisms: for an abelian variety $A/\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, an ample symmetric divisor $D$ and $f \in \mathrm{End}(A)$, we bound $\widehat{h}_{A,D}(f(P))$ from above and from below in terms of $\widehat{h}_{A,D}(P)$, with optimal constants given by the largest and the smallest eigenvalue of $f^{\dagger}f$, where $^{\dagger}$ is the Rosati involution associated with $D$.

items.title: Twisted Poincaré series at zero on surfaces
items.summary: Let $(Σ,g)$ be a closed, connected, oriented, Riemannian Anosov surface. We show that there exists an open subset $\mathcal V_g$ of the space of finite-dimensional irreducible representations of the fundamental group of $Σ$, whose complement has complex codimension at least one, such that the following holds: for all $x,y\in Σ$, $ρ\in \mathcal{V}_g$, the meromorphic extension of the twisted Poincaré series $s \mapsto η_{g,ρ,x,y}(s)$ vanishes at $s=0$. We also give examples of non-trivial representations whose Poincaré series does not vanish at zero. In addition, we describe the structure of twisted resonant states at zero for these examples and show that they admit non-trivial Jordan blocks.

items.title: Burn and density control in uncertain tokamak models with prescribed error bounds
items.summary: The stored energy and the electron density of a burning tokamak plasma must be kept inside prescribed bands, with the auxiliary heating power and the fuelling rate as actuators. For the standard zero-dimensional burn model with a dynamic confinement closure we show that this two-actuator configuration has vector relative degree $(2,1)$, independently of the confinement parameters. We design a model-free funnel controller which uses an input filter instead of output derivatives and meets all actuator constraints - sign, amplitude and rate - by construction, the input deficit being returned to the loop as a correction of the reference.
