For a system class containing the model we prove, under the compatibility assumption that the corrections stay bounded by constants fixed in advance, that the tracking errors evolve in prescribed funnels about the corrected references. Sufficient conditions for the assumption are given, and the design is illustrated on an ITER benchmark.

items.title: Teichmüller spaces with conical singularities and Virasoro coadjoint orbits
items.summary: We study Teichmüller spaces of hyperbolic \(0\)-metrics on a disk with ideal boundary and a marked point carrying a conical singularity with angle $θ= 2πβ$. For all $β>0$, we show that $\rm{Teich}^β(\overline{\mathbb D})\cong S^1\backslash \rm{Diff}(S^1)$, and we construct natural closed 2-forms $ω_β$ induced by the Atiyah-Bott construction. For non-integer $β$, the form $ω_β$ is symplectic, and one can identify $\rm{Teich}^β(\overline{\mathbb D})$ with the corresponding elliptic Virasoro coadjoint orbit. For positive integers $β=n$, $ω_β$ is presymplectic, and it descends to the Kirillov-Kostant-Souriau symplectic form on the exceptional Virasoro orbit $\mathrm{PSU}^{(n)}(1,1)\backslash\rm{Diff}(S^1)$. Infinitesimal isometries of a hyperbolic \(0\)-metric on a disk with a conical singularity with angle $θ=2πn$ are given by the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb R)$ which integrates to the group $\mathrm{PSU}^{(n)}(1,1)$ on the boundary of the disk but not in the interior for $n>1$. It is remarkable that the presymplectic structure of the corresponding Teichmüller spaces recovers this group and descends to the corresponding Virasoro coadjoint orbit.

items.title: Average density of rational points on quartic surfaces
items.summary: We establish an average asymptotic for the number of rational points of bounded height $B$ on quartic surfaces in $\mathbb{P}^3$ of height bounded by $A$, refining an argument of Le Boudec and using techniques of Browning-Le Boudec-Sawin. We extend the range of the asymptotic from $B=o(A)$ to $B=O(A^2)$. As an application, we show that almost all quartic surfaces of height $H$ have no rational point of height $o(H^{5/2})$.

items.title: Streamfunction-vorticity formulation for incompressible viscid and inviscid flows on general surfaces
items.summary: This paper presents a streamfunction-vorticity formulation for the Navier--Stokes and Euler equations on general surfaces. Notably, this includes non-simply connected surfaces, on which the harmonic components of the velocity field play a fundamental role in the dynamics. By relying only on scalar and finite-dimensional quantities, our formulation ensures that the resulting methods give exactly tangential and incompressible velocity fields, while also being pressure robust. Compared to traditional methods based on velocity-pressure formulations, where one can only guarantee these structural properties by increasing the computational costs, this is a key advantage. We rigorously validate our formulation by proving its equivalence to the well understood velocity-pressure formulation under additional regularity assumptions. Furthermore, we demonstrate the applicability of the approach with numerical examples.

items.title: On the action of the mapping class group on the fundamental group of a surface
items.summary: We describe the action of the mapping class group $M(g,n)$ on the fundamental group of $S_{g,n}$, the complement of $n$ distinct points in a compact orientable surface of positive genus $g$. This is achieved by computing the image of the generators of $M(g,n)$ as outer automorphisms of the fundamental group.

items.title: The sharp uniqueness threshold for the antiferromagnetic Potts model on regular trees
items.summary: We study Gibbs uniqueness for the $q$-state antiferromagnetic Potts model on the infinite rooted $d$-ary tree and the infinite $(d+1)$-regular tree, where $d\geqslant1$ and $q\geqslant2$. An edge has weight $p\in[0,1]$ if its endpoints have the same color and weight $1$ otherwise. We prove that there is a unique Gibbs state if and only if $p\geqslant p_c:=\max\{0,1-q/(d+1)\}$, except when $(q,p)=(d+1,0)$, thus completes the uniqueness thresholds for all $d\geqslant1$ and $q\geqslant2$. Our proof use a convex potential for the tree recursion and show that it strictly decreases away from the uniform distribution. Together with the result of Gu, Wu and Yang, our theorem gives the exact critical power law whenever $p_c>0$.

items.title: Numerical approximation of Markovian BSDEs in infinite horizon and elliptic PDEs
items.summary: We study backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs) in infinite horizon and {design} efficient numerical schemes for solving them. We establish a probabilistic representation of the solution of the BSDE using Malliavin derivative and prove results for contraction of a Picard scheme. We develop three numerical schemes, of which the first two are based on a fixed point argument using contraction, imposing additional assumptions compared to what is needed for existence and uniqueness of the solution. The first scheme is a space grid based approximation where we establish tight numerical error bounds using a growth truncation argument; it performs well in low dimensions but computational times increase exponentially with dimension. The second scheme uses neural network approximations for which we have proved a convergence result. Using neural networks alleviates the curse of dimensionality, giving good accuracy in very high dimensions. The third scheme also uses neural networks but does not directly rely on a contraction scheme, showcasing good performance even for larger z-Lipschitz dependence outside the empirical domain of contraction.

items.title: The Lafforgue Transform
items.summary: In this report, we survey the \emph{Lafforgue transform}, a natural representation-theoretic map from the Kazhdan cocenter to the Bernstein center of a reductive group over a local field. Its motivation comes from our study of the Braverman-Kazhdan proposal, a conjectural framework for establishing the meromorphic continuation and functional equations of general automorphic $L$-functions through harmonic analysis on possibly singular varieties. For $G=\SL_2$ and $\GL_2$, we explain how the stable part of the Lafforgue transform and its distinguished section are realized as integral transforms on the Steinberg-Hitchin base, with formulas of motivic nature that are valid over every local field.

items.title: On optimal packing of Minkowski spheres
items.summary: A method has been developed for the optimal packing of a continuum family of one-dimensional Minkowski spheres in the real plane. By applying this method to the problem of packing one-dimensional Minkowski spheres in the plane, an optimal lattice packing for a continuum family of such spheres has been obtained for the first time. Expressions for these optimal packing lattices have been derived, and their validity has been proven. Formulas for the packing density corresponding to these lattices have also been obtained.

items.title: Multiword matrix multiplication over large finite fields in floating-point arithmetic
items.summary: This article is concerned with the efficient computation of modular matrix multiplication C=AB mod p, a key kernel in computer algebra. We focus on floating-point arithmetic, which allows for using efficient matrix multiplication libraries. However, the existing approach is limited to primes p with bitsize at most half the mantissa size (e.g., 26 bits with double precision arithmetic), and becomes quite inefficient when p approaches this limit. We present a new approach that overcomes this limitation and can efficiently handle primes with larger bitsizes. The key idea is to use multiword decompositions, which represent A and B as scaled sums of u and v matrices (words) with smaller coefficients. We provide a rigorous analysis that proves the correctness of this approach for suitably chosen scaling parameters. Our analysis determines the maximum bitsize of p that can be handled for a given number of words; in particular, we show that decomposing in two words each input suffices to handle bitsizes almost equal to the full mantissa size (e.g., the 26 bits limit is raised to 52 bits in double precision arithmetic). Moreover, we show that (1,v) decompositions with v>1 are also of interest to handle intermediate bitsizes. We perform an extensive experimental analysis for various matrix shapes and prime bitsizes. Our performance benchmarks on both CPU and GPU architectures confirm the efficiency of the proposed approach, which can outperform the existing single word approach for bitsizes as low as 23, and can handle bitsizes as high as 52 while retaining high performance.

items.title: Isolated yet highly unstable 2D Euler equilibria
items.summary: We construct steady solutions of the two-dimensional Euler equations on smooth annular domains that are isolated, modulo scaling, in the $L^\infty$ vorticity topology. They are highly unstable: any Yudovich trajectory remaining sufficiently close to such an equilibrium on an open time interval is a stationary multiple of it, they admit wandering neighborhoods of initial data for all non-zero time and, moreover, at fixed energy, enstrophy and circulations, distinct nearby trajectories cannot return even weakly to the equilibrium. Further, on any non-circular annular domain, we show that this kind of isolated, highly unstable equilibria occurs arbitrarily close in the Yudovich norm to smooth equilibria which are themselves non-isolated.

items.title: Hopf sets and the Universal Chord Theorem
items.summary: We are interested in the set of horizontal chords of a real-valued continuous function on [0,1] with f(0)=f(1)=0. The equivalent set of non-chords, is defined in general as a Hopf set. First, we study some topological properties of such sets. Maximal and minimal Hopf sets are introduced, studied and constructed. Some problems are formulated and we answer a recent question posed in the American Mathematical Monthly (2024) related to these objects.

items.title: Fractional domatic number and minimum degree
items.summary: The domatic number of a graph $G$ is the maximum number of pairwise disjoint dominating sets of $G$. We are interested in the LP-relaxation of this parameter, which is called the fractional domatic number of $G$. We study its extremal value in the class of graphs of minimum degree $d$. The fractional domatic number of a graph of minimum degree $d$ is always at most $d+1$, and at least $(1-o(1))\, d/\ln d$ as $d\to \infty$. This is asymptotically tight even within the class of split graphs. Our main result concerns the case $d=2$; we show that, excluding $8$ exceptional graphs, the fractional domatic number of every connected graph of minimum degree (at least) $2$ is at least $5/2$. We also show that this bound cannot be improved if only finitely many graphs are excluded, even for bipartite graphs of arbitrarily large girth. This proves in a stronger sense a conjecture by Gadouleau, Harms, Mertzios, and Zamaraev (2024). This also extends and generalises results from McCuaig and Shepherd (1989), from Fujita, Kameda, and Yamashita (2000), and from Abbas, Egerstedt, Liu, Thomas, and Whalen (2016). Finally, we show that graphs of sub-exponential expansion and sufficiently large girth $g$ have fractional domatic number $3 - o_g(1)$.

items.title: Accuracy and Efficiency of Lowest-order and Higher-Order Single-Source Integral Equations
items.summary: The single-source integral equation allows the modeling of the electromagnetic field by only tracking a single surface-supported current density. It features products of integral operators, which pose unique challenges for the modeler in both the discretization and solution of the equation. Due to the unique structure of the single-source equation, its conforming and stable discretization requires expanding one of the two physical traces in primal basis functions and the other in dual basis functions. Primal functions are expected to have better approximation properties than dual ones. In this work, we study the impact of this asymmetric representation on the accuracy of the solution and propose an approach from which both traces can be recovered using only primal functions with modest additional computational cost. Moreover, we propose an alternative discretization scheme based on approximating the inverse of the duality mapping induced by the surface normal cross-product operator through the quasi-Helmholtz decomposition. This discretization provides greater flexibility in the choice of function spaces, enabling both a higher-order extension of the single-source equation and a more efficient lowest-order discretization using only Rao-Wilton-Glisson basis functions. Numerical results show the impact of the representation in terms of primal and dual functions in both lowest- and higher-order discretization.

items.title: Fairness-optimized interlacing knots for even-degree periodic B-spline interpolation
items.summary: Interpolating an ordered set of points by a B-spline curve is a fundamental operation in computer-aided geometric design. Most of the literature addresses open curves, where the Schoenberg--Whitney condition characterizes a nonsingular collocation matrix and averaging is the standard way to choose the knot vector. Periodic B-spline interpolation has received much less attention, and the open-curve algorithms cannot be transferred directly. No theoretical criterion is available for choosing the knots, and the few existing constructions, such as the shifting and energy methods, remain empirical, with neither a theoretical guarantee nor a supporting analysis. This paper addresses this gap for even degrees. We prove that for every even degree $p\ge2$ the periodic collocation matrix is nonsingular whenever the domain knots and the interpolation parameters interlace, in either of two admissible orderings, for arbitrarily nonuniform parameters. Rather than singling out one knot vector, this sufficient condition delimits an $n$-parameter family of admissible knot vectors and provides the theoretical foundation for knot selection that periodic interpolation has lacked. It also explains why the empirical shifting method is solvable, previously justified only by an incorrect diagonal-dominance argument. We then exploit the remaining freedom to place the knots by fairness optimization, which preserves admissibility at every iterate and leads to the methods Opt-R and Opt-L. On four closed shapes with irregularly distributed points these methods achieve a fairness comparable to the shifting and energy methods, improve on them in several cases, and offer guarantees that no empirical construction provides.

items.title: Sparse Additive Spanners and the Cost Spectra of Group Actions
items.summary: How sparse can a Cayley graph become if we retain all its vertices and allow distances to increase by at most a fixed additive constant? We study invariant random spanning subgraphs, measuring sparsity by the expected degree at a vertex. On the square grid, a random translate of a sparse mesh brings the mean degree arbitrarily close to two. If the choice must be made equivariantly from independent vertex labels, every edge is forced. In this expository note we follow these two answers through other groups. Geometry alone forces a positive gap on each non-elementary hyperbolic Cayley graph, while on one four-regular nilpotent Cayley graph the choice of action realizes every additive cost in $[1,2]$. The minimum of the action spectrum recovers the geometric cost. Open problems are presented in the end.

items.title: Seed thresholds and degree variance in heterogeneous bootstrap percolation with growing degrees
items.summary: We study bootstrap percolation with independent vertex thresholds taking values one and two, with threshold-one probability $(1-c/d)/d$ for fixed $c>0$. The seed set is chosen uniformly among sets of a prescribed deterministic size, independently of the graph and thresholds. We prove threshold statements at fixed relative margins. For uniform simple graphs with prescribed nonnegative integer degrees of even sum and exact mean $d$, assume $\max_i|d_i-d|\le C\sqrt d$ and $c+1-v_n\geκ>0$, where $v_n=\operatorname{Var}(D)/d$ and $C,κ$ are fixed. When $d\to\infty$ and $d=o(n^{1/7})$, the leading seed scale is $n(c+1-v_n)^2/(2d^4)$, without requiring a limit of $v_n$. At fixed relative margins below and above this scale, the final active set has size $O(n/d^3)$ and $n-o(n)$, respectively, with high probability. For regular graphs, the supercritical conclusion strengthens to full activation. For $G(n,d/n)$, the same $O(n/d^3)$ and $n-o(n)$ conclusions hold when $d\to\infty$ and $d^5/n\to0$, with seed scale $nc^2/(2d^4)$. Thus regular and independent-edge graphs have different coefficients at the same asymptotic mean degree. Local exploration estimates yield explicit inactive remainders and survive conditioning on simplicity in the prescribed model. We also quantify the precision obstruction to static inclusion transfer and compute deterministic response-barrier corrections, without identifying a shrinking random critical window. A separate appendix gives the corresponding fixed-margin terminal bounds for iid thresholds of fixed bounded support, with unchanged threshold-one probability and threshold-two mass bounded away from zero.

items.title: Recursive estimation of the Oja median and related simplex medians
items.summary: We study the recursive estimation of multivariate location functionals defined by minimizing the expected volume of a random simplex. This framework encompasses both the spatial median and the affine-equivariant Oja median. We introduce a sliding-window stochastic gradient algorithm and its averaged version, and establish their strong consistency and asymptotic normality. We further show that the sliding-window approach offers a favorable trade-off between statistical accuracy and computational cost compared with a naive disjoint-block stochastic gradient algorithm and offline methods, with the statistical comparison based on asymptotic covariances. Numerical experiments illustrate the computational advantages of the proposed procedures and their finite-sample accuracy.

items.title: Equivariant harmonic maps from $\mathbb{S}^3$ to $\mathbb{S}^2$: on a counterexample to a conjecture of J. Eells
items.summary: The present paper builds on a remarkable AI-generated counterexample to a long-standing conjecture of James Eells. We present the rigorous construction of a smooth harmonic map $f:\mathbb{S}^3\to \mathbb{S}^2$ between the round spheres which does not factor through a Hopf fibration, and improve some arguments to get that the Hopf invariant of $f$ is either $0$ or $\pm 6$. The construction is based on a min-max scheme in a $5$-equivariant class of maps $f$ with an additional dihedral symmetry. By passing to a suitable associated sphere bundle over $\mathbb{S}^2$, the problem is reduced to a variational problem for sections, where the imposed symmetries guarantee the mountain pass structure and the non-constancy of the desired limit harmonic map.

items.title: The one-velocity Baer--Nunziato system as a weak limit of solutions to a compressible two-fluid system
items.summary: We study how a macroscopic mixture arises from two compressible fluids that share a velocity but occupy disjoint regions. We fix the initial density profiles and the common initial velocity, and let the partition between the fluids oscillate on increasingly fine scales. The fluids remain segregated as they evolve, but in the weak limit the phase indicator becomes a volume fraction that may lie strictly between zero and one. For independent adiabatic exponents $γ^\pm\geq9/5$, we prove that the sequence of segregated solutions converges to a global weak solution of the viscous one-velocity Baer--Nunziato system in three space dimensions. The mixture pressure is the volume-weighted average of the two phase pressures, while their difference drives the evolution of the volume fraction along the flow and contributes to dissipation in the macroscopic energy inequality.

items.title: Uniform Algebraic Degeneracy of Entire Curves into Complex Projective Varieties
items.summary: This paper is devoted to the algebraic degeneracy of entire curves intersecting a simple-normal-crossing divisor on smooth projective varieties over C, within the logarithmic Green-Griffiths-Lang program. For negativelytwisted global logarithmic jet differentials, we introduce an intrinsic weighted conormal filtration along each positive-dimensional closed boundary stratum, with weights prescribed by the contact orders along boundary components. Applying the maximal Harder-Narasimhan slopes of logarithmic cotangent bundles and the normal degrees of the strata, we define an integer vanishing threshold which can improve the pole bound obtained from the slope-based ceiling. Under the stable-base-locus hypothesis for the logarithmic Semple tower, we then establish an improved second main theorem whose counting coefficients depend on the boundary stratum, actual contact orders and the ratio of source weight to twisting exponent. These coefficients are independent of the powers used to realize the stable base locus. We further derive a uniform algebraicdegeneracy criterion allowing positive corrected pole coefficients, formulated via a finite system of stratumwise inequalities together with the ampleness of a residual divisor class. This yields conditional orbifold Green-Griffiths-Lang type statements. Refinements arising from conormalbundle decompositions and sharp local pole estimates at surface boundary crossings are established. Our examples exhibit strict improvement over naive slope-based bounds and illustrate that full-weight poles can persist at boundary crossings, and furnish concrete instances satisfying the stablebaselocus hypothesis.

items.title: Diagonal and fine tower dimensions for minimal circle homeomorphisms and product actions
items.summary: We study minimal circle homeomorphisms and their products with Cantor systems, and show that these actions have diagonal dimension at most two and fine tower dimension at least two. Consequently, diagonal dimension, fine tower dimension, and tower dimension are all equal to two for minimal circle homeomorphisms. We also obtain a strict separation between tower dimension and fine tower dimension on a one-dimensional space.

items.title: Failure of bounded $\bar\partial$-solvability on pseudoconvex domains of finite type
items.summary: We show that for every integer $n\ge3$ there is a bounded pseudoconvex domain $Ω\subset\mathbb{C}^n$ with smooth real-analytic boundary whose D'Angelo $1$-type has maximum $16$ and a $\bar\partial$-closed $(0,1)$-form $f$, continuous on $\overlineΩ$ and smooth in $Ω$, such that $\bar\partial g=f$ has no solution in $L^\infty(Ω)$. On each of these domains, we also construct a uniformly bounded sequence of smooth $\bar\partial$-closed $(0,1)$-forms for which the infimum of the $L^\infty$ norms of bounded solutions tends to infinity. Each form in this sequence, together with one of its solutions, extends smoothly to a neighborhood of the closure. The construction uses a singular curve both to constrain holomorphic corrections and to separate the scales of the cutoff error and the resulting lower bound.

items.title: Edge State Propagation Near Multiple and Singular Interfaces
items.summary: We study the semiclassical propagation of edge-states for a two-dimensional Dirac operator with a spatially varying mass. The zero set of the mass models the interface between topological phases and is allowed either to consist of two disjoint smooth curves or to possess an isolated singular point. For disjoint interfaces, we prove that a wave packet initially localized on one component remains confined near this interface over long semiclassical time scales and we quantify the influence of the distance between the two components on the accuracy of the approximation. For singular interfaces, we determine the regime in which the wave-packet approximation remains valid as the packet approaches the singularity and identify the scaling at which our estimates lose their uniformity.

items.title: On some off-diagonal hypergraph Ramsey problems
items.summary: We give a new short proof of a theorem of Fox and He that the $3$-uniform Ramsey number $r_3(K_4^-, K_n)$ is at least $2^{Ω(n \log n)}$. The construction exploits a new connection with a directed graph recently introduced by Bradač in his work on off-diagonal graph Ramsey numbers. Moreover, it generalizes naturally to give sharp bounds for several extensions of this problem in higher uniformity, answering questions raised by Mubayi and Suk.

items.title: New families of vertex-transitive quaternionic lattices in products of trees
items.summary: We describe infinite families of quaternionic arithmetic lattices in $\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal{T}_1)\times \cdots \times \operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal{T}_n)$ acting transitively on the vertices of the Cartesian product $\mathcal{T}_1\times \cdots \times \mathcal{T}_n$, where $\mathcal{T}_1,\dots, \mathcal{T}_n$ are regular trees. We present an algorithm to determine a presentation for each of these lattices. We also introduce a method for constructing such lattices that act regularly on the set of vertices. We illustrate our results with numerous explicit examples, including several families of known cases, as well as many new instances in arbitrary characteristic.

items.title: Parke-Taylor Varieties
items.summary: Parke--Taylor functions are certain rational functions on the Grassmannian of lines encoding MHV amplitudes in particle physics. For $n$ particles there are $n!$ Parke--Taylor functions, corresponding to all orderings of the particles. Linear relations between these functions have been extensively studied in the last years. We here describe all non-linear polynomial relations between these functions in a simple combinatorial way and study the variety parametrized by them, called the Parke--Taylor variety. We show that the Parke--Taylor variety is equal to the log canonical embedding of the moduli space $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}$ into $\mathbb{P}^{(n-2)!-1}$ due to Keel and Tevelev by exhibiting a concrete linear isomorphism with the realization in coordinates based on Kapranov's map. We also show that the intersection with the algebraic torus recovers the open part, $\mathcal{M}_{0,n}$. We give an explicit description of this isomorphism. Unlike the realization of the log canonical embedding by using the iterated Kapranov's map, this Parke--Taylor embedding very explicitly respects the symmetry of the $n$ marked points and is constructed in a single-step procedure, avoiding the intermediate embedding into a product of projective spaces.

items.title: A convective $1$-homogeneous $p$-Laplacian problem
items.summary:
Let $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^{N}$ be a bounded, smooth domain, and let $a:\overlineΩightarrow\mathbb{R}$ be a continuous function that may change sign. We study the $1$-homogeneous problem \[ \left\{  egin{array} [c]{lll} -\operatorname{div}\left( \left\vert 
abla uight\vert ^{p-2}
abla uight) =λ\left\vert uight\vert ^{p-2}u+a(x)\left\vert 
abla uight\vert ^{p-1} & \mathrm{in} & Ω\ u=0 & \mathrm{on} & \partialΩ, \end{array} ight. \] where $1<p<\infty.$ We prove the existence of $λ_{a}>0$ for which this problem, with $λ= λ_a$, has a positive weak solution $u_{a}\in W_{0}^{1,p}(Ω)\cap C^{1}(\overlineΩ).$ The significance of this result lies in the fact that no restriction is imposed on the size of $\left\Vert aight\Vert _{\infty}.$ We also obtain lower and upper bounds for $λ_{a}$ in terms of the positive and negative parts of $a$ as well as the circumradius and inradius of $Ω.$

items.title: Identifying the critical mass in a quasilinear chemotaxis model with indirect signal production
items.summary: The mass threshold separating boundedness and unboundedness of global solutions to a critical quasilinear parabolic-elliptic chemotaxis model with indirect signal production is identified in the radially symmetric setting in a ball. Specifically, solutions emanating from initial values with mass below a critical mass M\textsubscr{c} > 0, which is characterized in terms of a variant of the Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev inequality, are global and bounded. In contrast, for any M > M\textsubscr{c}, there are initial values with mass M such that the corresponding global solutions are unbounded. The proof relies on the variational structure of the system and a detailed study of the stationary states.

items.title: Optimal polynomial meshes on quasicircles via conformal scale comparison
items.summary: We prove that every quasicircle $Γ\subset\mathbb{C}$ admits an optimal admissible polynomial mesh for univariate complex polynomials. More precisely, if $E$ denotes the closed Jordan domain bounded by $Γ$, then for every $Λ>1$ there are finite sets $A_n\subsetΓ$ with $\mathrm{card}(A_n)=O(n)$ and $\|p\|_E=\|p\|_Γ\leqΛ\|p\|_{A_n}$ for every $p\in\mathcal{P}_n(\mathbb{C})$. The nodes may be chosen as images of equally spaced points of the unit circle under the inverse exterior conformal map, equivalently as equal-mass points for harmonic measure at infinity. The proof combines the classical conformal level-curve scale with a discrete norming principle. If $ρ_n(z)$ denotes the distance from a boundary point to the exterior level curve $|Φ|=1+1/n$, Bernstein--Walsh and Cauchy's formula show that any sufficiently fine $ρ_n$-net is norming. A scale-comparison property then turns $O(n)$ equally spaced angular samples into such a net. Quasicircles satisfy this property by quasisymmetry. The argument requires no smoothness or rectifiability and applies in particular to the classical von Koch snowflake.

items.title: Convolution Algebras of Generalized Preprojective Algebras and Kac-Moody Positive Parts
items.summary: We realize the enveloping algebras of positive parts of symmetrizable Kac-Moody Lie algebras as convolution algebras of constructible functions on module varieties of Geiss-Leclerc-Schröer generalized preprojective algebras $Π(C,D)$. We characterize all pairs $(C,D)$ for which such a realization exists. These realizations generalize Lusztig's classical preprojective construction. The construction uses a folding embedding and torus actions on flag varieties.

items.title: The Subtractive Divisor Orbit: Unconditional Bounds, Parity Constraints, and a Conditional Framework
items.summary: Let $a(n)$ be the number of iterations of $F(m)=m-τ(m)$ needed to reach zero, where $τ(m)$ counts the positive divisors of $m$. Write $Δ(n)=a(n)-a(n-1)$. We prove that for every $\varepsilon>0$ and all sufficiently large $X$, each of the inequalities $Δ(n)\ge X^{1/2-\varepsilon}$ and $Δ(n)\le -X^{1/2-\varepsilon}$ holds for at least $X^{1-\varepsilon}$ integers $1\le n\le X$. The proof uses the identity $F(2m)=2F(m)$ at odd $m$ and the fact that an odd orbit first changes parity at a square. For every fixed $C>0$, a positive proportion of starting values $n\in(X,4X]$ satisfy $\left|a(n)-\frac{Cn}{\log n}\right|\gg_C\frac{\sqrt X}{\log X}$. For the hitting time itself we prove $a(x)\ll_b\frac{x}{(\log x)^b}$ for every $b<\log 2$, together with a lower bound having logarithmic exponent $2.988206\ldots$. On complete crossings of $(N,2N]$, with $Z=2N$, the logarithm of the step size has normal order $(\log 2)\log\log Z$, uniformly in the starting value. Computations through $10^9$ give the largest positive and negative first differences in this range.

items.title: Boiling Down Uncertainty: Deep Generative Scenario Search with Decision-Guided Evolution Strategies for Two-Stage Stochastic Optimization
items.summary: One of the most common models for handling uncertainty is two-stage stochastic programming. Choosing the right number of scenarios is a trade-off between the uncertainty that can be represented and computational cost. A recent method, Deep Generative Scenario Search, generates synthetic scenarios and improves them by learning from the decisions they induce. The original approach used a black-box gradient estimate, since decisions are piecewise constant across scenarios. This paper provides the missing analytical foundation by deriving the gradient in closed form from recourse duality and an adjoint solve of the regularized reduced problem. The decision-focused direction, with a heuristic direction as a backup when duals are unavailable, defines the sampling subspace of a guided evolution strategy rather than being used as a direct update. For any guiding subspace, the expected update is a descent direction of the smoothed objective, so an inaccurate guide adds variance while the expected step still descends. For six problem families, both guided estimators outperform the baseline. The decision-focused version reduces the mean gap by three-quarters, and on the two families with the most integer variables the reduced sets beat the exact solver's two-hour incumbent in most runs, using a fifth of the time.

items.title: Theta Functions and Intrinsic Mirrors of Laurent Phenomenon Algebras
items.summary: We construct bases of upper Laurent phenomenon algebras over a field by minimizing Newton polytopes in a single seed. For any translation-invariant total order on the exponents, each least exponent $a$ that occurs determines a smallest Newton polytope $Q_a$. Choose one element with Newton polytope $Q_a$ and least term $x^a$ for each such $a$. These elements form a basis. In every reachable seed chart, every Gauss valuation takes a nonzero basis expansion to the minimum of its values on the nonzero summands. Suppose the algebra has Laurent coefficients and smooth spectrum over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. After setting the curve parameters to one, we compute theta products on the intrinsic mirror from the exchange polynomials and give a finite presentation of the mirror algebra. A seed has a polynomial corner if each exchange polynomial can be multiplied by a unit of the coefficient ring to give a polynomial with constant term one. At such a corner, order the exponents by a weight with strictly positive, rationally independent coordinates. For every lattice exponent $a$ and integral weight $p$, the theta function indexed by $p$ has least $a$-weight $\min_{b\in Q_a}\langle b,p\rangle$ in the corresponding mirror chart. This reciprocity holds for cyclic exchanges and arbitrary pole orders. For fixed exchange supports and constant terms one, we determine when the mirror is smooth and the second mirror recovers the original algebra in the chosen torus coordinates. The coefficient tuples for which both conditions hold form a computable finite set. All their entries are positive integers.

items.title: Arithmetic Siegel-Weil formulas for unitary Shimura varieties with Iwahori levels
items.summary: In this paper, we formulate conjectural formulas for the arithmetic intersection numbers of special cycles on unitary Shimura varieties with Iwahori level structure. We first introduce a framework for formulating Kudla-Rapoport conjectures: we develop the theory of weighted representation densities and special cycles for general parahoric level structures, prove dimension-reduction formulas on both the analytic and geometric sides and duality relations for special cycles. We then formulate the Kudla-Rapoport conjecture for Iwahori level structures based on these properties. Finally, we prove the conjecture when $n=2$.

items.title: Coexistence and extinction in stochastic Lotka--Volterra systems with Volterra--Lyapunov stable interactions
items.summary: We consider stochastic Lotka-Volterra systems $dX=\mathrm{Diag}(X)(α+AX)dt+\mathrm{Diag}(X)Γ\,dB$ with nondegenerate noise and a Volterra-Lyapunov stable interaction matrix $A$, that is, $DA+A^\top D\prec0$ for some positive diagonal matrix $D$. This class covers every self-limited predator-prey food web that is conservative in the sense of Volterra, in particular every such web whose interaction graph is a forest. Let $β=α-\frac12\mathrm{diag}(ΓΓ^\top)$ be the vector of noise-corrected growth rates and $m=-A^{-1}β$. We show that the process has a stationary distribution under which all species have positive densities if and only if $m>0$. In that case the process is strongly stochastically persistent, and its stationary distribution is unique and has mean $m$. When $m>0$ fails, the species that survive are those present in the unique saturated nonnegative equilibrium $\bar x$ of the deterministic system $\dot x=\mathrm{Diag}(x)(β+Ax)$. Almost surely, the occupation measures converge to the stationary distribution of this subcommunity, and $\log X_i(t)/t$ converges to $(β+A\bar x)_i\le0$ for every species $i$. The proofs rely on the theory of invasion rates of Hening and Nguyen. For Lotka-Volterra systems, invasion rates are affine in the mean of the underlying measure. Combined with two quadratic identities, this provides explicit weights $Dm$ for their persistence theorem and identifies the limiting regime when persistence fails, without enumerating the invariant measures on the boundary.

items.title: How to facet a gemstone: from potential modularity to modularity lifting
items.summary: Let $F$ be a totally real field and $p\ge7$ a prime unramified in $F$. We prove that a potentially modular $p$-adic representation of $G_F$ which is potentially crystalline with distinct Hodge--Tate weights above $p$, and whose reduction is modular, non-dihedral and satisfies the usual Taylor--Wiles hypothesis, is modular. This removes the hypotheses of [MF] on the Serre weights: the multiplicity-free hypothesis, and the exclusion of Steinberg weights. The same method applies to potentially semistable representations. The proof combines the identity of cycles of [MF] with the modularity of lifts whose local components are mixed along an extension in which $p$ splits. These lifts exist by a theorem of Emerton, Gee, Pan and Zhu, they are potentially automorphic by a theorem of Calegari, Emerton and Gee, and their modularity is proved by tensoring with lifts of an auxiliary residual representation of a different weight: the tensor products lie on a common component of a local deformation ring for $\GL_4$, a lifting theorem of Thorne applies, and the factors of an automorphic tensor product are modular by [Die26].

items.title: Irreducibility, inertia and invertibility of the eccentricity matrices of unicyclic graphs
items.summary: The eccentricity matrix of a connected graph $G$, denoted by $\mathcal{E}(G)$, is obtained from the distance matrix of $G$ by keeping each entry that is the largest in its row or the largest in its column, and replacing all other entries by $0$. The eigenvalues of $\mathcal{E}(G)$ are called the $\mathcal{E}$-eigenvalues of $G$. In this article, we consider the eccentricity matrix of unicyclic graphs and study its various spectral properties. First, we give two sufficient conditions for the irreducibility of the eccentricity matrix of a connected graph, which generalize some previously known results. Then, we show that the eccentricity matrix of every unicyclic graph of girth $3$, $5$ or $7$ is irreducible and provide a unicyclic graph whose eccentricity matrix is reducible for every odd girth $g\ge 9$. On the other hand, we also provide a class of unicyclic graphs of odd girth, whose eccentricity matrices are always irreducible. Additionally, we find the inertia of eccentricity matrices of unicyclic graphs in which the trees attached to the cycle are nontrivial and have equal heights. Moreover, we characterize the graphs in this class whose E-eigenvalues are symmetric about the origin. Finally, we obtain necessary conditions for the invertibility of the eccentricity matrix of a unicyclic graph.

items.title: Low-Frequency Stable Single-Source Integral Equation
items.summary: Among the integral equations for scattering by homogeneous dielectric objects, single-source integral equations (SSIEs) provide the advantage of having only a single electric or magnetic current unknown. A well-conditioned SSIE can be obtained by appropriately combining the interior and exterior Calderón formulas. The condition number of the resulting operator appearing in the well-conditioned SSIE remains bounded at low frequencies. However, SSIEs still suffer from low-frequency cancellation, causing loss of significant digits in the solution, the right-hand side, and the system matrix. In this work, we apply a rescaling strategy based on quasi-Helmholtz projectors to the well-conditioned SSIE. Primal and dual space projectors are required since both primal and dual spaces are used to discretize the SSIE operators. We show that the solution of the rescaled SSIE is immune to catastrophic cancellations at low frequencies. Numerical experiments corroborate the method by testing the accuracy of the radiated field for extremely low frequencies.

items.title: On unique realisations of graphs under symmetry constraints
items.summary: Global rigidity asks whether a realisation of a graph is uniquely determined, up to Euclidean congruence, by its edge lengths. In this paper, we study global rigidity of bar-joint frameworks under finite point-group symmetry constraints. A framework is called forced-symmetric globally rigid in $d$-space if every realisation of the graph in $\mathbb R^d$ with the same edge lengths and the same prescribed symmetry is congruent to it. We establish symmetric extensions of two fundamental results on global rigidity. Our first result extends Hendrickson's necessary condition to the forced-symmetric setting. For symmetry-generic frameworks with an arbitrary finite point group acting freely on the vertices and with at least $d+2$ vertex orbits, we prove that forced-symmetric global rigidity implies forced-symmetric redundant rigidity. Our second result extends the classical characterisation of generic global rigidity for body-bar frameworks due to Connelly, Jordán and Whiteley. For the symmetric body-bar model considered here, we show that forced-symmetric global rigidity is a generic property and obtain a combinatorial characterisation in every dimension.

items.title: Deterministic Oracle Complexity for Goldstein Stationarity in Nonsmooth Nonconvex Optimization with Constraints
items.summary: We consider the deterministic oracle complexity of finding a $(δ,ε)$-Goldstein stationary point of a Lipschitz function under constraints. Our main result concerns products of convex bodies. Each block contains an inner ball and lies in a concentric outer ball. The inner radii have a common positive lower bound, and each outer radius is at most a fixed multiple of the corresponding inner radius. This class includes common constraints such as balls and boxes. On each prescribed feasible set of dimension $d$ in this class, every deterministic algorithm using a local oracle needs $\exp(Ω(d))$ objective-oracle calls in the worst case at fixed, sufficiently small accuracies $δ$ and $ε$. The objective Lipschitz and initial objective-value gap bounds are fixed, and each constructed function has a global minimizer in the interior of the feasible set. For broader classes of constraints, supplementary results show that every deterministic algorithm needs $Ω(ε^{-2})$ objective-oracle calls in the worst case when $d\gtrsimε^{-2}$ and $δ\lesssimε$. The constants depend on the interior-ball radius and, for inequalities, the local Lipschitz and Slater bounds. These supplementary results cover closed sets that are star-shaped with respect to a ball and convex coercive inequalities with a Slater point, and hold even for convex objectives.

items.title: A Proof of the Balister-Győri-Schelp Conjecture on Perfect Matchings with Prescribed Differences
items.summary: We prove the conjecture of Balister, Győri and Schelp on perfect matchings with prescribed differences. Let $n\ge 2$ and let $d_1,\dots,d_{2^{n-1}}$ be nonzero vectors in $\mathbb{F}_2^n$, with repetitions allowed. The space $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ can be partitioned into pairs $\{x_i,y_i\}$ with $x_i+y_i=d_i$ for every $i$ if and only if $\sum_i d_i=0$.

items.title: Aerodynamic Collision Avoidance Manoeuvres in Very Low Earth Orbit: Exploiting Lift for Short Warning Times and Reduced Orbital Decay
items.summary: Very Low Earth Orbits (VLEO, below $450\,\mathrm{km}$ altitude) offer promising mission capabilities for future spacecraft, but increasing traffic and the presence of orbital debris create collision risks that pose a particular challenge for satellites without conventional propulsion. Aerodynamic drag, resulting from interaction with the residual atmosphere, has been shown effective for performing collision avoidance manoeuvres (CAMs). However, short warning times remain challenging, and current methods do not exploit aerodynamic lift forces that enable out-of-track manoeuvres, which could help enhance control authority and mitigate drag-induced orbital decay. This work addresses both gaps by developing and evaluating two complementary optimisation methods: a heuristic approach using reachable set analysis to determine minimum lead times, and a direct shooting method to limit the increase in orbital decay due to the manoeuvre. Analyses using data derived from real conjunctions show that achieving a sufficient reduction in collision risk in the considered scenarios is feasible with lead times lower than one orbital period. Results also show that lift-based manoeuvres outperform drag-only approaches, with modest lead time reductions and more pronounced benefits in limiting orbital decay. Performance sensitivity to variations in control authority due to the type of gas-surface-interaction, altitude, and the encounter geometry is characterised. The methods and results presented highlight the potential of aerodynamic CAM for short warning time scenarios, contributing to sustainable operations in the increasingly congested VLEO environment.

items.title: Cup products with volume classes in bounded cohomology
items.summary: Let $M$ be a complete Riemannian $n$-manifold, $n\geq 2$, and suppose that either $M$ is negatively curved, or that it is a locally symmetric space of non-compact type. Via integration over straight simplices, every top-degree bounded differential form $ω\in Ω_b^n(M)$ defines a bounded cohomology class in $H^n_b(M)$. We prove that every such class belongs to the annihilator of the cup product in the whole graded algebra $H^{\geq 1}_b(M)$. In the case of closed orientable surfaces, this generalizes a result of Marasco, and, via transfer, provides a new proof of the fact that the cup product of the bounded Euler class of $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ with itself vanishes. Our result also applies to degree-3 bounded classes constructed by Soma and Farre, thus showing that, for surface groups and for free groups, the annihilator of the cup product is infinite dimensional also in degree 3.

items.title: Discrete approximation of semi-Dirichlet forms with non-symmetric perturbations of resistance forms
items.summary: In this paper, we study discrete approximations of semi-Dirichlet forms obtained by adding non-symmetric drift terms, expressed in terms of mutual energy measures, to resistance forms whose associated resistance metric spaces are compact. The main novelty is that the drift terms need not to be absolutely continuous with respect to the underlying measure. Under suitable smallness assumptions, we prove generalized Mosco convergence of the approximating forms and derive weak convergence of the associated Feller processes. We also demonstrate the applicability of our main theorem to post-critically finite self-similar fractals and describe the resulting perturbation of the approximating jump chains in the case of the Sierpiński gasket.

items.title: How many sorted projections determine any n points in k dimensions?
items.summary: Let $d_1,\dots,d_m$ be directions in $\mathbb{R}^k$, where $k\ge 2$. A multiset $X$ of $n$ points of $\mathbb{R}^k$ projects to the $m$ multisets of numbers $\{\{x\cdot d_j : x\in X\}\}$, or equivalently to the $m$ sorted lists of these numbers. How many directions are needed for these projections to determine every multiset of $n$ points? Two simple bounds are known in every dimension: more than $(k-1)\log_2 n$ directions are always needed, and $(k-1)n+1$ directions in general position always suffice. In the plane much more is known: Matousek, Privetivy and Skovron showed that almost every choice of $O(\log n \log\log n)$ directions suffices. Whether anything similar holds in higher dimensions was left open by Dym, Wellershoff, Tsoukanis, Levy and Balan. We observe that two lemmas of Hair and Sahai, proved for list recovery of random linear codes, answer that question, and by tightening their argument we show that in every dimension almost every choice of $(4k-2)\ln(2n)\ln(k\log_2 2n)+k+1$ directions suffices. For $k\le 10$ this beats the linear bound once $n$ is larger than about 100: for example, 144 directions suffice for multisets of 1000 points in the plane, and an exact computation lowers this to 133. Letting some of the random blocks in their argument fail removes a factor $\log k$: almost every choice of $O(k\log n\log\log n)$ directions suffices, uniformly in $k$ and $n$. We also show that $2k-1$ directions never determine three points, so that the logarithmic lower bound is not tight; that every $m$ directions in the plane fail on some pair of multisets of size $O(1.65^m)$, improving the bound $O(1.80^m)$ of Matousek, Privetivy and Skovron; and that for each $k$, $m$ and $n$, either almost every choice of $m$ directions works or almost none does.

items.title: The centre of mass of the primes and a reflection of Chebyshev's bias
items.summary: For $x\ge2$ we place a unit mass at $\log p$ for each prime $p\le x$, and let $D(x)$ be the distance from the centre of mass of this system to $\log x$; thus $D(p_n)=\log(p_n/G_n)$, where $G_n$ is the geometric mean of the first $n$ primes. Let $D_0(x)$ be the distance obtained when $π$ is replaced by $\mathrm{Li}(x)=\int_2^x dt/\log t$. We prove that $D(x)-D_0(x)\ll x^{Θ-1+\varepsilon}$, where $Θ$ is the supremum of the real parts of the zeros of $ζ(s)$, and that the exponent cannot be lowered; in particular, the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to $\log(p_n/G_n)=D_0(p_n)+O_\varepsilon(p_n^{-1/2+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$. Under the Riemann hypothesis we prove a pointwise mirror theorem: for large $x$ the centre of mass lies to the left of its predicted position only when $π(x)<\mathrm{li}(x)-1.95\sqrt{x}/\log x$. Under the Riemann hypothesis and the linear independence hypothesis, the set of such $x$ has the same logarithmic density as the set on which $π(x)>\mathrm{li}(x)$, although for large $x$ the two sets are disjoint. We prove analogues for primes in arithmetic progressions, for the higher moments of the system, and, under a linear independence hypothesis, for $\mathbb{F}_q[T]$, where the biases of even and odd degrees are interchanged.

items.title: Fast Queries of Fibered Barcodes
items.summary: The fibered barcode $\mathcal{F}(M)$ of a bipersistence module $M$ is the map sending each non-negatively sloped affine line $\ell \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ to the barcode of the restriction of $M$ along $\ell$. The simplicity, computability, and stability of $\mathcal{F}(M)$ make it a natural choice of invariant for data analysis applications. In an earlier preprint [arXiv:1512.00180], we introduced a framework for real-time interactive visualization of $\mathcal{F}(M)$, which allows the user to select a single line $\ell$ via a GUI and then plots the associated barcode. This visualization is a key feature of our software RIVET for the visualization and analysis of bipersistent homology. Such interactive visualization requires a framework for efficient queries of $\mathcal{F}(M)$, i.e., for quickly obtaining the barcode along a given line $\ell$. To enable such queries, we introduced a novel data structure based on planar line arrangements, called an augmented arrangement. The aim of the present paper is to give an updated and improved exposition of the parts of our preprint [arXiv:1512.00180] concerning the mathematics of the augmented arrangement and its computation. Notably, by taking the input to be a minimal presentation rather than a chain complex, we are able to substantially simplify our main algorithm and its complexity analysis.

items.title: Endowing phase-field fracture models with custom strength criteria
items.summary: By now, several approaches have been proposed to endow phase-field fracture models with the ability to describe crack nucleation under multiaxial stress states. These include techniques for splitting the free energy, direct modifications of the phase-field driving or resisting forces, and the introduction of additional internal variables, such as plastic strains or other nonlinear strains. In this paper, we propose a fundamentally different strategy for incorporating arbitrary elastic domains into phase-field fracture models, formulated within the energetic framework of generalized standard materials. The proposed approach relies on letting the dissipation potential depend on the current state of the material. In this way, the elastic degradation and the strength criterion remain two distinct and independently controllable aspects of the material response, while the governing equations directly descend from a local stability condition and energy balance. Simple yet representative models are presented and thoroughly discussed to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methodology. The resulting evolution of the elastic domain is investigated in both strain and stress spaces under proportional and non-proportional loading paths, with the latter highlighting the path dependence of the dissipated work. Moreover, numerical simulations demonstrate a range of crack nucleation processes under multiaxial loading conditions for various analytical strength surfaces. The present work paves the way for future developments and applications in several directions, including crack propagation studies and dedicated numerical solution strategies.

items.title: The Min-Cut Formulation of Ollivier-Ricci Curvature
items.summary: Computing Ollivier-Ricci curvature normally requires a local distance matrix and a linear program per edge, prompting workarounds based on entropic regularization or combinatorial proxies. We show that exact curvature needs neither. For any one-step measures, the Kantorovich dual has an integral three-level optimum, reducing each edge to one minimum s-t cut on a distance-free network linear in the read adjacency lists. This solves instances requiring quadratically many distance queries in linear time, while a converse reduction shows that no exact algorithm can beat bipartite matching. Our solver is a median 6 times (up to 506 times) faster than distance construction plus $\mathtt{POT}$'s C++ simplex, 441 times faster than $\mathtt{GraphRicciCurvature}$, and 23 times faster than graph min-cost flow. Even given the distances, Sinkhorn iterations at $\mathtt{GraphRicciCurvature}$'s regularization are a median 12 times slower, and combinatorial proxies alter edge rankings, missing the bulk of the most negatively curved ones.

items.title: Global Weak Solutions and Non-Formation of Vacuum States for Compressible Navier--Stokes--Korteweg Equations
items.summary: A long-standing open problem in the mathematical theory of M-D fluid dynamics in viscous compressible flow is whether vacuum can form in finite time from initial data with density bounded away from zero. The underlying assumption in the derivation of systems of Navier--Stokes type from physical principles is that the fluid is non-dilute and can be described as a continuum. A negative answer to this problem would support the self-consistency of the continuum assumption for the Navier--Stokes-type models. This issue is particularly important when the viscosity coefficients are constant, since, from a physical standpoint, it is unclear how to meaningfully define the fluid velocity in vacuum regions, which in turn makes it difficult to interpret the associated viscous stresses. In this paper, for the barotropic compressible fluid with capillary effects, when the coefficients of viscosity and capillarity are all constants, we establish the global existence of weak solutions of the Cauchy problem for the corresponding Navier--Stokes--Korteweg equations with initial data that are large, radially symmetric, and away from the vacuum in two and three spatial dimensions. The failure of the well-known BD entropy estimate poses a substantial challenge to establishing this existence theory. Moreover, we rule out finite-time vacuum formation for the 2-D radially symmetric weak solutions constructed here. This extends, for the first time, the well-known Hoff--Smoller non-vacuum-formation theory (Commun. Math. Phys. 2001) from 1-D compressible Navier--Stokes equations with constant viscosity coefficients to 2-D radially symmetric flows with capillarity.

items.title: On Observability Decomposition of Boolean Control Networks
items.summary: This paper studies the observability decomposition of Boolean networks (BNs) and Boolean control networks (BCNs) in the semi-tensor product framework. We characterize when a BN admits an observability decomposition in terms of the equivalence classes induced by indistinguishability. We prove that a decomposition exists if and only if all such equivalence classes have the same cardinality, and we explicitly construct the coordinate transformation together with the matrices of the observable and unobservable subsystems. The observable subsystem is shown to be the quotient graph obtained by contracting each class into a single vertex. For BNs whose equivalence classes have unequal cardinalities, we propose an extended observability decomposition by adding virtual states, and show that every finite BN admits an observability decomposition in an extended sense. These results are further generalized to BCNs, for which an algorithm and an illustrative example are provided.

items.title: Ergodicity of the geodesic flow on nonpositively curved surfaces
items.summary: We prove that the geodesic flow of a closed, connected surface of negative Euler characteristic with a $C^{3+\mathrm{Lip}}$ metric of nonpositive curvature is ergodic with respect to Liouville measure. The singular set, consisting of directions whose geodesics remain in zero curvature for all time, has zero Liouville measure. Ergodicity then follows from Pesin's theorem.

items.title: The transversal game
items.summary: Two players take turns claiming empty cells from an $n\times n$ grid. The first player (if any) to occupy a transversal (a set of $ n $ cells having no two cells in the same row or column) is the winner. What is the outcome of the game given optimal play? Our aim in this paper is to show that for $n\ge 4$ the first player has a winning strategy. This answers a question of Erickson. We also consider variants of the game in which the family of winning transversals is restricted, both in the original game and in its Maker--Breaker version.

items.title: High-order polynomial corrections for embedded curved boundaries in discontinuous Galerkin methods for hyperbolic systems: from staircase instabilities to a gap method
items.summary: High order polynomial corrections, which impose the boundary conditions on an embedded boundary by modifying the polynomial of the surrogate boundary cells, give accurate and robust discretizations of elliptic problems on unfitted meshes. We show that, used out of the box in discontinuous Galerkin discretizations of hyperbolic systems on Cartesian meshes, the shifted boundary and minimization-based (ROD) corrections become unstable, with eigenvalues of positive real part that no restriction of the time step can remove. Linear advection, whose operator is block triangular, is the least affected case: a tilted straight boundary makes every correction unstable with the geometry-normal map, while the face-orthogonal map, which likely gives a one-dimensional character to the boundary condition with tensor-product bases, keeps the 1D stability up to one polynomial degree less. The slip wall of the linear acoustic system is much more critical: all the corrections are unstable already on a tilted straight wall, and an energy balance shows that the cause is the misalignment, in direction and in position, between the faces of the staircase and the wall. Since the origin of the instability is geometric, we act on the surrogate boundary itself, and develop the gap paradigm for discontinuous Galerkin discretizations of hyperbolic systems: each boundary cell is extended, by extrapolating its polynomial without new degrees of freedom, up to the segments joining the projections of its vertices on the wall, where the boundary condition is imposed, and neighbouring extended cells exchange information through the numerical fluxes used on the interior interfaces. Numerical experiments confirm the energy stability of the gap method on a straight wall and show high order convergence on curved walls, in configurations where the classical corrections applied on the staircase diverge.

items.title: Integral Means of Fibonacci Numbers: Divisibility, Density, and Arithmetic Structure
items.summary: Motivated by recent works of Fatehizadeh, Yaqubi, Flynn-Connolly, Luca and Marques on the arithmetic mean of Fibonacci numbers, we study divisibility properties of sums of Fibonacci numbers whose indices form arithmetic progressions. We show that infinitely many even and odd $n$ divide such sums, and also the corresponding sums of squares and cubes, and we find all $n$ for which the geometric and harmonic means of $F_1,\ldots,F_n$ are integers. Further, we study the set $\mathcal{A}$ of integers $n\geq2$ for which the arithmetic mean of $F_1,\ldots,F_n$ is an integer. We show that $\mathcal{A}$ is both rich and sparse: it contains arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions and does not contain odd prime powers, yet $\#\{n\leq x: n\in\mathcal{A}\}\ll x/\sqrt{\log x}$. This density-zero bound holds more generally for every set $\{n: n\mid\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}F_{r+id}\}$. We also establish necessary conditions for three consecutive integral means (a question of Luca and Marques).

items.title: Homotopy types of complexes of hyperplanes in quasi-median graphs and applications to right-angled Artin groups
items.summary: In this article, we prove that, given two finite connected graphs $Γ_1$ and $Γ_2$, if the two right-angled Artin groups $A(Γ_1)$ and $A(Γ_2)$ are quasi-isometric, then the infinite pointed sums $\bigvee_\mathbb{N} Γ_1^{\bowtie}$ and $\bigvee_\mathbb{N} Γ_2^{\bowtie}$ are homotopy equivalent, where $Γ_i^{\bowtie}$ denotes the simplicial complex whose vertex-set is $Γ_i$ and whose simplices are given by joins. These invariants are extracted from a study, of independent interest, of the homotopy types of several complexes of hyperplanes in quasi-median graphs (such as one-skeleta of CAT(0) cube complexes). For instance, given a quasi-median graph $X$, the \emph{crossing complex} $\mathrm{Cross}^\triangle(X)$ is the simplicial complex whose vertices are the hyperplanes (or $θ$-classes) of $X$ and whose simplices are collections of pairwise transverse hyperplanes. When $X$ has no cut-vertex, we show that $\mathrm{Cross}^\triangle(X)$ is homotopy equivalent to the pointed sum of the links of all the vertices in the prism-completion $X^\square$ of $X$.

items.title: Online Ramsey numbers of the claw versus cycles
items.summary: The online Ramsey number $\tilde r(G,H)$ is defined via a Builder--Painter game on an empty graph with countably many vertices. In each round, Builder reveals an edge, which Painter immediately colors either red or blue. Builder wins once a red copy of $G$ or a blue copy of $H$ appears, and $\tilde r(G,H)$ is the minimum number of edges Builder must reveal to force a win. For a long cycle $C_\ell$, the online Ramsey numbers $\tilde r(G,C_\ell)$ are known only for a few specific choices of $G$. In particular, exact values were determined for $G=P_3$ by Cyman, Dzido, Lapinskas, and Lo (Electron. J. Combin., 2015), while asymptotically tight results were obtained when $G$ is an even cycle by Adamski, Bednarska-Bzdȩga, and Blažej (SIAM J. Discrete Math., 2024). In this paper, we consider the case where $G$ is the claw $K_{1,3}$ and determine the exact value of $\tilde r(K_{1,3},C_\ell)$. We show that \[ \tilde r(K_{1,3},C_\ell)=\left\lfloor \frac{3(\ell+1)}{2} \right\rfloor \quad \text{for all } \ell \ge 13. \]

items.title: Characterizing $2$-slices over finite groups
items.summary: For a finite group $G$, we characterize the $2$-slices of $G$-spectra in the regular slice filtration in terms of their homotopy Mackey functors and $k$-invariant. We explicitly compute this for cyclic $p$-groups and the alternating group $A_4$.

items.title: Diffusion-Score-Based Joint Topology Identification and Generative Particle Filtering
items.summary: Inferring the interaction graph of a networked system while tracking its latent state is central to infrastructure, environmental, and brain networks. Joint identification of topology and latent states is challenging when observations are intermittent and transition noise is unknown and non-Gaussian: a flexible generative transition can absorb graph-induced changes of the conditional mean, whereas a Gaussian transition discards the information in the residual shape. We develop a diffusion-score-based framework for joint topology identification and generative particle filtering. The graph governs a leaky-diffusion conditional mean, and a frozen diffusion emulator represents the conditionally centered residual. First, a score--topology duality expresses edge-wise likelihood gradients as edge projections of the residual diffusion score, so topology learning requires neither transition densities nor differentiation through the sampler. Second, we prove identifiability from intermittent observations, invariance of the population minimizer across noise levels, and global strong convexity above an explicit smoothing threshold for bounded-plus-Gaussian residuals. With known support and oracle state pairs, the asymptotic covariance approaches the Cramér--Rao bound as smoothing vanishes and is strictly smaller than that of any Gaussian quasi-likelihood estimator under an explicit non-Gaussianity condition; for unknown sparse support we characterize the boundary limit, and we quantify the topology bias caused by residual-score mismatch. Third, we couple score-driven graph updates with an approximately fully adapted generative particle filter and prove, for bounded residuals under explicit excitation and forgetting conditions, a mean-square closed-loop bound with a step-size-independent small-gain condition. Synthetic and real-data experiments confirm these gains under non-Gaussian forcing.

items.title: Steiner porism and boundary value problems
items.summary: The aim of this paper is to describe several interpretations of Steiner chains of circles in terms of certain boundary value problems and give a short review of related results. Our approach and discussion are motivated by the recent results on the geometry of Steiner porism based on an apparently novel analytic parametrization of poristic circles obtained by A.Diakvnishvili and the present author. We also mention a few feasible problems and generalizations suggested by the constructions and considerations presented in the paper. Keywords: Steiner chain of circles, Steiner porism, curvature, invariant moments of curvatures, boundary value problem, Riemann-Hilbert problem, Brylinski loop space, circle packing

items.title: Cyclic source pairings for Penrose--Sparling non-Hausdorff twistor spaces
items.summary: We determine the stable source information carried by the gluing-groupoid algebra of the Penrose--Sparling non-Hausdorff twistor double. Relative normal residues define supported analytic $K$-classes with specified normal orientations. For a smooth double along a closed submanifold, we compute the full geometric periodic cyclic homology as the parity sum of the compactly supported cohomologies of the ambient manifold and the doubled locus. In the physical model, $K_0\cong\Z^4$ and $HP_0\cong\C^4$, with both odd groups zero. Four explicit cocycles give integral $K$-coordinates and exhaust continuous periodic cyclic cohomology; every periodic cyclic pairing on supported source classes is therefore a linear combination of rank and degree. Finite moments recover $K$-valued normal profiles modulo integral common line twists. A first-jet criterion tests mixed-line triviality and identifies the residue with the torsion cokernel of a generically invertible second fundamental form for pullback quotients. The degree-one Euler modification and the diagonal Coulomb embedding have identical filtered $K$-profiles in every algebraic $SL_2$ representation, while their rank-two Ward connections are respectively indecomposable and split. We give the Euler connection and its transition between both root charts. An elementary holonomy realization shows that the inherited ambient and divisor transverse classes annihilate supported source classes. The relative degree pairing uses an additional choice of opposite defect orientations.

items.title: The Gilmer-Masbaum map is not injective on the Kauffman bracket skein module
items.summary: Gilmer and Masbaum use Witten-Reshetikhin-Turaev (WRT) invariants to define a map from the Kauffman bracket skein module to a set of complex-valued functions defined on roots of unity in order to provide a lower bound for its dimension. We compute the image of the evaluation map for a family of mapping tori of the 2-torus and find that the restriction of the map to certain homology classes is not injective. This provides an answer to a question posed by Gilmer and Masbaum in the latter paper. Moreover, we give a basis for the Kauffman bracket skein module in the case of the mapping torus of a power of the Dehn twist along the meridian of the 2-torus.

items.title: Integral Hodge/Tate conjecture of quotients via weak approximation
items.summary: For a finite group acting on a smooth projective separably rationally connected variety over an algebraically closed field, we prove that the rational quotient map induces a surjection from the coinvariants of its second Kato homology onto the second Kato homology of any smooth projective quotient model (with coefficients invertible in the ground field). The integral Hodge and Tate conjectures for one-cycles consequently descend to such quotient models. The proof uses weak approximation over function fields to retain the image of a smooth fiber in the total space.

items.title: Quantitative Gibbs Transfer in Fiber-Contracting Extensions:\ Thermodynamic Formalism, Livšic Theory, and Sharp Logarithmic Distortion
items.summary: We study the transfer of Gibbs estimates between a compact dynamical system and a factor with uniformly contracting fibers. A cohomological identity relates the orbit sums; the remaining issue is the comparison of Bowen-ball masses. Subexponential comparison errors give directional weak Gibbs transfer, while bounded errors preserve strong estimates. We also establish a blockwise sequential version along prescribed Gibbs-time sequences, with errors measured against the full block length. Geometric and conditional-mass hypotheses provide practical criteria for these comparisons. A stationary renewal model shows that the distinction between bounded and subexponential comparison is essential. Its invariant lift to a contracting Cantor-fiber extension is not supported on a measurable graph, and the optimal uniform forward logarithmic error is $\log n+O(1)$. This remains true under fixed changes of the base radius. The reverse comparison, along a specified section, has bounded error. We also give an example in which pointwise subexponential bounds cannot be made uniform. For context, projection gives an affine bijection of invariant probability measures and preserves entropy. When the potentials are cohomologous, invariant averages and pressure agree, as do minimizing measures and equilibrium states in the finite-pressure regime. For Hölder potentials, a continuous section yields a stable-direction reduction, with Hölder regularity under additional assumptions. Subactions and Livšic solutions can then be lifted whenever the corresponding quotient hypotheses hold.

items.title: Cone Restriction Estimates under Half-Scale Dimensional Conditions
items.summary: We prove cone restriction estimates under half-scale dimensional conditions. Building on the framework of Du--Li--Wang--Zhang, we incorporate the broad restriction estimate of Ou--Wang and a localized multilinear estimate obtained through cyclic bilinear pairing and multilinear Kakeya bounds for local packet $L^2$-norm. The zero-dimensional case yields a large-value estimate on $R^{1/2}$-cubes. For certain ambient and weight dimensions, our estimates are sharp in suitable ranges of $p$, up to an $R^\varepsilon$ loss.

items.title: On the maximal operator of the hybrid Hermite-Laguerre-Jacobi semigroup
items.summary: We consider the heat-diffusion semigroup related to expansions with respect to an orthogonal system emerging by taking arbitrary finite tensor products of classical Hermite, Laguerre and Jacobi polynomials. Our main result is the weak type $(1,1)$ estimate for the associated maximal operator. This implies pointwise almost everywhere boundary convergence of the semigroup to initial values for all initial conditions that are integrable against the orthogonality measure.

items.title: Bound-preserving Flux Limiters for Hyperbolic Conservation Laws on Two-Dimensional Adaptive Moving Meshes
items.summary: In this paper, we develop a bound-preserving finite-volume method on adaptive moving meshes for two-dimensional hyperbolic conservation laws. The proposed method extends our previous one-dimensional framework [Y. Gu, G. Hu, and T. Tang, Adaptive mesh methods for hyperbolic conservation laws with bound-preserving flux limiters, arXiv:2602.12580] to two dimensions within the arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian framework. The mesh velocity is determined by solving a moving mesh equation, allowing the numerical solution to evolve directly between consecutive time levels. A key challenge in this extension is to ensure compatibility between the evolution of the mesh geometry and the update of the numerical solution, as geometric information is essential to the convex decomposition underlying the bound-preserving construction in two dimensions. Specifically, the high-order scheme is reformulated as a convex combination of high-order sub-cell schemes, each of which is blended with its first-order counterpart to enforce the bound-preserving property. The discrete geometric conservation law ensures the compatibility needed to maintain this convex decomposition on moving meshes. The resulting correction acts locally at individual cell interfaces and is equivalent to applying a bound-preserving flux limiter, making the approach applicable to general unstructured or irregular meshes. The associated bound-preserving CFL conditions are established for both scalar conservation laws and the nonlinear Euler equations of gas dynamics. Extensive two-dimensional numerical experiments demonstrate the accuracy, robustness, and effectiveness of the proposed method.

items.title: Toward Extreme-Scale Full-Wave Maxwell Simulation: Low-Dispersion Discretization and a Massively Parallel Three-Grid Solver
items.summary: Full-wave simulation of three-dimensional time-harmonic Maxwell problems over hundreds of wavelengths leads to indefinite systems with tens to hundreds of billions of unknowns. We present a matrix-free three-grid solver for such systems and its implementation on GPUs and CPUs. The solver is built on an interpolated optimized finite-difference (IOFD) discretization on the Yee grid, whose compact face and edge filters keep the phase error small at 6 points per wavelength, and it applies the same compact stencil on all three grids: an unshifted intermediate-grid correction is preconditioned by a complex-shifted auxiliary cycle, so that one preconditioner application performs a fixed number of stencil sweeps and reductions with storage linear in the number of unknowns. The implementation uses a partition nested across the grids, $s$-step smoothers that need one global reduction per smoothing call, and bfloat16 storage of the smoother bases. On 216 GPUs, complete solves with approximately $71.7$ billion complex unknowns take 77--504 seconds in homogeneous and heterogeneous media, with weak-scaling efficiencies of 89--91\% per preconditioner application; strong scaling reduces solves with 2.7 billion unknowns to 4.5--18 seconds on 64 GPUs. A CPU implementation reaches approximately $574$ billion unknowns on 13\,824 cores, and the computed fields agree with the outgoing Green field over domains of up to 956 wavelengths per direction.

items.title: The socle of the last term in a minimal injective resolution II
items.summary: Let $R$ be a Gorenstein ring with left and right self-injective dimensions $n$. We prove that the last term of a minimal injective resolution of $_RR$ has an essential socle. It answers an open question of Iwanaga and Sato. As a consequence, we get that for any left $R$-module $M$ with injective dimension $n$, the last term of a minimal injective resolution of $M$ also has an essential socle.

items.title: Correlation functions of 2D critical models via a KPZ relation for conformal blocks
items.summary: The Knizhnik--Polyakov--Zamolodchikov (KPZ) relation allows scaling exponents of two-dimensional (2D) critical systems to be derived from their counterparts in Liouville quantum gravity. We extend this framework to correlation functions based on an integral inversion relation between Virasoro conformal blocks with complementary central charges $c$ and $26-c$. We demonstrate this method in various models by deriving the 2-point disk correlation from their quantum counterpart and the KPZ relation. Results on critical loop models were previously known, but our method is robust enough to include many scenarios previously unsolved, such as the Fuzzy Potts model. Our approach is complementary to the conformal bootstrap.

items.title: An adaptive finite element method for the interior problem of Helmholtz equations with generalized transmission boundary conditions
items.summary: This paper proposes a new adaptive finite element method for solving the interior transmission problem with generalized transmission boundary conditions (GTBCs) involving a surface Laplace-Beltrami operator. A $\mathbb{T}$-coercivity technique relying on a lifting operator is established to show the well-posedness of the variational problem in appropriate nonstandard Sobolev spaces. Then both the a priori error estimates and a posteriori error estimates including the upper bound and local lower bound of the finite element discretization are constructed. Numerical examples are presented to illustrate the accuracy and convergence of the adaptive finite element method. Extension and high efficiency of the proposed method for the computation of the interior transmission eigenvalues for the problem with GTBCs are also discussed numerically.
