items.title: Area-minimizing surfaces and the rigidity of three-dimensional electrostatic systems
items.summary: We study three-dimensional electrostatic systems, the Riemannian data of static solutions of the Einstein--Maxwell equations with cosmological constant $Λ$, by means of locally area-minimizing surfaces. Such a surface with non-empty boundary on the horizons is a totally geodesic hemisphere and forces the de Sitter system. A closed one in the interior forces a system of product type, one of eight models if the scalar curvature is somewhere positive on it, among them the Bertotti--Robinson, Nariai and cold and ultracold black hole systems. No compactness, asymptotic or pinching assumption is needed. In particular, closed systems without horizons are flat or compact quotients of the Nariai--Bertotti--Robinson system. For compact systems with connected horizon, the electric field vanishes even when the system is not simply connected, and the area of the horizon is either $12π/Λ$, for de Sitter, or at most $4π/Λ$. With several horizons, every horizon whose area does not exceed the sum of the others is stable, minimizes area in its homology class and satisfies an area--charge inequality, with equality only for the charged Nariai systems; its charged Hawking mass and charge therefore lie in the parameter region of the Reissner--Nordström--de Sitter black holes. Compact systems with horizons are spherical space forms with balls removed. Noncompact systems with strictly mean-convex ends have one end, and their horizons are stable and $π_1$-injective and satisfy a strict area--charge inequality.

items.title: Sharp estimates for imaginary powers of discrete Laplacians
items.summary: Let $Δ_{\rm d}$ be the nonnegative discrete Laplacian on $\mathbb Z^d$. We prove that, for $0<p\le1$, \[ \|Δ_{\rm d}^{iγ}\|_{H^p_{Δ_{\rm d}}\to H^p_{Δ_{\rm d}}} \lesssim (1+|γ|)^{d(1/p-1/2)}, \] and, for $1<p<\infty$, \[ \|Δ_{\rm d}^{iγ}\|_{\ell^p\to\ell^p} \lesssim (1+|γ|)^{d|1/p-1/2|}. \] The estimates are sharp with respect to the exponent of $1+|γ|$. We also explain why the general spectral multiplier theorem and the usual Calderón--Zygmund approach do not give the sharp power.

items.title: The Martingale Property in Volterra Volatility Models
items.summary: We study martingality and strict local martingality in a broad class of stochastic and path-dependent Volterra volatility models and explain the underlying mechanisms. Our martingality criteria allow rough kernels and rely on non-accessibility of an explosive direction or one-sided growth bounds on the Girsanov drift. For smooth kernels, we derive sufficient conditions for strict local martingality from an explosion criterion allowing multiplicative noise, coupled factors and general initial input curves. Our results recover classical criteria and yield new results for Volterra and path-dependent models.

items.title: Hardy and BMO spaces for the Laplacian with drift
items.summary: We study Hardy and BMO spaces associated with the Laplacian with drift. We define an atomic Hardy space $H^1$ whose atoms satisfy cancellation against constants and linear functions in directions perpendicular to the drift. We prove the John--Nirenberg inequality, Hardy--BMO duality, equivalence of finite and infinite atomic norms, and interpolation theorems. We show that the Riesz transforms and their adjoints are bounded from $H^1$ to $L^1$ and from $L^\infty$ to BMO. Moreover, we prove that the cancellation conditions are optimal, but the Riesz transforms do not characterize $H^1$. We also characterize the $L^p$ boundedness of their commutators, $1<p<\infty$, in terms of local BMO.

items.title: Perfect state transfer in Grover walks on generalized Bethe trees
items.summary: We completely classify the generalized Bethe trees $B(d_0,d_1,\ldots,d_{n-1})$ that exhibit perfect state transfer between vertex states in Grover walks. We prove that such a tree exhibits perfect state transfer if and only if it is a path or a uniform subdivision of either $B(2,3)$ or $B(1,2,3)$. We also determine all transferring pairs and the minimum transfer times.

items.title: A sharp form of Welsh's log-concavity inequality for chromatic polynomials
items.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph of order $n\ge 1$, and let $P_G(x)$ be its chromatic polynomial. In the early 1970s, Welsh conjectured that $P_G(k)^2 \ge P_G(k-1)P_G(k+1)$ holds for any positive integer $k$. This conjecture was also independently proposed by Brenti in 1992, while in 1997, Seymour disproved it for $k=6$ by constructing an infinite family of graphs of sufficiently large order as counterexamples. In 2005, Dong, Koh and Teo conjectured that $P_G(x)^2 \ge P_G(x-1)P_G(x+1)$ holds for all real $x\ge n$. In this paper, we prove that the inequality holds for all real $x\ge n-1$. Equality holds if and only if $n\ge 2$, $G$ is complete, and $x=n-1$. Moreover, the bound $x\ge n-1$ is best possible for every $n\ge 2$.

items.title: The clumsy coupon collector's problem
items.summary: We consider a generalisation of the classical coupon collector's problem, in which at each time step a collector either receives a new copy of a randomly chosen coupon, or loses all their previously collected copies of that coupon. We consider the amount of time it takes this clumsy coupon collector to obtain the full set of $m$ coupons. We establish limit theorems as $m\to\infty$ for the clumsy coupon collection time, and describe the large $m$ asymptotics of its mean and variance. We identify three regimes, depending on how the probability of a clumsy update, $p$, scales with $m$. If $p=o(1/m)$, we obtain a Gumbel limit theorem, as is the case for the classical coupon collector. If $p=ω(1/m)$, we instead show weak convergence to an exponential random variable. In the critical case, $p\sim c/m$, we give a full characterisation of the limiting distribution in terms of a birth-and-death process. We also describe the asymptotics of the mean and variance in these three regimes.

items.title: Counting tree-child and reticulation visible networks
items.summary: For tree-child networks with $n$ leaves and $k$ reticulations, we identify an entire critical scaling function at $k=x\sqrt n$ and its first uniform correction. The function is a Gaussian factor times the Laplace transform of Brownian excursion area. An exact coefficient integral then yields the explicit amplitude $π\Ai'(a_1)$ for the maximal-reticulation count, where $a_1$ is the largest negative Airy zero, together with three logarithmic corrections. A summable defect expansion transfers these results to the total number of tree-child networks. For reticulation-visible networks, we construct an exact weighted refinement over maximal tree-child networks. The total defect from $3n-3$ reticulations splits into a skeleton defect, an arity excess, and an ordinary-leaf count. The skeleton defect has a uniformly bounded exponential moment, and the full partition function differs from its maximal-skeleton sector by a bounded factor, smaller than $30$ at activity one. A positive algebraic kernel and an explicitly solved variational problem give the pressure with logarithmic error $O(n^{2/3}\log^{2/3}n)$. This determines the total exponential growth, the location of every mode, a full large-deviation principle, and limiting structural densities. At activity $z=t/n$ with fixed $t>0$, we also prove a $\operatorname{Poisson}(19t/4)$ limit and coefficient asymptotics uniform for defects $q=o(n^{1/3})$.

items.title: A posteriori error estimates for Runge-Kutta discontinuous Galerkin approximations of nonlinear convection-diffusion systems
items.summary: This work provides reliable a posteriori error estimates for Runge-Kutta discontinuous Galerkin approximations of nonlinear convection-diffusion systems. The classes of systems we study are quite general, with a focus on convection-dominated problems and systems with partial diffusion. Our a posteriori error bounds are valid for a family of discontinuous Galerkin spatial discretizations and various temporal discretizations that include explicit and implicit-explicit time-stepping schemes, popular tools for practical simulations of this class of problem. We prove that our estimators provide reliable upper bounds for the error of the numerical method and present numerical evidence showing that, in the convection-dominated regime, the residual quantities converge at the same rates as the discretization errors. Since one of our main interests is the convection dominant case, we also track the dependence of the estimator on the viscosity coefficient.

items.title: OpenAI's proof of the local smoothing conjecture: A harmonic analytic perspective
items.summary: This note presents OpenAI's proof of the local smoothing conjecture. It is written for harmonic analysts who may be new to quaternionic Monge--Ampère equations. We introduce the quaternionic Hessian and explain how the associated determinant equation leads to the critical annular estimate.

items.title: A proof of the weighted Böttcher-Wenzel inequality conjectured by Mayumi, Kimura, Ohno and Chruściński
items.summary: For a positive definite matrix $ω$ with two smallest eigenvalues $λ_1\leλ_2$ and the weighted Frobenius norm $\|X\|_ω^2=\mathrm{Tr}(X^*Xω)$, Mayumi, Kimura, Ohno and Chruściński conjectured that $\|[A,B]\|_ω^2\le\frac{λ_1+λ_2}{λ_1λ_2}\|A\|_ω^2\|B\|_ω^2$ for all complex matrices $A,B$. We prove this inequality for real and for complex matrices of every size, by a short computer-free argument, and we determine the cases of equality. In fact $\|XZY-YZX\|_2\le\|Z\|_{(2),2}\|X\|_2\|Y\|_2$ for all complex matrices of compatible sizes, where $\|Z\|_{(2),2}$ is the Ky Fan $(2),2$ norm (the $\ell^2$ norm of the two largest singular values), and the constant is attained unless $X$ and $Y$ are $1\times1$ matrices; the conjecture is the case $Z=ω^{-1/2}$. The best constant is the square of a unitarily invariant norm of $Z$, which is convex, so it suffices to treat weights whose $n-1$ largest eigenvalues coincide. For these, an inequality for one matrix and a pair of unit vectors, written in bases adapted to the pair of unit vectors, reduces the conjecture to the positive semidefiniteness of an explicit $4\times4$ Hermitian matrix depending on a $2\times2$ matrix $B$ in a convex set defined by two weighted operator-norm bounds, and an explicit determinant identity writes its determinant as a sum of products of factors that are visibly nonnegative; the phases of the entries of $B$ enter only through $|\det B|^2$, so the real case is literally a special case. As a second theorem we prove, for every weight, a strengthening of the conjecture that is equivalent to the inequality for one matrix and all pairs of unit vectors; its best constant is again a convex function of $ω^{-1/2}$, and the same argument applies. We also read the inequality as a sharp bound for inner derivations on the GNS space of a faithful state.

items.title: On the solving degree and complexity of Gröbner Basis computation over finite fields
items.summary: Solving systems of multivariate polynomial equations over finite fields is a central problem in algebraic cryptanalysis, commonly approached using Gröbner basis algorithms. The complexity of Gröbner basis computation depends on the algorithm employed and is governed by the solving degree, defined as the maximum degree of the polynomials processed during the computation. Estimating this quantity is therefore crucial, and several bounds in terms of the degree of regularity have been established in the literature. In this work, we investigate the effect of Buchberger's criteria on the elimination of redundant pairs, and prove that the solving degree of a Gröbner basis algorithm combining linear algebra with Buchberger's original algorithm is bounded above by the degree of regularity defined by the leading forms of the involved polynomials. This result provides a rigorous justification for using the degree of regularity in complexity estimates for Gröbner basis algorithms, thereby supporting a common assumption in algebraic cryptanalysis. We refine the complexity analysis by establishing bounds on the number of pairs that must be processed. These bounds improve upon published complexity estimates, with particularly significant gains in certain parameter ranges.

items.title: A quasi-orthogonal method based on the inverse operator for Schrödinger eigenvalue problems
items.summary: The simultaneous computation of many Schrödinger eigenpairs requires mutually orthogonal eigenfunctions. We propose a quasi-orthogonal evolution model based on the inverse operator and a two-stage time discretization for nonorthogonal initial data. The continuous trajectory and discrete iterates remain full rank and approach orthogonality without any orthogonalization. The discretization preserves the current Gram matrix in the first stage and reduces the orthogonality error in the second. We establish well-posedness, energy decay, asymptotic orthogonality, and exponential convergence to the target eigenfunctions up to fixed orthogonal transformations. Numerical experiments for two Schr{ö}dinger eigenvalue problems validate the decay of the energy, gradient norm, and relative iterate error, while the iterates become numerically orthogonal. Further experiments show that the discrete time steps remain effective under mesh refinement, that convergence rates depend on the spectral gap, and that dynamically adjusting the solve accuracy can accelerate the computation.

items.title: Derivations of Low-Dimensional Filiform Lie Superalgebras
items.summary: We determine the even and odd derivations of the 91 entries in Gilg's classification list of complex filiform Lie superalgebras of superdimensions (2|2), (2|3), (2|4), (3|2), (3|3), (4|2), (5|2) and (6|2). A unified linear system yields explicit matrix parametrizations and the dimensions of both homogeneous components of the derivation superalgebra. The results are given in block-matrix form.

items.title: Reflection positivity of discrete and Brownian loop-soup occupation fields
items.summary: The intensities guaranteeing reflection positivity of loop-soup vertex occupations on every reflection-symmetric finite graph with positive semidefinite cross-conductance matrix of rank $r$ form the real Wallach set $\W_r$. For the renormalized occupation field on the massless planar Dirichlet strip, the exact set is $\bigcap_{r\geq1}\W_r=\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\ldots\}$.

items.title: Shock formation in traffic flow models with Arrhenius look-ahead interactions
items.summary: We study finite-time shock formation in a nonlocal traffic flow model with Arrhenius look-ahead dynamics. For the constant interaction potential, we derive a time-dependent lower bound for the minimum slope and obtain a sufficient condition with logarithmic dependence on the magnitude of the minimum initial slope. For the linear interaction potential with look-ahead distance $γ$, we show that the condition $u'_0(x_0)>\frac{1}γ$ at a single point is sufficient for shock formation, which is independent of the minimum initial slope. Our results strictly improve the corresponding conditions of Lee and Liu \cite{r17}.

items.title: Sharp Barycentric Costs in Teichmuller Space
items.summary: The affine Beltrami fiber over a closed hyperbolic surface has a quadratic normal response whose least vertical $L^2$ energy equals the tangent norm dual to the hyperbolic cotangent supremum norm. We prove this calibration using a curvature identity and exact localized responses. Its strictness determines the energy measures of near-minimizers and, under an amplitude constraint, gives a positive excess with an explicit quadratic lower coefficient when the supporting differential has nondegenerate maxima. Pointwise Poincar'e barycenters of representatives in one fiber give a nonlinear realization: equal-weight pairs attain prescribed small outputs exactly, and their creation energy approaches the calibrated norm if and only if the output scale is negligible relative to the squared amplitude bound. Restoring the full local fiber graph has leading cost four times the squared Weil--Petersson norm. For degenerating surfaces, we identify the additive limit of the calibrated norm across persistent components and collar directions. The induced length metric completes to marked augmented Teichm"uller space and has distance $\fracπ{2}\sum_i \ell_i + O((\sum_i \ell_i)^2)$ to a fixed pinching stratum. Systole-dependent estimates also yield exact nonlinear realizations along degenerating families.

items.title: Rigidity, flexibility, and a sign error
items.summary: The documents [OAI26a, OAI26b, OAI26c] claimed to prove cases of the Hodge conjecture via homological mirror symmetry, before being withdrawn by OpenAI. We discuss the source of the error (but do not analyse the rest of the argument).

items.title: Inverse problems for ZS operators and their isomorphisms, II
items.summary: We study isomorphic inverse spectral problems for Zakharov--Shabat operators on the unit interval with generic boundary conditions. A unitary gauge transformation reduces these problems to the corresponding problems with basic boundary conditions, with an explicit shift of the spectral parameter. Using previous results for canonical boundary conditions and four-spectra data mapping we describe isomorphic inverse spectral problems for Zakharov--Shabat operators. Moreover, we study other inverse problems including replacing mappings and canonical relations.

items.title: A staggered discontinuous Galerkin neural network method with a computable error decomposition
items.summary: We develop a staggered discontinuous Galerkin neural network (SDGNN) method for scalar elliptic problems with a computable error decomposition. The staggered discontinuous Galerkin (SDG) method requires only local continuity of its trial functions and gives a square, inf-sup stable system without stabilization parameters; we carry this structure over to neural networks. Networks on the patches of a staggered mesh satisfy the SDG continuity conditions for all parameter values, and the loss, the squared dual norm of the SDG weak residual, is computed without the SDG finite element approximation or any solution data, so that the training is unsupervised. By the inf-sup stability, the loss is equivalent, with computable constants, to the square of the training error, the distance between the SDG projection of the network and the SDG finite element approximation, so that the full error is bounded by the discretization error, a multiple of the square root of the loss, and the network projection error. For a fixed network on uniform square meshes, this error decays exponentially in the polynomial degree. The weak residual requires no derivatives of the networks and no penalty or stabilization weights, and the scalar trial functions may jump across the midlines of the primal cells. Numerical experiments show that the square root of the loss tracks the error during training, that prescribed jumps across a square and a circular interface are captured consistently over the initializations, and that the method is more accurate than physics-informed neural networks at the same parameter counts.

items.title: Trace-defined double covers of the $S_3$-involution graph of $PSL_2(2^n)$
items.summary: For $q=2^n\ge 4$, we construct a family of Deza double covers $Γ(q,ξ)$ of the $S_3$-involution graph of $PSL_2(q)$, parametrized by $ξ\in\mathbb F_q^*$. We show that each resulting cover is connected, arc-transitive and amply regular with parameters $(2(q^2-1),q,Tr(ξ),1)$, where $Tr$ denotes the absolute trace. We also show that the trace-one covers are antipodal of diameter $5$ and girth $3$, whereas the trace-zero covers are non-antipodal of diameter $3$ and girth $5$. For $q=4$, these cases yield the well-known icosidodecahedral and dodecadodecahedral graphs, respectively. Then we determine the distance distributions and full automorphism groups of the covers and prove that, for fixed $q$, two covers are isomorphic if and only if their defining parameters lie in the same Frobenius orbit. We also express the Ramanujan property of a cover in terms of the spectral norm of a signed adjacency matrix of the base graph.

items.title: Nonexistence of positive entire solutions to systems of semilinear elliptic inequalities
items.summary: Consider the system $Δu \geq p(x)g(v)$, $Δv \geq q(x)f(|\nabla u|)$, with $u>0$ and $v>0$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$, where $n\geq2$, $f,g\in C[0,\infty)$ and $p,q\in C(\mathbb{R}^n)$. If $f,g$ are non-decreasing and convex, using a comparison argument we prove a sufficient Keller-Osserman type condition for the nonexistence of entire solutions. This result is sharp for a wide class of systems. Similar results are also shown to hold for systems without gradient terms.

items.title: Computing expectations associated with McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equations via probability-flow ordinary differential equations
items.summary: This work considers the numerical approximation of expectations of functionals of $d$-dimensional McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equations (MV-SDEs) with random initial conditions. Standard numerical schemes employ a stochastic interacting particle system of $P$ coupled $d$-dimensional SDEs, whose empirical measure converges to the MV-SDE law. However, naive Euler--Maruyama Monte Carlo (MC) estimators based on particle systems achieve a computational complexity of $\mathcal{O}\left( \text{TOL}^{-4} \right)$ to satisfy a prescribed error tolerance TOL. To reduce this complexity, this work reformulates the associated nonlinear Fokker--Planck equation as a Liouville equation describing the evolution of the law of a deterministic mean-field ordinary differential equation (ODE) with random initial conditions, sharing the same marginal distributions as the original MV-SDE. The resulting mean-field ODE eliminates the need to approximate Itô integrals and permits the use of higher-order integration schemes in time and stochastic space. However, simulating trajectories requires the score function of the MV-SDE's marginal law, which is approximated using a statistical estimator based on a system of $P$ coupled $d$-dimensional ODEs. The proposed estimator combines randomized quasi-MC in the stochastic variables and Runge--Kutta integrators in time, with efficient score estimation. Under assumptions on weak-error and variance convergence, the resulting estimator achieves a computational complexity of $\mathcal{O}\left(\text{TOL}^{-\left(\max\{β/α,2\} + 1/γ\right)}\right)$, where $α$ and $β$ denote, respectively, the weak-error and variance convergence rates with respect to $P$, and $γ$ is the order of the time-integration scheme.

items.title: Homothetic Copies of Polytopes and Binomial Barcodes
items.summary: Let $X\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ be a finite full-dimensional configuration, and put $F_X(N)=\max_{S\subset\mathbb{R}^d, |S|=N}\#\{(\mathbf{v},λ)\in\mathbb{R}^d\times(0,\infty):\mathbf{v}+λX\subseteq S\}$. Elekes and Erdős posed the problem of estimating $F_X(N)$. In this article, we determine its exact value when $X$ is the vertex set of a simplex. For several other classes of configurations, we obtain sharp asymptotic bounds and exact extremal values. We also introduce binomial barcodes for order polytopes and a recursive criterion for their effectiveness. In particular, if $X$ is the vertex set of the three-dimensional cube, then, for $n\ge 1$, $F_X(n^3)=\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}j^3=\left(\frac{n(n-1)}{2}\right)^2$.

items.title: Exact Last-Iterate Bounds and Optimal Stepsizes for Proximal Stochastic Gradient Descent
items.summary: Proximal Stochastic Gradient Descent minimizes the sum of an $L$-smooth convex function $f$, known through unbiased stochastic gradients of bounded variance, and a nonsmooth convex function $R$, known through its proximity operator. We derive the exact worst-case value of the expected objective gap of its last iterate, for every predetermined stepsize schedule in a broad class, which contains all the schedules with stepsizes at most $3/(2L)$. This extends to the composite setting a recent result of Grimmer and Shen for the smooth case $R=0$. The value is the sum of an initial-error term and of one term per iteration, which is the price of the noise injected at this iteration, damped by the stepsizes that remain after it. The upper bound is proved with a simple potential, the Moreau envelope of the objective with a smoothing parameter proportional to the remaining stepsize sum, and it is attained by an explicit instance. The formula shows that a logarithmic factor is unavoidable with a constant stepsize, and it gives the exact price of the proximity operator, relative to the smooth case. It also makes the choice of the stepsizes a tractable optimization problem: for a uniform variance bound $σ^2$, the best schedule is unique, decreasing, and computed by a scalar search, and it is minimax optimal among all predetermined schedules, unless the noise level is low. Asymptotically, the minimax value $M_T$ after $T$ iterations satisfies $(Dσ/M_T)^2=T+\log T+C_\star+o(1)$, where $D$ is a bound on the initial distance to a solution and $C_\star\approx1.768$ is a universal constant; unlike in the smooth case, $L$ plays no role at this order. This law is achieved by an explicit schedule, which is the optimal one when $f=0$.

items.title: Robust stochastic first order methods in heavy-tailed noise via medoid mini-batch gradient sampling
items.summary: We consider a first order stochastic optimization framework where, at each iteration, $K$ independent identically distributed (i.i.d.) data point samples are drawn, based on which stochastic gradients can be queried. We allow gradient noise to be heavy-tailed, with possibly infinite variances. For the considered heavy-tailed setting, many algorithmic variants have recently been proposed based on gradient clipping or other nonlinear operators (e.g., normalization) applied over noisy gradients. In this paper, we take an alternative approach and propose a novel gradient estimator. The core idea of proposed estimator is to split the $K$-sized data batch into $M$ distinct data chunks, form for each chunk the stochastic gradient, and select the stochastic gradient of the chunk that is medoid of gradients of all data-chunks. For a broad class of symmetric heavy-tailed gradient noise distributions, we show that the proposed estimator has a finite second moment even when the underlying gradient noise has an infinite second moment. For nonconvex objectives, this yields convergence to a neighborhood of zero in expected squared gradient norm at a rate of $\mathcal{O}(T^{-1})$. We explicitly characterize the size of this neighborhood in terms of the noise and algorithm parameters. When the time horizon $T$ is known in advance, we establish an $\mathcal{O}(T^{-1/2})$ convergence rate. A diminishing step size achieves the same rate up to a logarithmic factor. Incorporating clipping or a more general nonlinear transformation yields high-probability convergence guarantees with the same rate up to logarithmic factors. Experimental results indicate that R-SGD-Mini and its clipped or nonlinear variant consistently perform favorably compared to SGD, clipped SGD, Nonlinear SGD and Median-of-Means based methods.

items.title: An Introduction to O-minimal Geometry
items.summary: These lecture notes on o-minimal geometry comprise six chapters: 1 - O minimal Structures. 2 - Cell Decomposition. 3 - Connected Components and Dimension. 4 - Definable Triangulation. 5 - Generic Fibers for Definable Families. 6 - Smoothness.

items.title: Three combinatorial identities of the Rogers-Ramanujan type
items.summary: The purpose of the present paper is to establish three combinatorial Rogers--Ramanujan type identities. Although their motivation comes from the representation theory of affine Lie algebra of type $A_2^{(2)}$, our proofs are entirely combinatorial and analytic. They follow the automata-theoretic approach introduced by Takigiku and Tsuchioka in their proof of Nandi's conjecture and adapt it to the present setting.

items.title: Invariant measures for stochastic heat equations with dissipative drift in the whole space
items.summary: We study the long-time behavior of a nonlinear stochastic heat equation on the whole space $\mathbb{R}^{d}$, driven by a Gaussian noise that is white in time and spatially homogeneous. The equation features a reaction term $f$ satisfying a one-sided Lipschitz condition and a bounded, globally Lipschitz diffusion coefficient $σ$. Solutions are constructed in a scale of weighted continuous function spaces. Under an additional dissipativity condition on $f$, which covers reaction terms of the form $f(u)=u-u^{3}$, we prove that the transition semigroup admits an invariant measure on some weighted space $C_ρ$. This constitutes the first step toward a complete ergodic theory for dissipative stochastic heat equations on unbounded domains, a setting that has so far remained largely open in the literature.

items.title: On moments of the Erdős--Hooley Delta-function
items.summary: For integer $n\geqslant 1$ and real $u$, let $Δ(n,u):=|\{d:d\mid n,\,{\rm e}^u<d\leqslant {\rm e}^{u+1}\}|$. The Erdős--Hooley Delta-function is then defined by $Δ(n):=\max_{u\in{\mathbb R}}Δ(n,u).$ We provide new upper bounds for weighted real moments of this function.

items.title: Notes for a seminar on vortex layer cascades
items.summary: After the seminars I recently gave at New York University, the University of Chicago, Princeton University and the University of Bonn and after having been asked by some people to publish these notes, I decided to upload them to arXiv. In recent years, the method of vortex layer cascades has successfully been applied to construct finite-time singularities in multiple fluid equations (3D Euler, Boussinesq, IPM, g-SQG...). In this talk, I will motivate and describe the method and sketch how it can be applied to the 2D Boussinesq and 2D non-homogeneous Euler equations. In both systems, the growth of the vorticity is driven by an accumulated hysteresis effect triggered by the cyclic deformation of the density layers, whose dynamics is governed by an infinite chain of degenerate pendula. Our work also settles the previously open question about global existence of classical solutions of the (forced) 2D non-homogeneous Euler equations.

items.title: Smyth completeness and nonexpansive iteration in $q$-hyperconvex $T_0$-quasi-metric spaces
items.summary: We study the specialization order $\le_d$, defined by $x\le_d y$ if and only if $d(x,y)=0$, of a $q$-hyperconvex $T_0$-quasi-metric space $(X,d)$. We show that every nonempty bounded subset $A$ of $X$ has an infimum $\bigwedge A$ characterized by the metric formula $d(w,\bigwedge A)=\sup_{a\in A}d(w,a)$ for all $w\in X$, and dually a supremum, and that powers and copowers exist. For bounded $X$ this gives an elementary proof, with explicit metric formulas, of the known fact that Isbell-convex Lawvere metric spaces are complete in the sense of enriched category theory; the formulas themselves and the extension to bounded subsets of unbounded $q$-hyperconvex spaces are not covered by the enriched-categorical argument, which requires radii in $[0,\infty]$. Consequently no $T_1$-quasi-metric space with at least two points is $q$-hyperconvex, and the fixed points of every order-preserving self-map of a bounded $q$-hyperconvex space form a nonempty complete lattice. We show that the fixed point set of a nonexpansive self-map need not be a sublattice and that the specialization order need not be distributive. Our main result concerns the continuity of nonexpansive maps. Nonexpansive self-maps of bounded $q$-hyperconvex spaces need not preserve suprema of increasing sequences, and the supremum of the orbit of the least element need not be a fixed point. We prove that for a bounded $q$-hyperconvex $T_0$-quasi-metric space the following are equivalent: the space is Smyth complete; every increasing sequence converges to its supremum in the symmetrized metric; every nonexpansive self-map preserves suprema of increasing sequences; every nonexpansive self-map preserves suprema of directed sets; every nonexpansive self-map is Yoneda-continuous. In this case Kleene iteration from the least element converges to the least fixed point; this applies for instance when the symmetrized metric is compact.

items.title: Interpolation of nonlocal Sobolev spaces for general gradients
items.summary: We study the interpolation structure of nonlocal Sobolev spaces associated with general radial gradients. For compactly supported kernels satisfying suitable regularity and two-sided growth assumptions of fractional order, we characterize the spaces $H^{ρ,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$, $1<p<\infty$, by the Gustavsson--Peetre interpolation method between $L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ and $W^{1,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$. The function parameter is determined, up to equivalence, by the behavior of the kernel near the origin. We also establish a complex interpolation formula between spaces associated with different kernels and integrability exponents, in which the interpolated kernel is their geometric mean. For the corresponding nonlocal Gagliardo spaces $W^{ρ,p}(\R^n)$, defined through an integral seminorm of first differences, we prove an identification with generalized Besov spaces and a real interpolation characterization involving the same function parameter. These results extend the classical relation between Bessel potential and Gagliardo spaces beyond power-type kernels, yielding continuous embeddings between the two families and their coincidence in the Hilbertian case. We further discuss logarithmic kernels and restriction spaces on Lipschitz domains, and obtain extension and compact embedding results for the Gagliardo spaces under weaker assumptions on the kernel.

items.title: Admissibility of Linear Time Series Models under Cone Constraints
items.summary: Time series analysis extends beyond vector-valued observations to evolving probability densities, quantile functions, and covariance operators. These objects carry intrinsic constraints, raising questions about the admissibility of additive linear models, which have long served as a foundation for time series modelling and theory. We give a necessary and sufficient support condition for a stationary Hilbert-space linear process to remain in a closed convex cone almost surely. Innovations with unbounded lower tails, including Gaussian innovations, confine randomness to the cone's largest linear subspace. For fractional filters with convergent normalized cumulative coefficients, the leading stochastic directions obey the same restriction, even with bounded innovations. For real-line quantiles, variation under unbounded lower tails and leading fractional accumulation can occur only through location shifts. For cone-valued processes, partial sums of centred stationary increments remain bounded in mean square when evaluated by any linear functional that is nonnegative on the cone, in contrast to the growing variance of a random walk. We derive an exact slope criterion for locally absolutely continuous quantiles and construct nondegenerate additive models with bounded innovations for quantiles, densities, and covariance matrices. These findings clarify the scope of ordinary additive modelling under structural constraints.

items.title: Time-uniform bounds and long-time asymptotics for a three-species drift-diffusion model for memristors
items.summary: The qualitative behavior of weak solutions to the two-dimensional drift-diffusion equations for memristors, incorporating Shockley-Read-Hall-type generation-recombination terms and time-dependent boundary conditions, is investigated. The model couples the electron, hole, and oxygen-vacancy densities to the electric potential through the Poisson equation. The global existence and uniqueness of weak solutions are established. If the boundary data converge to the thermal equilibrium at an integrable rate, the densities remain uniformly-in-time bounded above and below, and the solution converges exponentially fast to thermal equilibrium. For time-independent boundary data and sufficiently small applied bias, solutions converge exponentially fast to steady states carrying nonzero fluxes.

items.title: Well-Posedness of the Hodge Wave Equation on a Compact Manifold
items.summary: In this work, we study the Hodge wave equation on a compact orientable manifold. We present the necessary differential geometry language to treat Sobolev spaces of differential forms and use these tools to identify a boundary triplet for the problem. We use this boundary triplet to determine a class of boundary conditions for which the problem is well-posed.

items.title: On the number of positive solutions of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation on compact star graphs
items.summary: In this paper, we consider the number and the shape of positive solutions of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation on compact symmetric star graphs with Dirichlet condition at the exterior vertex and Kirchhoff condition at the central vertex.

items.title: OmniAct: One Policy, One Million Embodiments
items.summary: A single policy that controls diverse robots must not only transfer task knowledge across embodiments, but also adapt its behavior to each robot's capabilities. Existing approaches facilitate transfer through shared action representations, but these representations do not necessarily capture how differences in robot morphology should shape manipulation strategies. We introduce OmniAct, a cross-embodiment manipulation policy that conditions directly on each robot's kinematics in a specific scene to produce embodiment-specific behavior. This kinematic graph represents the robot's joint positions, motion axes, and connectivity to its visual observation, allowing the policy to account for how its embodiment related to objects and surfaces in the scene. A flow-matching policy predicts relative joint motions for each node, enabling control across robots with different degrees of freedom and kinematic configurations. To learn how physical structure shapes behavior at scale, we procedurally design and filter one million physically feasible robot embodiments; next, we develop algorithms to generate robot trajectories in simulation for all embodiments; finally, we train across diverse simulated manipulation tasks. On 2,000 embodiment-scene-held-out evaluation episodes, OmniAct achieves 63.0% success, compared to 17.8% for pi 0.5 and 57.9% for the strongest baseline; on the task families GPT-6 Astra was evaluated on, it achieves 64.7% against GPT-6 Astra's 41.1%. On a previously unseen real-world robot, it achieves nearly twice the success rate of the next best method, MolmoAct2. Beyond task success, we observe that OmniAct learns distinct manipulation strategies that exploit the capabilities and accommodate the limitations of different morphologies. Project: https://omniact.github.io/

items.title: PointX: Multi-View Consistent Intrinsics by Querying Surface Points
items.summary: The appearance of a scene is determined by the albedo, roughness, metallicity and normal of every point on its surface, and by the light that reaches it, its irradiance. Recovering these intrinsics from images is ambiguous, and methods that predict them per pixel give the same surface point a different decomposition in every view. We introduce PointX, a simple feed-forward model that predicts intrinsics per 3D surface point instead. A multi-view transformer encodes a set of unposed images, and for any queried surface point, PointX pools the point's tokens across the views in which it appears and decodes the point's intrinsics once. Each point of a 3D reconstruction of the scene, such as a point cloud or a mesh, thus receives a single prediction, which is exactly consistent across views by construction and enables view-consistent relighting and editing. The same model also predicts per-view maps, from one image or many, by querying the point seen at every pixel. These maps agree across views up to the precision of the estimated geometry and correspondences. PointX is significantly more consistent than existing methods, while remaining competitive in accuracy from a single image and improving as views are added. Project page: https://pointx-paper.github.io/

items.title: DiaCap: Jointly Learning Who Speaks When for Audiovisual Dialogue Captioning
items.summary: We present DiaCap, an audiovisual LLM for comprehensive dialogue captioning, which produces the transcript, timestamps, and a visual description of the speaker for every utterance in a video. Considering that utterance timing and audiovisual diarization are tightly coupled, DiaCap unifies the tasks in a single model, trained in two complementary stages. First, we train DiaCap on 225K curated clips, using synthetic captions that densely label every utterance in detail. Second, we further refine the model via reinforcement learning on 2.9K human-corrected clips, using fine-grained feedback that directly evaluates utterance timing, speaker grouping, and speaker binding. On DiaDemBench, which we extend with utterance-level timestamps and subtitle redaction, both DiaCap with off-the-shelf transcripts and its end-to-end variant DiaCap-E2E achieve strong results. Specifically, DiaCap performs on par with Gemini 4 Argon in audiovisual diarization while clearly outperforming it in timestamp accuracy (76.59 vs. 42.76 TIME). It also maintains strong diarization on multilingual and minute-long videos, and transfers to audiovisual question answering.

items.title: BioLoom: Scaling Biomedical Vision-Language Models by Learning from the Structure of Scientific Articles
items.summary: The development of biomedical vision-language models (VLMs) with contrastive image-text pretraining has been driven by scaling to increasingly large and diverse image-text datasets. Beyond scaling, further progress can come from learning richer representations from existing data. We hypothesize that the structure of scientific literature itself provides an additional source of supervision: figures, panels, captions, and accompanying article text encode rich relationships across modalities. Yet, treating these as independent image-text pairs overlooks their relationships. To address this limitation, we incorporate these structural relationships into contrastive image-text supervision. We preserve exact image-text matches while introducing weaker positive supervision for related pairs, such as a panel and the caption of a sibling panel. We upweight cross-article negatives of the same content type to encourage finer discrimination. We also enrich panel descriptions using visual content, original figure captions, and mentioning paragraphs. Pairing panels with these descriptions and whole figures with their original captions yields Loom52M, a dataset of 52.4 million image-text pairs spanning scientific charts and biomedical images. Using Loom52M, BioLoom (DFN-2B) achieves 56.82% domain-balanced mean accuracy across 67 zero-shot classification tasks from 43 datasets in 10 domains, compared with 48.77% for MedPMC-CLIP. On BioLoomBench with concise captions and BioMedFlickr, it achieves bidirectional mean Recall@1 of 63.20% and 10.59%, versus 46.37% and 7.55% for the respective strongest evaluated baselines, BiomedCLIP and MedPMC-CLIP. Code, datasets, benchmarks, and models are available at https://bioloom-clip.github.io/.

items.title: Envy-Free Cake-Cutting for Five Agents
items.summary: We study the envy-free cake-cutting problem, in which a divisible resource must be divided among a set of agents with heterogeneous preferences in a way that ensures that no agent envies the piece obtained by another. Remarkably, under some mild continuity assumptions on the agent valuations, it is known that an envy-free division where each agent receives a \emph{connected} piece of the cake is always guaranteed to exist. When the valuations are monotone, prior work has shown that a connected $\varepsilon$-envy-free division can be obtained using $\poly(\log(1/\varepsilon))$ queries for up to four agents, leaving the case of five or more agents open. In this work, we develop a new simpler approach that yields such an efficient algorithm for five agents. Our algorithm uses $\mathcal{O}(\log^3(1/\varepsilon))$ queries and also yields a novel proof of existence for five agents that does not rely on any fixed-point theorems beyond the intermediate value theorem.

items.title: CoT-Proxy: Cross-Format Transfer for Distilling Long-Horizon Policies
items.summary: Reasoning models become long-horizon agents through reinforcement learning or, more cheaply, through fine-tuning on a stronger teacher's trajectories, which contain the teacher's chain-of-thought as well as its actions. The standard fine-tuning approach imitates both, yet the strongest teachers are closed models whose chain-of-thought is hidden behind an API. We show that the chain-of-thought can be left out altogether and that the long-horizon policy can be distilled from the teacher's actions alone. The student is trained on these trajectories with its reasoning block left empty, while a KL loss on a replay buffer of its own generations limits drift from its initial model. Surprisingly, the policy learned from these trajectories with an empty reasoning block carries over to inference with thinking enabled, where the student reasons in its own style while acting like the teacher, an effect we call cross-format transfer. Distilling the actions of Qwen3.6-27B raises the task success of Qwen3-4B on AppWorld from 7% to 18% and that of Qwen3-32B from 12% to 25%. We further introduce CoT-proxies, short summaries of the teacher's reasoning placed after the empty reasoning block, which raise Qwen3-4B further, to 35%. Since neither actions nor CoT-proxies need the hidden chain-of-thought, the recipe applies unchanged to closed teachers. Distilling GPT-5.6 Luna from its visible outputs and the reasoning summaries its API returns raises Qwen3-4B from 7% to 48% on AppWorld and from 3% to 28% on SWE-bench Verified.

items.title: One Take, Many Cameras: Audio-Grounded Shot Synthesis for Dialogue Re-Cinematography
items.summary: Creating a dialogue scene typically requires cutting between multiple views (e.g., close-ups, medium shots, and over-the-shoulder shots) of the actors. Yet capturing such coverage is costly and in many settings unavailable. We study dialogue re-cinematography: synthesizing additional shots from a single wide-angle dialogue video. Existing video generators can synthesize new shots, but rely on visual cues alone, so when the source video barely shows the lips, the generated lip motion fails to match the speech. Our key observation is that the speech audio is view-invariant: it constrains lip motion in any target view. Building on this insight, we adapt a pretrained audio-visual diffusion model to generate the new shot from a target frame that specifies the view, a source video that contains the performance, and the speech audio that drives lip motion. In multi-person scenes, however, pretrained audio-visual models drive every visible face with the same speech, causing speech leakage, where silent listeners mouth the speaker's words. We therefore introduce speaker-aware audio gating, a training-free module that lets the audio drive only the faces that speak in the target shot. On a cinematic paired-view benchmark spanning diverse viewpoints and framings, our method lowers perceptual error by 59%, landmark error by 56%, and speech leakage by 97% relative to the strongest baseline, Wan 3.0. Our method also remains robust on in-the-wild scenes, highlighting its potential for film post-production.

items.title: Lost on Campus: Evaluating Embodied Spatial Reasoning of Vision-Language Models in the Wild
items.summary: Embodied Spatial Reasoning (ESR) is central to deploying Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in real-world embodied tasks, yet remains inadequately evaluated. Existing benchmarks primarily assess spatial reasoning in static images or synthetic indoor environments, where semantic shortcuts often suffice, making it difficult to faithfully evaluate spatial reasoning capabilities in the wild. In light of this, we present Lost on Campus, a benchmark for evaluating ESR in large-scale real-world outdoor 3D environments reconstructed by 3D Gaussian Splatting. Our benchmark introduces a unified reasoning-action evaluation framework that seamlessly integrates diagnostic QA for isolated reasoning with closed-loop interactive navigation for active reasoning under multimodal instructions. To enable fine-grained diagnosis, we evaluate six capability aspects of ESR: action grounding, spatial foresight, metric awareness, goal-directed planning, ego-allocentric localization, and spatio-temporal consistency. Extensive experiments reveal that: (i) Compared to indoor settings, real-world outdoor environments impose substantially higher demands on spatial reasoning, where existing models exhibit poor performance; (ii) VLMs still struggle with fine-grained visual alignment, with failures in spatial foresight and ego-allocentric localization emerging as primary bottlenecks; (iii) Improving multimodal interaction capabilities and long-term spatial reasoning is crucial for advancing embodied intelligence. These findings highlight that faithful evaluation of ESR demands benchmarks tightly coupling perception, reasoning and action within realistic and continuous environments.

items.title: PyRUA-Dex: Learning Programmatic Policies for Dexterous Bimanual Manipulation with Coding Agents
items.summary: Learning for dexterous manipulation is limited by the scarcity of high-quality demonstrations: retargeting from human video is imprecise, teleoperation gives no force feedback to the operator, and exoskeleton-based collection is hard to scale up. We present PyRUA-Dex, a framework that enables coding agents to develop dexterous manipulation through programmatic policy, without the need of demonstrations. The programmatic policy is developed in two stages: during exploration, multiple agents explore in parallel for task skills and ways to compose them, and a distilling agent condenses the successful attempts into a task library and one program. During refinement, this program is improved through randomized layouts for enhanced robustness and execution efficiency. In simulated environments, PyRUA-Dex achieves SOTA on Bench2Dex with a score of 72.9 and reaches 81.0% success on DexJoCo under full randomization, ahead of every trained policy on both benchmarks. In real world experiments on a bimanual platform with two 22-DoF hands, PyRUA-Dex learns to play piano, write calligraphy, and other tasks efficiently: learning a new piece from sheet music takes as little as 30 minutes. These results suggest that PyRUA-Dex is an effective framework for developing dexterous manipulation policies with coding agents in the absence of high quality dexterous manipulation demonstrations.

items.title: ROAM-Bench: Evaluating Embodied Active Spatial Intelligence through Evidence Verification
items.summary: Embodied spatial intelligence requires agents to gather information through exploration and interaction, then use it to reason and act. Existing benchmarks insufficiently distinguish correct outcomes from completion of these task requirements. We introduce ROAM-Bench to evaluate these abilities under robot motion and collision constraints. Independent checks use simulation state and episode records to assess outcomes and task requirements, with stronger checks of geometry, coverage, or placement. It comprises 250 manually validated tasks across 11 types in five groups and 27 indoor environments, covering object and room search, counting, geometric judgments, direction reasoning, and relocation. Human evaluators achieve 84% strict task success on 100 sampled tasks, with every correct outcome satisfying the required checks. Across seven frontier vision-language models, we identify two complementary failure modes: correct outcomes with unmet task requirements, and incorrect outcomes despite passing stronger checks. Oracle-input diagnostics show that more complete target observations and calibrated feedback improve final spatial judgments.

items.title: iWAM: Efficient Action Prediction from World Models without Explicit Future Prediction
items.summary: World-action models (WAMs) build policies on pretrained video-generation models, on the premise that predicting how a scene evolves helps determine how to act. However, generating future scenes is expensive for real-time control. This motivates efficient proxies for future imagination, but how to train such proxies without sacrificing action-prediction quality remains unclear. An effective proxy need not generate a high-resolution frame; it only needs to provide enough information to distinguish between possible futures. This leads to the design principle behind iWAM: rather than denoising an entire future frame, can we condition the action policy on intermediate features from a single video-model evaluation? We show that the answer is yes. Exploiting the reversible dynamics of flow-matching models, we invert each training future into the corresponding latent noise vector. However, a single velocity evaluation at this latent does not necessarily yield informative features for action prediction. We therefore learn a bidirectional flow map that amortizes future-generation computation, enabling a single model evaluation to provide effective conditioning features. At inference, we sample a latent noise vector from the prior and condition the policy using just one video-backbone forward pass. Across simulated benchmarks and real robots, iWAM recovers the generalization benefits of WAMs while substantially reducing its inference cost.

items.title: On Euclidean Diameter in Dynamic Streams
items.summary: We give a streaming algorithm for maintaining the diameter of a high-dimensional Euclidean point set under arbitrary insertions and deletions that achieves update time polylogarithmic in the number of points and polynomial in the dimension. For every fixed $c>\sqrt3$, there is an $ε_c > 0$ such that our one-pass algorithm uses $\tilde O(N^{1-ε_c}\poly(d))$ space, has worst-case update time $\poly(d,\log N)$, and maintains a factor-$c$ pair witness. On the hardness side, we prove that every constant-factor approximation requires polynomial memory even on short dynamic streams: a factor-$c$ approximation needs $N^{Ω(1/(c^2\log(c+1)))}$ space on streams of at most $2N-1$ updates. Our upper bound combines a geometric hull, Gaussian hashing through successively smaller caps, and local and global rebuilding schedules. Every update changes only one leaf of the hash hierarchy, while the answer is maintained through small variance certificates. The lower bound is based on a communication complexity argument. Together, these results separate the polynomial memory regime from the time needed to process an update.

items.title: Physicl Scenes: An Artist-created 3D Dataset for Learning Perception and Action
items.summary: We present Physicl Scenes, a high-quality artist-created and curated dataset of 6,499 3D scenes spanning household rooms, public interiors, and outdoor spaces. The dataset combines detailed geometry, physically based materials, and carefully composed environments with object- and part-level semantic annotations, providing rich, joint supervision for visual and embodied learning. We demonstrate its value as training data across inverse rendering, 3D reconstruction, scene understanding, and mobile manipulation. Across these tasks, training state-of-the-art methods with our scenes improves performance over alternative synthetic datasets. In addition, we introduce a mobile manipulation benchmark, evaluating vision-language-action models performing physical pick and place in diverse 3D scenes with realistic layouts, and using our part annotations to also score where each object is grasped. Our dataset will be released publicly to facilitate research in visual and embodied AI.

items.title: BriConstrain: Geometrically Constrained Decoding for Autoregressive Brick Assembly Generation
items.summary: Language models can generate LEGO$^\circledR$ assemblies from text, but their builds often contain parts that collide or attach to nothing. The usual approach of rejecting and resampling invalid placements discards decoded tokens without guaranteeing a valid build. We present BriConstrain, a constrained decoding method that restricts a pretrained language model's next-token probabilities before sampling, steering it towards valid placements. Because the validity of a brick placement depends on the non-predetermined build state, it cannot be compiled into a fixed grammar and must be checked dynamically. However, checking the validity of a brick before sampling is challenging as the space of valid placements is combinatorially large and cannot be enumerated exhaustively. Our key idea is to narrow the search space by constraining how parts attach rather than which parts attach to each other. Concretely, given the model's predictions of the currently placed part, and the previously placed parent it wants to connect to, we constrain the model's choice of how they attach. This allows us to span the space of part attachments, using a precomputed geometric oracle, and to effectively filter out colliding options. With valid attachment candidates in hand, we bias the model's next-token distribution towards the remaining valid candidates. We evaluate our method on two LEGO$^\circledR$ formats and models: BrickNet, which annotates connectivity explicitly, and our proposed Implicit Connectivity LDraw Format (ICLF), which uses numeric values for placements and leaves connectivity implicit. Our method raises collision-free builds from 31% to 91% on BrickNet and from 15% to 65% on ICLF, and outperforms rejection sampling on both formats at about 60% of its decoding cost.

items.title: A Bias in Disguise: Tiny Gradient Edits Stop a Small Language Model's Thinking Loops and Complement a Frontier Model's Weight Edit
items.summary: Qwen3.5-0.8B rarely finishes reasoning in thinking mode: at a 4,096-token budget only 1 or 2 of 500 MATH-500 answers close their think block (two seeds), and accuracy is 15.4%. A recent demonstration had GPT-6 Astra edit 131,072 of the model's weights without gradients and reported MATH-500 rising from 7.9% to 48.1% at a 32,768-token budget. We provide the missing gradient baseline, then combine the two edits. Fine-tuning only the 140 to 139,750 weights with the largest gradient, on the model's own correct answers to MATH training problems, raises thinking-mode MATH-500 at 4k tokens to 39.0-45.5% after 2-9 minutes of training on one GPU; 50 training examples suffice, and 1,398 random positions give only 16.3%. The gradient concentrates the edit on the most nearly constant channel of each of the first three layers. Because the model has no bias terms, an edit confined to those channels acts as a constant vector added to the residual stream: adding three fixed vectors to the unedited model matches the accuracy of such an edit. Under the Astra protocol (32k tokens, presence penalty 1.5), the Astra edit scores 52.1% (finished and correct) in our reproduction and our full-strength edits reach 45.6-45.7%, but ours win at every budget up to 16k tokens (39.5% against 6.7% at 4k). The two edits are complementary. The Astra edit plus our 139,750-weight edit at half strength scores 62.2% at 32k, 10 points above the Astra edit alone (p = 3e-9), with half as many tokens; our half-strength edit alone scores 46.7%.

items.title: Exploratory Midtraining for Robot Policies
items.summary: Robot policies predominantly learn from human-collected data emphasizing competent behavior, limiting coverage of the low-level behaviors needed to support autonomous improvement. We study how a form of midtraining can be used to build coverage over diverse low-level behaviors that connect challenging states of the robot and its environment to states from which further progress is possible ("connected behavioral coverage"). We also examine how this coverage supports downstream adaptation and online improvement. To this end, we introduce $β$-Data, a dataset collected via adversarial teleoperation, where a human adversary reversibly perturbs the environment while a human operator continues toward completion without resetting. We relabel trajectory segments with local outcomes in natural language and finetune a pretrained policy conditioned on recent action history. The resulting policy exhibits sustained use of more low-level behaviors. Across manipulation tasks in simulation and on three real-robot platforms, our approach yields more favorable data scaling laws, better zero-shot generalization, and more effective use of additional rollout time than training on standard demonstrations. During online finetuning, these policies need fewer rollouts to collect successful experience and reach higher success rates, suggesting that midtraining can prepare robots for both more robust task execution and continued autonomous improvement. Our project page and robot videos are available at https://kshitiz-1225.github.io/exploratory-midtraining-robot-policies/.

items.title: A Koashi--Imoto Criterion for Holevo-Rate Visible Compression
items.summary: For a finite memoryless quantum source whose encoder knows the sequence of classical labels, we determine when the Holevo rate is achievable with shared classical randomness and no shared entanglement. In the maximal Koashi--Imoto decomposition of the signal ensemble, this occurs exactly when each signal is pure on the quantum part of every sector it occupies. For qubits, this means that the signals are all pure or commute pairwise. If any occupied quantum part is mixed, every code with sufficiently small mean local error has rate bounded away from the Holevo information, uniformly in blocklength. To prove the converse, we apply Fawzi--Renner recovery to a hypothetical sequence of visible codes approaching the Holevo rate at vanishing local error, then invoke a decoupling bound of Baghali Khanian and Winter for blind compression.

items.title: Classical algorithms for sparse random Hamiltonians via free probability
items.summary: The search for quantum advantage in average-case problems is a pressing open question in physics and computer science. The widest conjectured example of such an advantage is in simulation of quantum many-body systems, where sign problems and entanglement growth cause the breakdown of many classical methods. Nonetheless, theoretical evidence for or against such an advantage remains scarce. Here, we investigate this in sparse random non-local Hamiltonians. We design a classical algorithm for such Hamiltonians that enables accurate computation of spectral fluctuations, thermal values, and time-ordered and out-of-time-order correlation functions. For any subexponential precision $\varepsilon$, our algorithm runs in time $(1/\varepsilon)^{2+o(1)}$, nearly identical to a quantum simulation. Crucially, this applies even at late evolution times, low temperatures, and near critical points, where existing classical methods require exponential time. Rather than directly simulating a quantum state or operator, our algorithm first computes the model's mean behavior and then a short hierarchy of instance-dependent corrections. These corrections predict long-time behavior based on short-time data using free probability theory.

items.title: Multimodal Masked Diffusion Autoencoder for Modeling Impaired Driving
items.summary: Human cognitive state (e.g., distraction, stress), gaze, and behavior interact with the driving environment in subtle ways that AI could use to assist drivers, but ground-truth labels for human cognitive state levels are costly to obtain at scale. We propose a multimodal masked-diffusion autoencoder, ID-MAE, that adds a self-supervised objective to impairment prediction: alongside predicting the impairment label as a masked token, it reconstructs masked gaze and trajectory. To probe the effects of different modalities and types of impairments on model inference, we introduce DIVERT, a driving-simulator dataset containing 103 hours of driving data (n = 109) with ten impairment inductions spanning cognitive, visual, and emotional states, recorded with gaze, vehicle state, and scene video. We demonstrate how ID-MAE affords significant improvements in impairment inference results on both the DIVERT dataset and existing datasets, and enables strong results in additional tasks, such as trajectory and gaze prediction. For location-matched pairs, our model achieves a paired AUC of 0.706 for impairment detection on DIVERT, compared to 0.590 without reconstruction loss, improving over existing baselines. We probe the design space in terms of input modalities, masking scheme, positional encoding, attention mechanism, and decoding. We also investigate the interaction between various impairments in training and inference, demonstrating that visually demanding distractions are separable from cognitive distractions. We plan to publicly release the code and data.

items.title: A note on input-oblivious unambiguous hierarchies
items.summary: Unambiguous hierarchies are defined similarly to the polynomial hierarchy; however, all witnesses must be unique. Their versions differ in the mode of using oracles. We consider input-oblivious unambiguous hierarchies built from the class OUP, in which all positive inputs of the same length have the same unique witness: the hierarchy OUH with language oracles and the hierarchy OUH$_\bullet$ with loose access to promise oracles, which is the input-oblivious version of the loose unambiguous hierarchy of Hirsch and Sokolov (IPL, 2015). We show that languages in OUH$_\bullet$ can be decided in deterministic polynomial time with an ONP oracle, and for languages in OUH oracle queries can be made nonadaptive. Moreover, languages in OUH can be decided in deterministic polynomial time with a tally NP oracle, and languages in OUH$_{\bullet}$ can be decided in P/OptP, that is, a subclass of P/poly where the advice is generated by a function that maximizes outputs of a nondeterministic machine on a unary input. We show that P/OptP can be characterized in terms of OGTD and OUGTD generator--tester--decoder classes recently considered by Hirsch and Volkovich (arXiv:cs.CC/2611.16096) and, in particular, is contained in their "ultimate" Karp--Lipton collapse class OUM. We also observe several other facts related to OUP: (1) the hierarchy defined by input-oblivious unambiguous dot-operators collapses, (2) in OUP computations, a single loose query to prOUP can be replaced by a query to OUP, (3) SOUP=OUP$\cap$coOUP, where SOUP is the same-witness class recently considered by Hirsch, Volkovich, and Williams (2026).

items.title: SAG-Mem-1.0 Technical Report
items.summary: Long-term conversational memory requires retrieving complementary facts scattered across dialogue sessions, including intermediate evidence with limited similarity to the original question. Existing approaches often rely on derived memory representations or persistent relational structures, introducing construction costs and potentially losing source details. We present SAG-Mem, a conversational memory framework that preserves complete dialogue messages in non-overlapping chunks and discovers complementary evidence through query-time lexical expansion. Memory construction requires no model inference, using a lexical index without LLM-based extraction, summarization, or semantic relation construction. At query time, BM25 retrieves initial candidates, an evidence evaluator identifies useful chunks, and lexical cues from selected evidence guide an additional retrieval round. Retrieved dialogue is further annotated with calendar interpretations of supported relative-time expressions, preserving the original wording and temporal granularity. We also introduce SAG-Mem-Lite, an alternative configuration that replaces evidence scoring with embedding-based candidate scoring, achieving lower operational cost than Full Context and all memory-based baselines across both benchmarks with low query latency. On LoCoMo and LongMemEval, SAG-Mem achieves overall scores of 83.08 and 80.20, respectively, the highest among the evaluated methods on both benchmarks. On LongMemEval, it exceeds the strongest compared baseline by 7.20 points. SAG-Mem-Lite achieves scores of 77.09 and 77.20, respectively. These results support dialogue preservation and evidence-guided retrieval expansion as an effective design for long-term conversational memory.

items.title: Token Pruning Needs a Protected Sink Token: Coherent Spatial Aggregation in Vision Transformers
items.summary: Vision Transformers (ViTs) are a predominant architecture for computer vision, with token reduction emerging as a popular paradigm to improve their efficiency. Prior work compares reduction algorithms, but not how models respond to them, nor how their response changes with model depth. We propose Monte Carlo Token Pruning (MCTP), which estimates each token's impact on the prediction when tokens are explicitly removed during the forward pass. Applying MCTP to recent pretrained models, we observe that most, such as DINOv3, maintain a similar ranking of token importance at every depth (high Coherent Aggregation), while SigLIP 2 does not. This coherence requires predictions to survive pruning, which depends on keeping high-norm "sink" tokens: prefix tokens are kept by design, while prefix-free SigLIP 2 forms them on patch tokens, which pruning may remove. We show that in removing DINOv3's prefix tokens, its predictions and coherence collapse, while protecting only 5 tokens for SigLIP 2 cuts the token impact outside the object's bounding box by up to 62%. Beyond this, MCTP offers a post-hoc method to evaluate how a pretrained ViT responds to pruning, and suggests that token reduction methods should keep "sinks".

items.title: MetaFORGE: A Meta-Learning Framework for Harness Optimization in Automated Code Generation for Parallel Computing
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) can generate parallel programs, but their correctness and performance depend strongly on the instructions that guide generation. We present \textsc{MetaFORGE}, an execution-grounded meta-learning framework that iteratively optimizes persistent natural-language skill specifications for MPI C code generation. \textsc{MetaFORGE} combines correctness testing, compiler diagnostics, static-analysis findings, runtime measurements, and rank-level load-imbalance profiles into a scalar reward that drives textual-gradient refinement, while an external memory distills and retrieves reward-supported optimization knowledge across runs. Across six MPI tasks and three workload sizes, \textsc{MetaFORGE} improves static-analysis quality, runtime, and load balance relative to zero-shot generation and generally exceeds the evaluated \textsc{TextGrad} iterative baseline. A model-matched refinement ablation shows that the MetaFORGE advantage persists when its refinement model is reduced to \texttt{gpt-4o}. An expanded retrieval ablation across all 18 task--workload configurations shows consistent runtime benefit and broad static-analysis and load-balance benefit from retrieved context. Leakage-controlled held-out and zero-update experiments further provide evidence that optimization knowledge persists in both the transferred skill and external memory under the evaluated protocol.

items.title: Neural Implicit Representation for Bathymetry Estimation using Sidescan Sonar Imagery
items.summary: Bathymetry measurement and estimation is critical for understanding the structure of underwater environments. While multibeam echosounders (MBES) provide accurate depth measurements, their deployment on surface vessels limits spatial resolution in deep water. Sidescan sonar (SSS), in contrast, can be deployed on autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) to operate closer to the seafloor, enabling high-resolution acoustic imaging. However, the inherent ambiguity in measurements and the limited observation coverage of sonar datasets degrade the performance of state-of-the-art methods for underwater bathymetry estimation from SSS. In this paper, we propose a differentiable neural rendering framework for SSS that enables effective estimation of bathymetry from SSS measurements. Our approach incorporates a measurement model based on SSS geometry, explicitly accounting for its wide elevation aperture and associated ambiguities. We evaluate our method on both synthetic and real-world datasets, demonstrating improved robustness and accuracy compared to alternative approaches.

items.title: Read My Lips: Context-aware Lip Reading Using Language and Audio-Visual Models
items.summary: Real-world speech is often partially observable: audio may be missing or corrupted by noise and competing speakers, while the speaker's lips remain visible. Recovering speech requires combining what can be heard, seen, and inferred from context. We introduce RML (Read My Lips), a collaborative method combining a lip reader, a language model, and an audio-visual generative model. The lip reader provides articulation hypotheses, the language model uses context to resolve ambiguous or missing words, and the audio-visual generator reconstructs synchronized speech while preserving speaker identity. Since source reliability varies, RML generates multiple reconstructions and uses the available evidence to favor the most reliable ones. This allows RML to handle missing audio, strong interference, and poor visual evidence without manually defined thresholds. Quantitative and qualitative experiments across these conditions show the benefit of combining visual, acoustic, and linguistic signals.

items.title: Lyris: Layout-Guided Long Video Generation with Persistent 3D Memory
items.summary: Exploring a scene from as little as a single photo requires generating a long, camera-controlled walkthrough that extends far beyond what was captured, yet remains consistent upon return. Memory-based video generation methods preserve what they have already seen, but have no anchor beyond it, where the camera drifts from its path and a text prompt can name objects but not place them. Layout-conditioned methods provide such an anchor and precise control over what appears where, but rely on layouts that are typically authored by hand. Both limitations arise because, beyond what was captured, nothing anchors the video model unless a human authors one. To overcome both, we propose Lyris, a long video generation framework that never leaves the video model without an anchor: a persistent point-cloud memory where the scene has been observed or generated, and a 3D layout that a vision-language model authors where it has not. Our key insight is that the interface between the two models can be surprisingly coarse. A layout of one labeled 3D box per object is simple enough for a vision-language model to author (and for a user to edit), yet expressive enough for a video model to follow once rendered along the camera path. We demonstrate walkthroughs of over three minutes and 50 meters from a single photo, passing through doorways into rooms it never shows. When evaluated on minute-long round trips across four datasets, Lyris outperforms state-of-the-art methods by a wide margin, reducing camera error by 3.8x and improving consistency upon return by 22% on average.

items.title: Generative Modeling via Drifting
items.summary: Generative modeling can be formulated as learning a mapping f such that its pushforward distribution matches the data distribution. The pushforward behavior can be carried out iteratively at inference time, e.g., in diffusion/flow-based models. In this paper, we propose Drifting Models, a new generative modeling paradigm that evolves the pushforward distribution during training and naturally admits one-step inference. We introduce a drifting field that governs the sample movement and achieves equilibrium when the distributions match. This leads to a training objective that allows the neural network optimizer to evolve the distribution. In experiments, our one-step generator achieves state-of-the-art one-step results on ImageNet 256x256, with FID 1.54 in latent space and 1.61 in pixel space. We hope that our work opens up new opportunities for high-quality one-step generation.

items.title: Draft Calibration for Speculative Decoding: Accelerating LLM Serving by Matching Draft and Target Distributions
items.summary: Speculative decoding accelerates large language model (LLM) inference by employing a lightweight draft model to propose draft tokens and allowing the target model to verify the new tokens in parallel to improve inference-time compute utilization. The speedup relies on the acceptance probability of draft tokens in target verification, which is directly related to the gap $\|p-q\|_1$ between the target distribution $p$ and the draft distribution $q$. In this paper, we study draft calibration of speculative decoding to improve the speedup of speculative decoding, where we employ post-hoc methods to calibrate the draft distribution to mitigate the distribution gap. We observe that though current community open-source draft models may learn the top candidate token correctly, they are generally underconfident compared to the target model, suggesting a consistent distribution mismatch. To mitigate the effect of this mismatch on the acceptance rate of the draft models, we try various post-hoc calibration methods, including standard temperature scaling and token-wise calibration. Our results suggest that a standard temperature scaling applied to the draft distribution improves the acceptance length by up to approximately 10\% with almost no additional cost across different tasks. Throughput analysis further verifies that this improvement in serving efficiency. Analysis of more general calibration methods reveals further potential room for improvement.

items.title: Visual Similarity in Adult Word Extension and Artificial Word Learning
items.summary: When two objects share a name, how much does their visual similarity explain, and what do the teaching examples add? We studied word extension across ten visual representations: eight trained encoders, a randomly initialized network, and raw pixels. Reanalyzing trial-level data from a large adult word-extension study (Lewis & Frank, 2018; 520 people), we computed each test image's distance to the teaching examples. Within the taught domain, greater distance was associated with less extension for all eight trained encoders and for the untrained network, so the association cannot be attributed only to what the encoders learned; raw pixels showed no negative association. In post hoc models that let the distance slope vary across images, seven of the eight trained encoders retained a negative estimate and five had 95% intervals entirely below zero; the interval of the reference encoder included zero. Whether trial order changes the distance slope, the frozen primary question, remained inconclusive. Example composition changed extension at comparable distances: after three examples, adults extended a word to 1.1% of superordinate items when the examples were subordinate and to 77.5% when they were superordinate.
