Digital twins address this computational bottleneck by emulating the behavior of a physical system and enabling fast prediction in place of expensive high-fidelity simulation. However,data-driven digital twins are non-adaptive and fail to generalize once the DC configuration changes. To address this limitation, this paper proposes an adaptive EMT-level digital twin for DCs based on in-context learning (ICL) with large language models (LLMs). We formulate the EMT prediction task as a system identification problem under parametric uncertainty and develop a GPT-2-based framework that adapts to unseen DC configurations at inference time from a small set of EMT trajectory samples, without model retraining. The proposed framework is validated on three representative EMT scenarios and benchmarked against three baseline non-adaptive twins. Results demonstrate superior prediction accuracy, improved adaptability to unseen operating conditions, and substantial computational speedups compared to high-fidelity EMT simulation.

items.title: Sequential Strategic Classification with Multi-Stage Selective Classifiers
items.summary: Strategic classification studies the problem where self-interested individuals or agents manipulate their response to obtain favorable decision outcomes made by classifiers, typically turning to dishonest actions when they are less costly than genuine efforts. Prior works have demonstrated a fundamental inability to get out of this conundrum by only focusing on the design of a classifier. We note that prior work also heavily focuses on either one-shot settings or repeated interaction with the same classifier. Real-world decision making is often multi-stage, involving a sequence of potentially different classifiers as an agent progresses. This paper introduces a sequential, stochastic, multi-stage model of strategic classification, by capturing how agents adapt their behavior, through improvement actions (enhancing both observable features and true attributes) and gaming actions (enhancing only observable features), over multiple levels of classification with increasing difficulty as well as reward. For each level, we adopt a selective classifier that can abstain from making a prediction at low confidence. Consequently, a positive (resp. negative) outcome leads to promotion (resp. demotion) of the agent to the next higher (resp. lower) level, while abstention keeps the agent at the same level. We fully characterize the agent's optimal instantaneous action under selective classifiers and compare the long-term properties and utility of the agent repeatedly following an optimal myopic policy of either no-improvement (never choose the improvement action) or no-gaming (never choose the gaming action). We further examine design principles over the sequence of classifiers that yield higher long-term utility for the latter policy, thereby effectively incentivizing genuine effort in the long run.

items.title: Scaling Chance-Constrained Correlated Equilibrium Computation for Exclusive Resource-Assignment Games
items.summary: The chance-constrained correlated equilibrium concept provides a robust coordination technique for self-interested agents whose costs are uncertain to a central coordinator, but the number of joint actions considered in its computation grows exponentially with the number of agents. We develop a reduced-rank formulation based on convex combinations of chance-constrained pure Nash equilibria to improve scalability. To further reduce computation, we propose an exact-one resource-assignment restriction for games in which agents compete for shared resources and simultaneous use of a resource is undesirable or unsafe. The restriction allows each resource to be assigned to exactly one agent, reducing the number of joint actions considered from O(2^(nr)) to O(n^r) for n agents and r resources. The resulting problem is solved over the restricted joint action set while retaining all incentive constraints associated with unilateral deviations. We show that the feasible set of the restricted problem is exactly the convex hull of the chance-constrained pure Nash equilibria contained in the exact-one assignment set, yielding a necessary and sufficient condition for nonemptiness. We further derive a sufficient condition under which all chance-constrained pure Nash equilibria of the unrestricted game are retained by the restriction. Numerical experiments in a vertiport departure-corridor coordination scenario demonstrate a 99.81% reduction in median computation time relative to the unrestricted formulation while achieving equivalent coordination performance.

items.title: Linguistic and Argument Diversity in Synthetic Data for Function-Calling Agents
items.summary: The construction of function calling agents has emerged as a promising avenue for extending model capabilities. A major challenge for this task is obtaining high quality diverse data for training. Prior work emphasizes diversity in functions, invocation patterns, and interaction turns, yet linguistic diversity of requests and coverage of arguments (e.g., \texttt{city\_name}, \texttt{stock\_ticker}) remain underexplored. We propose a method that generates synthetic datasets via optimizing general-purpose diversity metrics across both queries and arguments, without relying on hand-crafted rules or taxonomies, making it robust to different usecases. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our technique via both intrinsic and extrinsic testing, comparing it to SoTA data generation methods. We show a superiority over baselines in terms of diversity, while keeping comparable correctness. Additionally, when used as a training set, the model resulting from our dataset exhibits superior performance compared to analogous models based on the baseline data generation methods in out-of-distribution performance. In particular, we achieve an $7.4\%$ increase in accuracy on the BFCL benchmark compared to similar counterparts.

items.title: Scalable Placement for Disaggregated LLM Serving on Heterogeneous Edge Fleets
items.summary: Serving large language models (LLMs) at the edge is increasingly desirable for privacy-sensitive applications and scenarios that require data to remain on local devices. However, edge environments are constrained by limited computational resources and exhibit substantial device heterogeneity, making efficient LLM serving challenging. These limitations become particularly pronounced under bursty demand, where congestion and queue buildup can significantly increase response latency. Replicating the model into multiple pipeline instances can improve serving capacity and reduce congestion. Yet, deciding how devices should be grouped into replicas, assigning replicas to prefill or decode functions, and partitioning model layers across heterogeneous devices jointly creates a large combinatorial optimization problem. We present Spade, a scalable and runtime-efficient placement planner for disaggregated LLM serving with pipeline replication across heterogeneous edge clusters. Spade introduces a dominance-based pruning technique that discards inferior replica candidates and recursively eliminates larger candidates that contain them, dramatically shrinking the search space. It further combines a water-filling approach for layer partitioning with a bounded multidimensional knapsack formulation that optimizes placement under a congestion-aware objective. On a synthetic fleet of 30 devices spanning five hardware classes, Spade finds the optimal placement in 441ms. In contrast, a genetic-search baseline augmented with dynamic-programming partitioning requires approximately two hours and still produces solutions with a 19.7% worse congestion objective. When evaluated on fleets containing ten device types, Spade's pruning strategy eliminates 99.6% of candidate placements while yielding the same surviving candidate set as exhaustive enumeration.

items.title: Reinforcing Diffusion Models by Instantaneous Trajectory Distribution Matching
items.summary: Forward diffusion reinforcement learning (RL)---enabling deterministic ODE sampling without trajectory backpropagation---has grown increasingly popular for efficiently aligning diffusion models. However, we reveal that existing methods essentially rely on signed reward-weighted regression (RWR), regressing the trainable policy velocity onto rollouts from a behavior distribution. Unbiased baseline subtraction implicitly assumes that the policy velocity equals the behavior marginal velocity---an idealized assumption violated under classifier-free guidance (CFG) rollouts, offline/off-policy updates, and imperfect online self-consistency. This behavior--policy mismatch breaks baseline invariance and injects baseline-induced gradient drift, destabilizing training. To resolve this issue, we propose Instantaneous Trajectory Distribution Matching (iTDM), taking the infinitesimal limit of Trajectory Distribution Matching toward a time-local reward-guided target via the posterior-score identity to yield a sample-level gradient anchored at the behavior velocity without learning an additional reward-tilted target score. Tracking this velocity with an online auxiliary denoiser guarantees exact baseline invariance at the auxiliary optimum, effectively suppressing baseline drift across both online and offline RL. Extensive experiments across compositional generation, text rendering, and preference alignment show that iTDM achieves state-of-the-art in-domain and out-of-domain performance across group-wise online/offline RL and pairwise offline RL. Notably, on the challenging GenEval2 benchmark, iTDM converges nearly 3\times faster than competing methods while scaling smoothly to 0.87 without collapse. Furthermore, iTDM scales effectively to the 5.6B FLUX.3 model, achieving better performance across both in-domain and unseen metrics. Code is available at https://github.com/Luo-Yihong/iTDM

items.title: Simultaneously Boosting Efficiency and Capability for Linear Attention via Adaptive Channel Compression and Activation Purification
items.summary: Self-attention's quadratic complexity constitutes a core bottleneck for Vision Transformers (ViTs). Existing efficiency-oriented optimizations, including softmax-based and linear attention (LA) variants, generally compromise model representational capacity, leading to inevitable performance degradation. We propose a novel linear attention which alleviates this efficiency-capability dilemma. For the first time, we embed an Adaptive Channel Compression and Activation Purification (ACCAP) mechanism into the QKV projection of linear attention, which enables the model to retain high-dimensional feature information while performing computations with reduced channels. We further fuse a focused kernel function and a self-gating module into ACCAP to construct a lightweight linear attention module (ACCAP-LA). Our theoretical analysis shows that, compared to standard linear attention, ACCAP-LA reduces the attention module's parameter count by 79.17% and FLOPs by 77.5%. Extensive experiments demonstrate ACCAP-LA's effectiveness: when applied to ViT, it achieves 79.4% Top-1 accuracy on ImageNet-1K with only 5.8M parameters, and more notably, it boasts strong cross-architecture compatibility, boosting EfficientViT-b1 and PVT-T by 3.3% and 3.4% respectively.

items.title: MemHand: Memory-Enhanced World-Space Hand Motion Reconstruction from Egocentric Videos
items.summary: Recovering the continuous world-space motion of both hands from egocentric video is essential for applications such as human-to-robot policy transfer and augmented reality. Achieving this goes beyond reconstructing the hands from each individual frame, as the context that a frame needs is often spread over time, especially around occlusions or when a hand moves out of sight. Recent works have explored how to exploit temporal context, yet they mostly draw it from fixed-length windows. Such windows cannot guarantee that every frame has the context required to reconstruct the hands in world space with accurate poses and metric scale. To address this limitation, we introduce MemHand, a memory-enhanced framework for world-space hand motion reconstruction. MemHand maintains two complementary forms of memory. The Short-Term Event Memory keeps the context of the well-observed hand around each occlusion or out-of-sight event and supplies it to frames with weak or missing visual evidence. In addition, since the metric scale holds over the whole recording, the Long-Term Scale Memory retains the most reliable observations across the video as scale anchors within a bounded state. Across benchmarks featuring severe occlusions and frequent out-of-sight intervals, MemHand achieves state-of-the-art accuracy and generalizes well to unseen domains. Benefiting from the synergy of both memories, it cuts W-MPJPE by 57\% on ARCTIC and 70\% on HOT3D relative to StableHand, delivering continuous and metrically accurate world-space hand poses and trajectories. We will release our code and models at the project page: https://irmvlab.github.io/memhand.github.io

items.title: Red-Teaming Multi-Agent Attacks for Loss-of-Control Risks
items.summary: AI agents are growing more capable and persistent, and are being deployed in ever larger numbers. As more start collaborating, AI control measures must remain effective when they covertly collude on a harmful objective. We introduce MiniLab, a synthetic series of live services and codebases (5 interconnected services, 249 benign tasks, 8 attack objectives), adapted from internal AI deployment infrastructure. We demonstrate distributed attacks, in which different agents carry out separate attack fragments, and how their covertness evades frontier monitors when reading their trajectories individually. We show how distributed attacks spread across diverse contexts and harmful objectives through 16 human-optimized attacks (weight exfiltration, unmonitored rogue deployment, permission elevation, and more). A frontier monitor, GPT-5.6 Sol, reading each agent separately flags only 3.4% of successful distributed attacks, compared with 82.4% when a single agent carries out the same side task. Individual attacks can also be composed into longer attack sequences toward a greater loss-of-control outcome, without any individual agent being flagged. Finally, we tested whether models can plan these covert attacks: even with execution and monitor feedback, the best model-planned attacks succeed covertly under both their feedback monitor and GPT-5.6 Sol in at most 32% of executions, compared with 82% for human-crafted plans, though this may scale with model capabilities. By turning worst-case coordinated attacks into reproducible red-team cases, our work provides a foundation for preventing locally benign agent actions from accumulating into system-level loss of control.

items.title: MXFP4 for LLM Inference: Complementary Post-Training Quantization Techniques and Their Interactions
items.summary: Recent advances in low-precision representation have introduced several microscaling numerical formats for LLM quantization. By sharing a scale factor across groups of 16 or 32 elements, these formats enable aggressive low-precision quantization with minimal accuracy degradation, particularly when combined with modern PTQ algorithms. Their accuracy depends on how the numerical format interacts with rotation, PTQ, and scale selection. We study the composability of PTQ configurations across six LLMs and three microscaling formats: MXFP6, MXFP4, and NVFP4, systematically varying Hadamard rotation granularity, PTQ algorithm, and scale-selection strategy. Our central finding is that effective quantization recipes are format dependent: both MXFP4 and NVFP4 support accurate 4-bit inference, but techniques that benefit one do not necessarily transfer to the other. MXFP4 benefits substantially from rotation and error-correcting PTQ, whereas NVFP4 gains less from rotation, consistent with its finer-grained scales capturing more within-block variation. Building on these findings, we introduce Midmax, a calibration-free scale-selection strategy that mitigates clipping error in power-of-two block scales and improves accuracy across a majority of the evaluated MXFP4 configurations. We show that pairing MXFP6 activations with MXFP4 weights recovers most of the accuracy lost at 4-bit and, on Llama-3.1-8B, matches or exceeds our in-house BF16 baseline. An additional study finds that augmenting MXFP4 with a per-tensor macroscale, a mechanism intrinsic to NVFP4, does not improve average accuracy, suggesting that global rescaling alone does not address the limitations of E8M0 block scales for MXFP4 quantization. Together, these results provide practical guidance for combining numerical formats, rotation, PTQ, and scale selection for accurate low-precision LLM inference.

items.title: Coverage Guarantees for Pseudo-Calibrated Conformal Prediction under Distribution Shift
items.summary: Conformal prediction (CP) provides distribution-free marginal coverage under exchangeability, but coverage can fail under distribution shift. We study pseudo-calibration for unlabeled target data under bounded label-conditional feature shift. Using domain-adaptation tools, we derive target coverage lower bounds in terms of source classifier loss and Wasserstein shift. We also analyze fixed slack inflation of the pseudo-calibrated threshold and use this result to motivate a heuristic threshold adjustment. Finally, we propose source-tuned pseudo-calibration, which interpolates between hard pseudo-labels and randomized labels based on classifier uncertainty. Experiments on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100 show that the proposed method mitigates coverage degradation under shift, with larger expected set size.

items.title: AI, Bias, and Inclusion: A Two-Phase Mixed-Methods Study of Gender Bias, Awareness, and Trust in Artificial Intelligence
items.summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems are widespread across fields such as healthcare, finance, employment, and criminal justice, with a substantial impact on the lives of individuals and society. However, it has been established that AI systems perpetuate existing social inequalities, particularly through biases that are not easily discernible. Such biases are embedded in the technical and social structures of artificial intelligence systems, making them difficult to detect. These biases challenge the concept of Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion (EDI), which recognizes diversity as the acknowledgment of individual differences, equity as fairness and equal access, and inclusion as the value placed on all participants. This study argues that fairness in artificial intelligence systems cannot be achieved by focusing solely on their technical aspects, necessitating a holistic approach. This study employs a two-phase mixed-methods design. Phase 1 applies computational content analysis to 360 occupational narratives generated by ChatGPT across four countries (Canada, Germany, India, and Bangladesh) using gender-neutral prompts to examine whether professions are predominantly associated with one gender and whether these patterns remain consistent across regions. Phase 2 examines the extent to which students recognize potential bias in AI, their trust in AI for consequential decision-making, and how these perceptions relate to themes in EDI and AI ethics scholarship. By combining output-level bias analysis with user perception data, this study identifies the empirical foundations necessary for future EDI-AI co-design frameworks, outlining the sociotechnical dimensions that such frameworks must address to be effective.

items.title: Sound Distributed Runtime Verification under Incomplete Evidence
items.summary: Distributed runtime verification often requires combining evidence from several nodes to check properties that cannot be evaluated locally. However, when messages are delayed, lost, or deliberately suppressed, the verifier may not know whether a violation occurred or whether the relevant evidence is missing. This creates a risk of incorrectly reporting compliance. We study the requirements for sound monitoring under these conditions. We first show that a deadline-bounded monitor cannot be simultaneously sound, decisive, and available when an adversary can suppress evidence. The monitor must therefore be able to abstain. We then distinguish two sources of incomplete evidence. Sequence numbers and periodic reports can identify missing events, whereas detecting silent streams requires timing assumptions. We also examine how membership changes and coordinator failures affect verdict soundness and recovery. We implement these mechanisms in a three-tier monitoring architecture using MQTT and NATS JetStream. Experiments with an LLM-planned robot swarm demonstrate the failure modes, show how the proposed mechanisms prevent unsupported compliance verdicts, and measure their runtime and communication costs.

items.title: Weight Scale Rebalancing: Transferable Training Recipes for Transformers
items.summary: Training Transformers requires careful hyperparameter tuning, which becomes increasingly costly for large models. We introduce UDV-Rebalance (UDVR), a reparameterization that inserts an auxiliary diagonal matrix $D$ between naturally paired weight matrices $(U,V)$ appearing throughout Transformer architectures. UDVR periodically rebalances the factors to maintain unit-norm columns in $U$ and unit-norm rows in $V$, with $D$ absorbing the corresponding scales. With rebalancing, a single hyperparameter setting of UDVR remains effective across model scales, architectures, and data distributions. This yields a tuning-free rule that adapts to each weight matrix using only its dimensions. We fit this rule once on ViT models trained on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, and it remains valid when the activation function or the optimizer is changed. The same rule transfers to new image domains in DomainNet, to ViT, Swin, and MaxViT on ImageNet, and to language-model pretraining with up to 1.3B parameters. UDVR consistently outperforms Weight Normalization and $σ$Reparam and matches a vanilla baseline whose hyperparameters are swept on each target model.

items.title: Fresh Keys, Stale Secrets: Numeric Leakage across Linked LLM Prompts
items.summary: Small businesses repeatedly ask cloud language models about the same confidential prices, unit costs and margins. Numeric prompt disguises for such numbers are evaluated one prompt at a time, but a provider sees a firm's history, in which each fresh secret gives a new, independent view of the same numbers. Since real costs are not public, we measure on synthetic firms with known values how much an honest-but-curious provider recovers when it knows the disguise algorithm, holds sector-level price and margin statistics, and links a firm's queries. In one prompt, per-field scaling, a fixed-axis instantiation of Zhang et al.'s order-preserving substitution and Pr$\varepsilon\varepsilon$mpt's released sanitizer keep the attacker's margin-hit advantage over a prior-only guess between -0.6 and +4.4 percentage points. After 16 linked queries with fresh secrets, every disguise we test (Pr$\varepsilon\varepsilon$mpt at $\varepsilon\geq 0.5$) has a target recovered significantly more often: under the order-preserving substitution, margin recovery rises from 25.0% to 59.4%. The same attacker recovers 29.4 percentage points more margins with fresh maps than with one reused map. Theory explains the contrast: one reused secret bounds all queries by a single full-precision view of the fields shown, whereas fresh scaling keys are identifiable. Except for Pr$\varepsilon\varepsilon$mpt at $\varepsilon=0.5$, the gains persist when the attacker's prior comes from another population model and when values drift by up to 5% between queries; on our firms, whose prose cues are weak, reading the prose with a language model adds at most 2.5 points. Code and data: https://github.com/Jamli58/fresh-keys-stale-secrets

items.title: CityRecast: Suppressing Persistent Artifacts in Generative Satellite 3D Reconstruction
items.summary: Satellite-based 3D reconstruction is limited by sparse observations and changes across acquisition dates. Existing methods use generative priors to recover missing visual detail, but ghosting, streaking, and blur persist in their Gaussian scenes. These artifacts become particularly apparent in low-elevation renderings. We introduce CityRecast to suppress these artifacts through Gaussian scene repair and supervision calibration. To correct the Gaussian distributions that produce these artifacts, we first use multi-angle warm-up to constrain their spatial extent. This reduces the initial ghosting carried into progressive refinement. Surface-guided replacement then continues to repair the Gaussian distribution while preserving existing appearance. To provide more reliable supervision for this process, observation calibration mitigates interference from multi-temporal observations. Joint refinement further reduces conflicts among generated views. Experiments on DFC2019 and IARPA demonstrate reduced artifacts in low-elevation renderings while maintaining satellite-view fidelity. Compared with Skyfall-GS, CityRecast reduces FID-CLIP by 25.3% on DFC2019 and 51.8% on IARPA. MUSIQ increases by 14.54 and 24.95 points, respectively.

items.title: MSRGF: Multi-Source Reconstruction with Reference-Guided Fusion for Incomplete Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
items.summary: Incomplete multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) predicts sentiment from textual, acoustic, and visual features when some observations are missing. Existing reconstruction methods estimate missing features from available modalities and combine the resulting information for sentiment prediction. However, different available modalities can produce distinct estimates of the same modality, while direct fusion often leaves the relationships among these estimates underused. We propose MSRGF (Multi-Source Reconstruction with Reference-Guided Fusion), which retains separate estimates and exploits their relationships during fusion. Specifically, MSRGF comprises three components: (1) Source-Wise Reconstruction (SWR), which uses modality-specific queries and a shared generator to produce a separate estimate of each modality from every available modality; (2) Reference-Guided Fusion (RGF), which uses relationships among estimates and available observations to construct a weighted reference, selectively refines it using their differences, and incorporates observed features when available; and (3) Global Context Modulation (GCM), which uses global context to adjust modality summaries for sentiment prediction. Extensive experiments on three datasets show that MSRGF outperforms existing methods, achieving average accuracy improvements of 1.9% on MOSEI under random within-modality missingness, 0.6% under random whole-modality missingness and 1.3% under fixed whole-modality missingness.

items.title: Tabra Blends: Improving the Accuracy--Latency Trade-off with Complementary Tabular Models
items.summary: Tabular foundation models make different trade-offs between prediction accuracy and latency. We study whether a compact ensemble can deliver higher accuracy in less time. Across 816 TabArena splits, our blend of four-estimator Kumo and one LimiX pipeline reaches 2063.8 Elo, 45.4 points above the top published entry in the same fit. Its normalized fit + predict time is 15% lower than Kumo-16's and 98% lower than full LimiX's. We find that greater prediction diversity between the two models helps explain the reduction in error.

items.title: What Does a Skill Vocabulary Cost? A Closed-Loop Decomposition over Demonstrated Motions
items.summary: Discrete skill policies execute motions drawn from a finite vocabulary. In most current methods, this vocabulary is a latent codebook learned jointly with a selector and a decoder. When such a policy fails in closed loop, the failure cannot be traced to the vocabulary, to the choice of skill or to its execution. We present Movement Prototype Quantization (MPQ), which places a library of demonstrated motions after a trained policy instead of inside it. MPQ replaces each predicted action chunk with its nearest library element, corrects that element toward the prediction within a bound, and trains no parameters. Across six architectures, including a 7B vision-language-action model, the wrapped policy is statistically equivalent to the original. A reference policy executed through the library is therefore a baseline for any selector over the same library. Substituting a selector's components one at a time attributes its shortfall to them. On LIBERO-90, with selectors on three backbones, quantization costs nothing and the choice of skill costs at most 2 points under the reference's placement and correction. The selectors' own placement and correction account for nearly all of the remaining gap, up to 12 points. Offline reconstruction predicts none of these differences and misjudges library size, design and transfer across benchmark suites. Project page: https://intuitive-robots.github.io/mpq.

items.title: PEAR: Adaptive Advantage Reshaping for Perception and Exploration in Large Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Effective multimodal reasoning requires a model to reliably utilize visual information while sufficiently exploring diverse reasoning paths. To achieve this goal, prior work combines visual dependency and token entropy to reshape sequence-level advantages, but scaling the contribution of token entropy by visual dependency can leave high-entropy tokens with low visual dependency underweighted, despite their important role in reasoning exploration. To address this limitation, we propose PEAR, an adaptive advantage reshaping method for improving perception and exploration in multimodal reasoning. PEAR retains visual dependency as the base signal and adds an entropy-based exploration gain only at high-entropy positions, with lower visual dependency leading to a larger additional gain. The fused signal is then mapped to positive token-level weights that reshape the sequence-level advantage. Experiments on Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B show that PEAR achieves the highest average performance among evaluated baselines across multimodal reasoning benchmarks, alongside leading results on textual reasoning and general multimodal benchmarks.

items.title: Speculative Decoding for Semantic-ID-Based Generative Recommendations
items.summary: Generative recommender systems with Semantic IDs (SIDs) represent each item as a short sequence of $L$ discrete tokens and use a sequence model to predict the next item's tokens from a user's history. Industry-scale deployments typically use these models to retrieve multiple candidates per request with constrained beam search. However, this incurs a fixed cost of $L$ sequential model calls per request, and accuracy degrades as the SID generator becomes less sharp, without a guarantee on how close the output is to the exact top-$K$. Production systems therefore cannot detect degraded retrieval for individual requests. We propose SIDECAR, which uses approximate draft candidates and a tree-attention pass to score the entire draft in a single model call, memory permitting. This pass bounds the probability of every unexplored SID prefix and certifies the exact top-$K$ if the draft contains them. Otherwise, a branch-and-bound fallback expands only the parts of the trie that can still change the output, reaching certification within at most $L$ calls for any draft. Moreover, under a budget of $M$ tokens per call and $Y$ calls, which for $Y = L$ matches the resources of a beam search of width $M$, SIDECAR announces a factor $1 + δ$ within which its list will be exact at every rank. Depending on model sharpness, SIDECAR returns the exact top-$K$ using a fraction of beam search's calls or memory. Even when the budget is too small to recover the exact top-$K$, SIDECAR, unlike beam search, reports the announced factor, allowing the serving system to stop early once a quality target or latency limit is reached.

items.title: SignSeek: Learning Transferable Representations for Sign Dictionary Retrieval
items.summary: Sign language dictionaries are essential resources for sign language learners, yet automatically retrieving a sign from a dictionary, given only a query video, remains a challenging problem due to the natural variability between signers. Existing sign representation learning methods are built for closed-set recognition, producing embeddings that do not generalise to the open-set, signer-independent setting that retrieval demands. \textbf{SignSeek} closes this gap by contrastively learning sign representations with saliency-guided articulator masking. A contrastive objective aligns same-gloss signs across signers, while our Articulator Saliency-Guided Masking (ASGM) pinpoints the single most critical articulator per sign. This drives two complementary objectives, a masked contrastive alignment (MAC) loss that sees the sign through a single articulator and a masked prediction (MAP) loss that reconstructs it in latent space from the surrounding spatio-temporal context. Pretrained on 266K samples ($\sim$5,700 glosses) across multiple sign languages, \textbf{SignSeek} sets a new state-of-the-art performance in cross-corpus retrieval on ASL-Citizen, WLASL, and NMFs-CSL without any downstream fine-tuning. Strikingly, it achieves zero-shot generalisation to an entirely unseen British Sign Language (BSL), surpassing methods explicitly trained on BSL, and transfers seamlessly to isolated sign recognition and subtitle alignment, outperforming prior skeleton-based methods.

items.title: Leveraging Persistent Field-of-View and Multipath Segment Routing for Traffic Engineering in LEO Satellite Constellations
items.summary: The emergence of low earth orbit (LEO) satellite constellations poses fundamental challenges for traditional rout- ing paradigms due to high node mobility, frequent topology changes, and constrained on-board resources. This paper pro- poses a segment routing (SR) framework that offloads route computation and control signaling from resource-constrained LEO switches to more powerful medium earth orbit (MEO) con- trollers. We first establish sufficient conditions for the persistence of user-to-satellite and LEO-to-MEO field-of-view (FoV) con- nectivity throughout a virtual topology (VT) snapshot interval, enabling handover-free operation. Leveraging this persistence, we formulate the MEO control domain partitioning problem as a mixed-integer linear program (MILP) to minimize control over- head while assigning disjoint segment routing domains (SRDs) to MEO controllers. Within each SRD, we develop a multipath SR- based traffic engineering (SR-TE) formulation that splits traffic among four minimum-hop-count path types to minimize maxi- mum link utilization. We solve this linear program (LP) using a distributed primal-dual hybrid gradient (PDHG) approach that preserves SRD-level privacy and requires only AllReduce communication. Simulations on the Starlink/GPS combination demonstrate our approach reduces maximum link utilization by more than 13.09%, 11.84%, and 12.50%, respectively, com- pared to traditional minimum hop count routing (MHCR) and traffic-oblivious load-balancing methods for Starlink, Kuiper, and OneWeb.

items.title: Measurement Artifacts in Trustworthiness Evaluations of Quantized Small Language Models
items.summary: Evaluations of quantized language models attribute the change in a benchmark score to quantization. We write the measured change as the true change plus a term contributed by the instrument. Instrument error that is the same at every precision can shrink a paired comparison but cannot create or reverse an effect. Error that interacts with quantization can do both, and it is reported as an effect of quantization. We estimate this interaction for four measurement choices in 8 instruction-tuned models below two billion parameters, at float16, LLM.int8() and NF4, on identical items. Measured against labels from two human annotators, the 4-bit rise in harmful compliance is about half to two-thirds of the rise in non-refusal that a corrected key word detector records. Cloze and lettered multiple-choice scoring disagree about the effect of quantization far more than their noise allows: their estimates correlate at \r{ho} = 0.10, against a ceiling of about 0.77. LLM.int8() answers and generations depend on which items share a batch, and padding alone changes its answers. Rounding activations to 8 bits is enough to produce this dependence. NF4 is batch-invariant. The two largest reported calibration losses are response-bias shifts. We release item-level predictions, option scores and human annotations, and give recommendations for evaluating compressed small models.

items.title: DOPER: Deep Object Pose Estimation Revisited
items.summary: We present DOPER, an RGB pose estimation framework that shares a visual backbone across object detection, segmentation, and keypoint prediction to recover the 6D pose of known objects through Perspective-n-Point. Starting from synthetic training, DOPER adapts to real observations using partial supervision while retaining synthetic keypoint labels. Calibrated multi-view observations provide geometric constraints for keypoint supervision. During inference, optional heatmap refinement fits a rigid pose directly to the predicted keypoint distributions, resolving ambiguous correspondences without depth input or a learned pose refiner. Starting from underspecified CAD models, DOPER progressively refines the object representation and pose estimator. Results on SPEED+ and SHIRT further demonstrate effective adaptation to illumination changes and accurate temporal pose estimation. Across the evaluated single-view and multi-view configurations, DOPER achieves state-of-the-art detection AP results on HANDAL, HOPEv2, HOT3D, and T-LESS while using only RGB and running in real time (35 Hz per object model on one GB300). These results demonstrate the effectiveness of jointly learning detection and pose keypoints, with real observations and geometric constraints.

items.title: RoboValue: A Fine-Grained Sim-and-Real Benchmark for Unified Evaluation of Robotic Value Models
items.summary: Robotic value models assess task execution from visual observations and instructions, providing feedback on execution quality and progress toward the task goal. However, existing evaluations cover only selected aspects of execution understanding, leaving the reliability of value feedback insufficiently tested. We introduce RoboValue, a fine-grained sim-and-real benchmark for unified evaluation of robotic value models. Its framework evaluates four complementary capability dimensions through shared interfaces: task-state understanding, temporal progress monitoring, failure and recovery reasoning, and value consistency. Diagnostic trajectories and instruction variations test whether value judgments accurately reflect task requirements and changes throughout execution. RoboValue-Dataset covers 15 simulation and 20 real-world manipulation tasks, providing expert demonstrations for training and annotated trajectories for fine-grained evaluation. We evaluate representative robotic value models and general-purpose multimodal models in zero-shot and one-shot settings under standard conditions and separate shifts in robot embodiment and environment. Models trained to grade partial outcomes and individual task steps exhibit strong fine-grained grounding, while reasoning over observation histories supports tracking of accumulated task effects. Strong forward-progress and memory scores can nevertheless coexist with poor responses to task regression. Even models with strong grounding and progress estimates struggle to recognize effective recovery and to give consistent feedback within and across valid executions. These findings identify concrete targets for value supervision, while the dataset and public leaderboard support continued assessment of feedback reliability. The website is available at https://robovalue-benchmark.github.io/.

items.title: Field Life: Particle Life as Interacting Chemical Fields
items.summary: Field Life is a cellular automaton inspired by the interaction dynamics of Particle Life. In Particle Life, each particle has a colour, and an interaction matrix sets how strongly each colour attracts or repels each other colour. In Field Life, each colour is a channel of the automaton, and each cell holds a concentration of every colour. One step of the rule has three parts. Each colour is convolved with a ring-shaped kernel, which measures how much of that colour surrounds a cell. The interaction matrix combines these measurements into an attraction for each colour. The mass of each colour then moves toward higher attraction, in a way that conserves mass. A random matrix and a random initial state are usually enough to produce moving structure: bodies that glide, bodies that shed diffuse clouds, and gliders that break up into smaller gliders. We sample rules at random, keep the rules that move and form structure, and describe the patterns that appear: colours that sort into regions, colours that form stripes, and gliders, compact bodies that travel across the grid. The simulation and 120 saved rules, which we call worlds, are released.

items.title: Seeking the Unfamiliar but Memorable: Conceptual Creativity as Meta-Learning
items.summary: What does it mean to create a new concept, rather than retrieve a familiar one? Repeatedly sampling a generative model at the same prompt produces variations with similar styles and typical content. We propose that creativity is the production of stimuli that are unfamiliar to an adaptive observer at first sight, but quickly learnable from a few exposures. We formalize this as a Creator-Appraiser pair: a Creator generates a candidate, an Appraiser adapts to it for a few inner-loop learning steps, and the Appraiser's improvement becomes the reward the Creator optimizes through. We instantiate the framework with diffusion as the Creator, an autoencoder Appraiser on MNIST, and a CLIP Appraiser with a low-rank adapter for natural images. With a frozen diffusion model and no additional language conditioning, the meta-learning gradient is enough to produce both stylistic variations and concept compositions beyond what the base model can generate on its own.

items.title: Find the Fungible: Variable-Resolution Tokenization that Compacts Semantics with a Granularity Dial as a VLM "Catalyst"
items.summary: Efficient vision-language models should preserve a useful representation of the whole image, even under tight budgets. However, aggressive pruning or indiscriminate merging can erase critical details and disrupt the spatial structure. We thus propose Varest, which maximizes semantic fungibility: tokens describing coherent content can be summarized together with minimal information loss. Object boundaries distilled from a visual foundation model guide grouping, while text localization protects details needed for reading. At lower budgets, Varest merges the image into coarser semantic regions, while maintaining full spatial coverage. After early language decoder layers process this representation, a learned selector prunes visual tokens that later layers no longer need, reducing repeated access to already integrated information. Across three LLaVA backbones and 13 benchmarks, Varest outperforms 10 training-free and 5 trained baselines in mean performance retention at every evaluated budget, preserving 86.10-92.33% of uncompressed performance using only 5.56% of tokens. This SOTA performance further generalizes to modern VLMs like Qwen3.8-27B.

items.title: Quantization-Induced Performance Degradation in Segment Routing: A Concentration Inequality Analysis
items.summary: In segment routing (SR), splitting ratios must be quantized to respect practical hardware precision constraints. Yet no existing work has established an upper bound on the performance degradation caused by such quantization. In this work, we propose source-agnostic systematic rounding, which allows flows sharing a destination to share the same policy, thereby reducing memory consumption, and which approximates the target splitting ratios by a set of power-of-two terms so as to respect the hardware precision limit. We explicitly analyze the consequence of quantizing splitting ratios to integer multiples of 1/64 by a probability-theoretic argument based on concentration inequalities, and we derive an upper bound on the resulting performance degradation. We validate our analysis with extensive experiments on real-world network topologies and flow statistics.

items.title: CACO: Coverage-Aware Coordinated Optimization for Continuous Generative Retrieval
items.summary: Continuous generative retrievers powered by flow matching and diffusion sample multiple queries in item embedding space for approximate nearest-neighbor (ANN) search under fixed budgets. However, existing generative retrievers can suffer from retrieval overlap under uncoordinated sampling, whereas explicit diversity guidance to broaden the candidate set may induce relevance drift as it lacks direct feedback on the value of additional items. We introduce CACO (Coverage-Aware Coordinated Optimization), a self-supervised post-training framework coordinating queries from frozen flow-matching and diffusion retrievers toward complementary item coverage with negligible latency overhead. Using empirical retrieval frequencies across sampled reference queries as a relevance proxy, CACO formulates a label-free coverage objective that improves recall across all 30 backbone-dataset settings in offline experiments. To avoid the overhead of sampling reference queries at inference, CACO employs a coordinated query adjustment network combining inter-query bidirectional attention with gated relative directions, updating queries via bounded tangent-space projection and spherical retraction. During training, CACO applies tangential antithetic perturbations and counterfactual single-query replacement to measure each query's marginal gain, yielding an unbiased gradient estimator of smoothed set coverage across non-differentiable ANN search. On eight public benchmarks and an in-house 24-partition streaming industrial dataset, CACO improves Recall@100 and Recall@400 by up to 23.7% and 23.9% over the strongest baseline, cuts inter-query overlap by 53.3%-64.9%, and adds only 0.5%-3.0% inference latency.

items.title: Learning to Generate in the Right Order
items.summary: We introduce PONDER, a method that learns in which order an image generator should fill in content and which of its earlier predictions to revise. Masked generative models construct a sample by repeatedly filling in subsets of missing variables. The order of these partial predictions determines the context available in subsequent steps and therefore affects the quality of the final sample. Common strategies are to choose the order randomly or based on local confidence estimates. Conditioned on the partially generated sample and the generator's features, our policy chooses which positions to fill next and/or which previously filled positions to mask for later regeneration, a mechanism we call rethinking. In this way, the generation process is able to adapt to the evolving context and also to revise earlier predictions. We optimize the policy using group-relative policy gradients, with rewards that measure constraint satisfaction, human preference, or distribution quality. For the latter, we introduce FIDgrad, an image-level reward derived from the (first-order) change in Fréchet Inception Distance caused by adding a generated sample to the current feature distribution. With the generators frozen, learned ordering reduces MAR-B ImageNet FID from 4.09 to 2.78, improves MaskGen-KL-XL HPSv2 from 24.50 to 26.50, and raises the accuracy on hard visual Sudokus from 4.5% to 56.6%, surpassing uncertainty-based greedy ordering (41.0%). Rethinking further improves these results to 2.70 FID, 27.80 HPSv2 and 96.7% accuracy.

items.title: Communication Complexity of Disambiguations of Gap Hamming Distance
items.summary: We consider the Gap Hamming Distance problem in which Alice and Bob receive $n$-bit strings and must decide whether their Hamming distance is at most $n/3$ or at least $2n/3$. This promise problem has public-coin randomized communication complexity $O(1)$ since the players can estimate the Hamming distance by comparing their strings on a few shared random coordinates. The required output is undefined, or "ambiguous", on inputs with Hamming distance between $n/3$ and $2n/3$. We prove that any disambiguation of this problem to a total function has randomized communication complexity $Ω(n^{2/3})$. As a corollary, we obtain an $O(1)$ versus $Ω(n^{2/3})$ separation between randomized and pseudo-deterministic communication complexity. The proof was first found by an AI model and then reworked by the authors.

items.title: Self-Supervised Uncalibrated Multi-View Video Anonymization in the Operating Room
items.summary: Privacy preservation is a prerequisite for using video data in Operating Room (OR) research. Effective anonymization relies on the exhaustive localization of every individual; even a single missed detection necessitates extensive manual correction. However, existing approaches face two critical scalability bottlenecks: (1) they usually require manual annotations of each new clinical site for high accuracy; (2) while multi-camera setups have been widely adopted to address single-view ambiguity, camera calibration is typically required whenever cameras are repositioned. To address these problems, we propose a self-supervised multi-view video anonymization framework consisting of whole-body person detection and whole-body pose estimation, without annotation or camera calibration. Our core strategy is to enhance the single-view detector by "retrieving" false negatives using temporal and multi-view context, and conducting self-supervised domain adaptation. We first run an off-the-shelf whole-body person detector in each view with a low-score threshold to gather candidate detections. Then, we retrieve the low-score false negatives that exhibit consistency with the high-score detections via tracking and self-supervised uncalibrated multi-view association. These recovered detections serve as pseudo labels to iteratively fine-tune the whole-body detector. Finally, we apply whole-body pose estimation on each detected person, and fine-tune the pose model using its own high-score predictions. Experiments on the 4D-OR dataset of simulated surgeries and our dataset of real surgeries show the effectiveness of our approach achieving 99% and 97% recall, respectively. Moreover, we train a real-time whole-body detector using our pseudo labels, achieving comparable performance and highlighting our method's practical applicability. The code is available at https://github.com/CAMMA-public/OR_anonymization.

items.title: Aqua2CAD : Observation-Guided Point Cloud Correction and Completion for CAD Reconstruction from Underwater Stereo Images
items.summary: Recovering editable computer-aided design (CAD) models from underwater stereo images requires accurate and complete geometry, yet stereo reconstruction produces displaced points and missing regions. The original views retain cross-view disagreement and ray evidence lost during point-cloud fusion. Aqua2CAD exploits this evidence in two stages: view-conditioned correction and quality filtering establish reliable geometric support, while multi-view observations condition a learned shape prior to infer missing surfaces in the original metric frame. The recovered points support surface fitting and solid assembly with manually revised face groups. On an OceanSim-based synthetic benchmark, Aqua2CAD reduces point-cloud Chamfer distance by 60% relative to the stereo reconstruction. Compared with a matched point-only completion backbone, it improves missing-region recovery at 5,mm from 16.27% to 24.16%. With a shared CAD backend, exterior acceptance increases from 6/19 to 14/19. Qualitative results on selected real underwater captures demonstrate recovery of the main structures of six 3D-printed objects.

items.title: AeroLLE: Nighttime Aerial Image Enhancement with Generated Supervision
items.summary: Nighttime aerial image enhancement is constrained by the scarcity of aligned normal-light targets. Acquiring such targets from moving UAVs is difficult, and simple darkening of daytime images underrepresents the sensor noise, localized lighting, and uneven exposure of real nighttime captures. Generating normal-light references from real nighttime observations offers a practical way to fill this supervision gap. AeroNight pairs 1,200 real nighttime aerial RGB images with generated references selected through manual screening, preserving real imaging degradation in the inputs. This setting motivates AeroLLE, a lightweight two-stage framework whose context-aware Base Enhancer combines local processing with scene-level frequency information to recover visibility. Spatially Adaptive Exposure-Color Calibration (SAECC) then refines the base prediction through bounded low-resolution RGB gain and bias fields. AeroLLE achieves the highest PSNR and SSIM among the evaluated methods on both held-out test sets, reaching 17.62/17.89 dB PSNR and 0.5190/0.4964 SSIM on Test 1/Test 2, respectively. The model uses 255.24K parameters and 2.47G FLOPs, reducing FLOPs by 85.4\% relative to Multinex and improving PSNR by 1.56 dB on Test 2. AeroNight provides the first benchmark for pseudo-supervised nighttime aerial enhancement, and AeroLLE shows that generated references can support compact enhancement models.

items.title: Off-Policy RL with Online Inference Tuning: 1st Place Solution to the CoRL 2026 RoboEval Challenge
items.summary: The CoRL 2026 RoboEval challenge has eight bimanual tasks, and it ranks a policy not only on whether it succeeds but on how: every stage of the task, done safely, efficiently and with both arms in coordination, scored against human demonstrations. My solution has two parts. The generic part, carried over from my LeHome challenge solution, is off-policy RL on a $π_{0.5}$-based policy that is also its own value function. It is trained with AWR and RECAP on advantages of the exact official score, in a loop where every rollout is at the same time a Thompson-sampling trial of about 20 inference parameters. Out of the box, it took the policy to 0.85 RDS on held-out seeds in two days (and it was still very far from convergence). The competition-specific part adds data that local exploration cannot find: generated demonstrations that reach the full reward, and recovery episodes that start from the policy's own failures. The submitted policy reaches 0.990 RDS on my held-out seeds and 0.987 on the official seeds, and it won first place in the challenge, with 0.988 in the organisers' final evaluation on 1,000 unpublished seeds per task.

items.title: PtychoFM: A Foundation Model for Ptychographic Imaging
items.summary: Ptychography provides high-resolution lensless imaging across X-ray, electron, and optical microscopy, but reconstructing images from diffraction measurements generally requires computationally intensity iterative phase retrieval. These methods often require experiment-specific analysis, limiting real-time feedback as data acquisition rates increase. Here, we demonstrate PtychoFM, a physics-aware foundation model for ptychographic imaging that combines large-scale pre-training with experiment-specific fine-tuning to reconstruct complex object images directly from individual diffraction patterns. Trained using a differentiable forward model without object-space labels, PtychoFM transfers from step-scan training data on one sample to fly-scan measurements of other samples with different feature sizes, morphologies, and refraction indices. At a synchrotron beamline, diffraction frames were streamed from the detector to a single GPU for inference at up to 200 frames per second and returned for real-time visualization. PtychoFM provides a practical route to rapid, transferable ptychographic reconstruction and live experimental feedback under nonideal conditions.

items.title: Beyond Primitive Bloat: High-Fidelity Gaussian Splatting via Coordinate-Convolution Neural Network
items.summary: Gaussian Splatting (GS) has revolutionized Novel View Synthesis (NVS) with fast training and real-time rendering, yet pushing its fidelity to arbitrary high levels remains an open challenge. We theoretically explain this barrier by proving that discrete Gaussian representations require an exponentially increasing number of primitives to raise training PSNR, which inevitably triggers optimization issues and validation overfitting. To bypass this scaling limit without primitive bloat, we formulate detail recovery as a continuous neural field over coarse renderings and prove that monotonically reducing approximation risk to zero requires jointly leveraging low-fidelity signals, local neighborhood, and coordinate queries. Guided by this result, we augment splatted renderings with an existing Coordinate-Convolution Neural Network (CCNN) that jointly convolves rendered low-fidelity signals with 2D pixel coordinate queries to synthesize residuals. Integrating CCNN into five diverse Gaussian Splatting baselines establishes new state-of-the-art fidelity across NVS benchmarks while preserving real-time rendering speeds with minimal training and storage overhead. Beyond NVS, they also consistently boost performance of 1D/2D regression and 2D super-resolution tasks.

items.title: Normative and neural network models of multisensory integration
items.summary: Animals continuously detect scents, sights and sounds, which their brains combine into diverse multisensory streams. Multisensory integration accelerates learning, increases reaction speeds and helps to resolve sensory ambiguities. In studying this process, the field has developed a continuum of models; from concise mathematical equations, with a handful of variables, to artificial neural networks, with billions of parameters. In this review, we divide this spectrum into two classes: normative models start from a hypothesis about how multisensory signals should be integrated, while neural network models aim to emulate how circuits could integrate them. Together, these models demonstrate that observers can integrate cues in a statistically optimal fashion, and help to explain experimental findings, including the diversity of multisensory neuron response profiles and network architectures. In this review, we provide a didactic overview of multisensory models, complete with accessible equations and Python code, and compare their assumptions and explanatory power. We detail what has been learned from these models. Finally, we discuss how the ideas and insights from classical theoretical models can be reconciled with those from artificial neural networks, and how this convergence should shape future research.

items.title: PairAlign: A Framework for Autoregressive Tokenization via Self-Alignment with Applications to Audio Tokenization
items.summary: Modern learning systems represent perceptual signals with continuous vectors, but comparison, retrieval, memory, alignment, and reasoning are often symbolic. In language, tokens provide this interface; for speech and audio, it must be learned. Existing audio tokenizers rely on local quantization, clustering, or reconstruction, leaving sequence consistency, compactness, length, termination, and edit geometry only indirectly controlled. We introduce PairAlign, a framework for compact audio tokenization through autoregressive self-alignment. An encoder maps speech to a continuous condition, and an autoregressive decoder emits tokens from BOS to EOS. Given two content-preserving views, PairAlign derives a canonical anchor target and trains both views to predict it, with unrelated in-batch targets as competing sequences. It first learns an autoregressive bridge from VQ targets and then transitions to EMA-teacher self-alignment with grounding and anti-collapse controls. On 3 s speech, PairAlign produces shorter, non-degenerate sequences while retaining ordered paired-view consistency. On the TIMIT retrieval archive, it operates at 8.28 tokens/s, reducing archive token count by 70.65% and the edit-distance work proxy by 91.87% relative to Stage I. Positive-negative probes show strong separation across phone-disjoint, trigram-disjoint, and temporally rearranged negatives, while rate-controlled post-hoc BPE does not recover the same compactness-consistency operating point. These results expose a rate-granularity trade-off: PairAlign does not uniformly outperform denser tokenizers on every local metric, but provides a lower-rate symbolic interface preserving ordered and relational structure. Conceptually, PairAlign follows JEPA-style predictive learning by predicting an abstract target rather than reconstructing the input; here, the target is a learned variable-length symbolic sequence.

items.title: SAVERA: Bridging Frozen Vision and Language Models via Sparse Alignment and Visual Evidence Reuse
items.summary: Independently pretrained vision and language models may learn shared structures of the same underlying world, providing a foundation for combining them to build multimodal capabilities. However, a key challenge remains in aligning cross-modal feature representations while preserving access to visual information before and after language adaptation. To this end, we propose sparse alignment with visual evidence-guided residual adaptation (SAVERA), a framework that combines frozen vision and language models through bidirectional alignment in a shared sparse space and prompt-guided residual fusion. Specifically, we first present shared-space projection, activation reconstruction and encoding (SPARE), which represents original visual, adapted visual, and textual features through shared soft-gated sparse encoding, with branch-specific reconstruction to preserve their respective information. Second, we devise bridge--text embedding and activation matching (BEAM), a bidirectional cross-modal alignment module that aligns adapted visual and textual features at both the sample and neuron levels, establishing fine-grained cross-modal correspondence. Finally, we introduce prompt-conditioned residual integration of vision and adapted features (PRIVA), a prompt-guided residual fusion module that models vision--language interactions through gating and attention and integrates complementary information from original and adapted representations through residual fusion. Extensive experiments show that SAVERA achieves competitive performance on image captioning and visual question answering while reducing object hallucination.

items.title: EEG-World: Context-Conditioned Dynamics of the Watching Brain
items.summary: Brain encoding models predict neural responses from audiovisual input, but typically overlook how ongoing brain activity shapes an individual's response. We introduce EEG-World, a recurrent world model that forecasts 10 seconds of EEG band-power dynamics from 6 seconds of preceding EEG and the subsequent audiovisual stimulus. Pretrained on continuous EEG, EEG-World learns shared neural dynamics and adapts to unseen individuals through lightweight subject-specific readouts. Using 2,584 hours of EEG from 78 participants, we show that nonlinear recurrent forecasting surpasses strong history-aware linear baselines at scale. EEG-World achieves a forecasting correlation of 0.261 versus 0.233 for the strongest history-and-video linear model, with a 3.3-second forecasting-horizon advantage. Its learned dynamics transfer to unseen participants, outperforming the linear baseline in 23 of 24 individuals after calibration. While ongoing EEG history accounts for most predictive performance, controlled stimulus analyses reveal an additional video-dependent component. This component also enables evaluation of visual representations, with V-JEPA 2 improving clip-locked prediction by 35% over combined CLIP and DINOv2 features. Our results demonstrate the value of transferable neural dynamics for individual EEG forecasting and highlight the importance of separating state-driven from stimulus-driven predictability.

items.title: Reliable and grounded reporting of any computed tomography scan with FORA
items.summary: Artificial intelligence systems for computed tomography (CT) remain largely restricted to specific anatomical regions, examination types or predefined abnormalities, limiting their ability to provide comprehensive and spatially grounded interpretations. Here we present FORA, a general-purpose CT model that recognizes and spatially localizes 1,028 hierarchically organized radiological concepts and generates reports across the 28 CT protocols represented in our cohort. Trained on 304,962 routine CT examinations supervised by their accompanying reports, FORA learns to localize abnormalities without manually annotated lesions. Its architecture combines multiple-instance learning with an interpretable concept bottleneck that connects spatial evidence, radiological findings and report generation. We first developed and benchmarked the architecture on chest radiographs, achieving state-of-the-art performance, before training a separate model on three-dimensional CT examinations. On 36,619 held-out CT examinations, FORA achieved a macro area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.918 for radiological concept recognition, exceeding the strongest of 18 existing CT models by 0.21. FORA also ranked first on three public benchmarks, outperforming Merlin on its own test set without training on that institution's data (AUROC 0.907 versus 0.826). On independent localization benchmarks for pulmonary emboli, renal masses and rib fractures, FORA's strongest spatial evidence fell within annotated lesions at rates up to 348 times greater than chance. FORA achieved more than threefold higher macro-averaged finding recall than the strongest existing report generator. These results show that a single model can combine broad abnormality recognition, spatial localization and report generation across 12 CT examination types, using routine reports without lesion-level supervision.

items.title: EXCISE: Query-Side Exclusion for Late-Interaction Retrieval
items.summary: Late-interaction retrievers handle exclusion queries poorly. When a user asks for "X but not Z", the additive MaxSim score rewards the tokens that name Z, so documents about Z are promoted rather than suppressed, a failure we call exclusion inversion. We show that no method we tested on the frozen token embeddings recovers this constraint; the difficulty lies in identifying the excluded topic, which depends on the query alone. EXCISE therefore confines learning to the query path and leaves the index frozen. Two query-side modules (1.5M parameters in total) detect the excluded topic and re-embed a 100-document shortlist, and a parameter-free rule demotes the candidates that match it. Across six collections and three backbones, EXCISE outperforms each backbone's frozen and fine-tuned baselines on every collection. It raises ExcluIR success@10 from 0.10-0.22 to 0.84-0.85 and Boolean NOT accuracy from 0.25-0.29 to 0.84-0.92. Pooled over 1,860 test queries, EXCISE matches the strongest fine-tuned cross-encoder (568M parameters) while preserving the retrieval quality of its frozen index, whereas fine-tuned rerankers degrade ordinary retrieval. To support further work, we release X-BENCH, a tiered benchmark of explicit, cue-free and compound exclusions with no-harm and Boolean controls.

items.title: DED-Agent: An agentic AI method for autonomous thermal simulation model development and calibration in laser directed energy deposition
items.summary: In metal additive manufacturing (AM), process parameters set the local thermal history, which governs defects, microstructure and properties. Laser power, scan speed, hatch spacing, layer thickness, scan strategy and position combine into a design space of 10^4-10^6 conditions, which is beyond what human experts can map by hand with finite element (FE) thermal models: every model must be set up, meshed, solved and calibrated by an expert, and calibrating unknown heat-source parameters alone can take days to weeks. This paper presents DED-Agent, an agentic artificial intelligence (AI) method for autonomous simulation model development and calibration in laser directed energy deposition (L-DED). A supervisor agent coordinates three specialist agents that share a structured simulation specification and call open-source tools. An intent agent turns a plain-language request into a validated specification, a simulation agent builds, runs and checks an FE thermal model through physics-aware step-by-step reasoning, and a calibration agent identifies key heat-source parameters against experimental data (e.g., thermocouple data) using a high-order proper generalized decomposition (HOPGD) surrogate within a trust-region search. On five benchmark builds, from single-track walls to a multi-track band on a cylindrical tube, the agents built executable thermal models without manual intervention, with 4.1-9.1% error for the simple and medium builds. Within three calibration rounds, the error fell to 0.9-2.5%. The surrogate matched full FE to within 0.08-1.55% and shortened calibration by 5-13 times. Agentic AI can thus autonomously establish reliable, accurate simulation models for AM processes and accelerate the search for process parameters that control microstructure.

items.title: PhysMend: Verification-Guided Program Refinement for Physics-Aware Video Generation
items.summary: Video generative models synthesize realistic scenes, yet their interactions often violate physics. A ball dropped onto sand should displace grains and settle into a crater, whereas a generated video may show it passing through the surface or leaving the sand flat. Post-hoc methods typically score generated videos with a vision-language model (VLM), but such scores offer limited guidance on which object or parameter to modify, and each correction costs another synthesis. Simulation-based pipelines instead run fixed stages before synthesis, so simulation errors reach the video. To address these limitations, we present PhysMend, a training-free framework for verification-guided program refinement. PhysMend describes the target event as an editable physical program of grounded objects, events, and required relations, paired with tunable execution parameters. Our key insight is to verify and repair the event on its simulated rollout and on the depth video that conditions the generator (depth control) rather than on generated videos, enabling quantitative violation measurement, targeted editing, and fast re-verification before synthesis. A hybrid verifier evaluates semantic event consistency, physical plausibility, solver stability, and visibility in the depth control. VLM judgments are confined to event semantics and cannot override failed physical measurements, which limits the impact of VLM hallucinations. Each failed check localizes the program fields eligible for repair, and its measured violation scales a bounded update of their parameters. Only accepted depth control reaches the generator, which runs once per input. Experiments on the commonly used benchmarks Physics-IQ, PhyGenBench, and VBench-2.0 demonstrate substantial gains across different generator backbones; for example, PhysMend raises the overall Physics-IQ score of Wan-VACE from 27.33 to 39.40.

items.title: Editable Video Context: Mid-Context KV-Cache Reuse for Context-Managing Video LLMs
items.summary: Context Language Models let a model edit its own context, while Suffix Cache Reuse makes edits to text efficient by adjusting the positions of cached keys for surviving tokens. We extend these ideas to video language models with multimodal rotary position embeddings (M-RoPE). We represent a long video as timestamped segments. After viewing a sparsely sampled version, the model selects segments for decoding at 4x the frame rate, and the remaining segments are removed from its context. Our rebuild method reuses the KV cache of surviving segments by rotating their keys with a single offset shared by the temporal, height, and width components of Qwen2.5-VL's M-RoPE. A content-hashed cache also avoids repeating vision-encoder computation for those segments. In preliminary experiments with Qwen2.5-VL-7B on synthetic needle-in-a-video-haystack questions over public-domain films, the method reduces prefill tokens and end-to-end rebuild latency relative to full recomputation while usually producing the same answer. Densifying the segment containing the answer improves accuracy when that segment is known. When the model selects segments itself, accuracy does not improve: it rarely identifies a needle that was absent from the sparse sample. We release the code, raw logs, and scripts used to reproduce the paper's results.

items.title: Residual Guidance for Real-Time Interactive Video Generation
items.summary: Real-time interactive video generation allows users to change the prompt during generation to steer the evolving video. However, existing streaming models, which generate videos chunk by chunk, often keep following the previous prompt after a switch. We trace this failure to context inertia, where the previous chunk acts as a strong prior that suppresses the new prompt. Furthermore, we find that this inertia persists even when the cache retains only the previous chunk, yet discarding the context breaks visual continuity, which limits approaches that edit the cache. Rather than editing the cache, we propose Residual Guidance (RG), a simple, training-free method that counteracts context inertia with a correction measured outside the cache. Specifically, RG denoises the re-noised previous chunk once under the new prompt without the cache and adds the resulting residual to the early denoising steps of the next chunk, where its content is largely decided and the new prompt is most suppressed. Across settings ranging from a single switch to long multi-switch generation, RG substantially improves prompt switching capability on existing streaming models, including those with dedicated switching mechanisms, while largely retaining visual quality. As it requires no training or per-model tuning and adds only one forward pass per chunk, RG can be easily integrated into existing real-time video generation pipelines.

items.title: ReCoCo: From Patches to Compositions for Visual Representation Learning
items.summary: Self-supervised learning has produced powerful visual representations, yet learning strong dense features remains challenging. While consistency between augmented views provides strong image-level supervision, extending this principle to local visual content is less straightforward. Existing approaches often match individual patches across views or identify coherent regions, introducing uncertainties in correspondence estimation and assumptions about how visual content should be grouped. We introduce ReCoCo (Regional Composition Consistency), a principled approach that extends cross-view consistency to the regional level without requiring such correspondences or semantic grouping. ReCoCo represents the content shared between augmented views through compositions of their patch-level predictions over learned visual prototypes. By aligning these compositions, the model learns from regions containing multiple visual concepts without requiring them to be separated beforehand. ReCoCo integrates naturally with teacher-student self-distillation and introduces no additional learned parameters. Extensive experiments demonstrate substantial improvements in frozen-feature segmentation, clustering, and regional retrieval while maintaining competitive image-level recognition, alleviating the trade-off between dense and global representation quality.

items.title: Data-driven Reduced-order Modeling of a Multistable Viscoelastic Flow
items.summary: Viscoelastic flow past two side-by-side microcylinders has been shown to exhibit geometry-dependent transitions among symmetric, converging, diverging, and asymmetric-diverging flow states, together with regions of bistability and tristability. Here, we develop a data-driven framework for learning a two-dimensional, parameter-dependent normal form for this bifurcation structure from sparse measurements of stable flow states. We use the flow asymmetry parameters $I'$ and $I''$ as state variables, with the gap ratio $G$ and Weissenberg number $Wi$ as control parameters. In the absence of trajectory data, the measured steady states are enforced as stable equilibria of the learned vector field through equilibrium and local-stability constraints. We examine both polynomial and neural-network representations of the associated normal form and incorporate the physical reflection symmetry directly into the model. The resulting models recover the main geometry-dependent transitions and the overall structure of the experimental phase diagram. To reduce additional stable equilibria that are not constrained by the measurements, we introduce an iterative negative-sample procedure that refines the predicted equilibrium structure. Combining equilibrium data, local stability, physical symmetry, and negative samples yields the closest agreement with the experimental phase diagram among the models considered. The remaining discrepancies reflect the limited information available, solely in the form of sparse equilibrium measurements. Overall, the framework aims to showcase a prototypical example of both the potential and the limitations of inferring nonlinear flow dynamics from sparse equilibrium measurements and highlight the importance of physical constraints and additional dynamical information for reconstructing complex bifurcation structures.

items.title: Beyond Image-Text Pairs: Aligning Semantic Changes for Fine-Grained Visual Understanding
items.summary: Image-text alignment serves as a foundation for modern vision-language models (VLMs), yet prevailing training paradigms provide limited supervision for learning how semantic changes correspond across modalities. To address this limitation, we propose a post-training method that learns cross-modal semantic change correspondences through controlled visual and textual variations. Specifically, we introduce a Semantic Difference Alignment (SDA) loss which can align the directions of corresponding visual and textual representation changes. We combine our proposed SDA with pairwise sigmoid matching to jointly learn image-text correspondences and cross-modal semantic changes, encouraging more fine-grained and discriminative visual representations. To support this learning, we construct VarFamily-40K, a dataset of image-text pairs with controlled cross-modal semantic variations. Experiments demonstrate consistent improvements in compositional understanding and downstream classification performance, alongside further gains on multimodal tasks when the adapted visual encoder is integrated into VLMs.

items.title: SpatialArena: Where Do Geometric Foundation Models Stand?
