However, their ability to achieve sharp localization in both time and frequency is inherently limited by the Gabor-Heisenberg uncertainty principle. In this paper, we address this limitation by introducing a method to generate super-resolution spectrograms through the fusion of two or more spectrograms with varying resolutions. Specifically, we compute the super-resolution spectrogram as the barycenter of input spectrograms using optimal transport (OT) divergences. Our method does not require the input spectrograms to share the same time-frequency grid. The input spectrograms can be computed using any STFT parameters, and the resulting super-resolution spectrogram can be defined on an arbitrary user-specified grid. We explore various OT divergences based on different transportation costs. Notably, we introduce a novel transportation cost that preserves time-frequency geometry while significantly reducing computational complexity compared to standard Wasserstein barycenters. We adopt the unbalanced OT framework and derive a new block majorization-minimization algorithm for efficient barycenter computation. We validate the proposed method on controlled synthetic signals and recorded speech using both quantitative and qualitative evaluations. The results show that our approach combines the best localization properties of the input spectrograms while maintaining a smooth energy distribution, and preserving computational efficiency.

items.title: From Points to Trajectories: Rethinking Multimodal Alignment for Physical Events
items.summary: Advancing physical artificial intelligence (Physical AI) requires moving beyond static object recognition to ground how real-world mechanics (e.g., impact, friction, and force transfer) unfold over time. While multimodal aligners seek to capture these interactions by matching multi-sensor streams, prevailing architectures compress each temporal sequence into a single pooled embedding. We show that this paradigm fails on twin events: distinct physical executions recorded under identical task conditions. Collapsing the temporal dimension averages out transient cross-modal dynamics, effectively reducing physical event alignment to static scene recognition. Formally, we prove that as sequence length increases, any temporally pooled representation converges to the stationary recording condition. Consequently, as windows grow, no choice of loss function or embedding geometry can disambiguate twin events from pooled features alone. Instead, we show that physical events are uniquely identified by the event gap, namely the instantaneous, synchronous co-fluctuations across modalities that are erased by pooling and accumulate only along unpooled trajectories. To recover this signal, we introduce CounterPoint, a lightweight plug-in module that strips out each modality's temporal mean to score frame-level cross-modal agreement. Integrated across four state-of-the-art (SOTA) multimodal aligners, CounterPoint shifts representations from coarse condition matching to fine-grained physical event alignment, consistently outperforming existing temporal alignment methods.

items.title: A Closed-Loop Thermal Dynamic Model for AI Data Center Cooling Load Simulation
items.summary: Accurate modeling and simulation of cooling electricity demand is essential for characterizing AI data center loads, but time-synchronized operational measurements are scarce. Constant coefficient-of-performance models can oversimplify cooling behavior, while detailed thermal state-space models are cumbersome to use. This paper proposes a closed-loop simulation framework that couples a linear thermal dynamic model with deadband-based control to capture nonlinear cooling behaviors. The framework is validated against operational data from the Marconi100 supercomputer. Compared with the baseline, the proposed model reduces the mean absolute error from 95.80 to 23.52 kW and the root-mean-square error from 109.79 to 29.91 kW. The statistical evaluation further shows improved reproduction of daily peak demand and intraday variability. The framework provides a computationally tractable approach to generate physically interpretable cooling load profiles for power system studies.

items.title: Constructive continuous and sampled-data control of nonstandard singularly perturbed parabolic systems
items.summary: The existing results on control of singularly perturbed (SP) PDE systems are all qualitative with stability guaranteed for small values of SP parameter $\varepsilon$, whereas control design is confined to stable fast systems. In the present paper we study the finite-dimensional output-feedback boundary stabilization of SP parabolic systems with Neumann actuators and nonlocal sensors acting on both the slow and fast dynamics. This configuration allows us to treat not only unstable fast systems, but even a larger class of nonstandard SP systems (where the fast dynamics with $\varepsilon=0$ cannot be solved with respect to the fast state). We design a finite-dimensional controller based on the slow descriptor PDE system. We consider the continuous-time control and, for the first time, (even for the state-feedback for SP PDEs) its sampled-data implementation. For the latter, we introduce a multi-rate sampled-data framework in which the slow and fast variables can be sampled asynchronously. We consider time-triggered control input sampling and event-triggered output sampling. We prove the avoidance of Zeno behavior and derive LMI conditions for finding upper bounds on the observer dimension, sampling control intervals and $\varepsilon$ that preserve the stability. Our results include a new finite-dimensional controller design for the parabolic-elliptic equation. Numerical simulations demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed method.

items.title: Data-Driven Nonlinear Observer Design Using the Koopman Generator
items.summary: This paper deals with the data-driven design of nonlinear continuous-time observers using the Koopman generator. For systems without inputs, an observer is designed that consists of a linear system part with a nonlinear output injection. Therein, the output injection introduces additional degrees of freedom to ensure an invariant dictionary or a small projection error. Subsequently, this observer is extended to systems with inputs. These results form the basis for a data-driven nonlinear observer design using generator extended dynamic mode decomposition. Probabilistic finite-data error bounds are derived for the observer error w.r.t. the data-driven observer error dynamics and for the corresponding steady-state observation error. Examples of nonlinear systems with invariant and non-invariant dictionaries illustrate the effectiveness of the novel data-driven observer design procedure.

items.title: PPGFlowECG: Latent Rectified Flow with Cross-Modal Encoding for PPG-Guided ECG Generation and Cardiovascular Disease Detection
items.summary: Electrocardiography (ECG) is the clinical gold standard for cardiovascular disease (CVD) assessment, yet continuous monitoring is constrained by the need for dedicated hardware and trained personnel. Photoplethysmography (PPG) is ubiquitous in wearable devices and readily scalable, but it lacks electrophysiological specificity, limiting diagnostic reliability. While generative methods aim to translate PPG into clinically useful ECG signals, existing approaches are limited by the misalignment of physiological semantics in generative models and the complexity of modeling in high-dimensional signals. To address these limitations, we propose PPGFlowECG, a two-stage framework that aligns PPG and ECG in a shared latent space using the CardioAlign Encoder and then synthesizes ECGs with latent rectified flow. We further provide a formal analysis of this coupling, showing that the CardioAlign Encoder is necessary to guarantee stable and semantically consistent ECG synthesis under our formulation. Extensive experiments on four datasets demonstrate improved synthesis fidelity and downstream diagnostic utility. These results indicate that PPGFlowECG supports scalable, wearable-first CVD screening when standard ECG acquisition is unavailable.

items.title: Closed-loop Properties of Value Iteration in Continuous Time with Approximation Errors
items.summary: Value iteration is an important tool for approximating solutions of infinite-horizon optimal control problems, but in practice it is never carried out exactly: value functions are represented by finite-dimensional approximators, and the iteration is stopped after finitely many steps. This paper analyzes which closed-loop guarantees remain under these limitations for continuous-time nonlinear systems. We consider a value iteration scheme in which each iteration solves a finite-horizon optimal control problem with the previous iterate as terminal cost, and the associated controller applies the optimal input of this problem over each horizon in a sampled-data fashion. We show that if the convergence tolerance and the approximation error are small enough, the controller asymptotically stabilizes the system on sublevel sets of the computed iterate, and provide a suboptimality bound. This condition consists of pointwise inequalities that can be checked for the computed iterate, without establishing convergence of the iteration, and is a first step towards sample-based certification. We further establish inherent robustness of the controller with respect to model errors and recover classical results for the linear-quadratic regulator. Numerical studies on a linear-quadratic problem and on a nonlinear system with known optimal value function are consistent with the guarantees and show that the suboptimality bound is conservative.

items.title: Beyond Domain Randomization: Real-World Policy Adaptation in Learned Dynamics for Legged Robots
items.summary: Reinforcement learning policies are often trained with static domain randomization for real-world deployment. However, real-world environments often exhibit unmodeled dynamic variations, such as payload changes or friction shifts, that lie outside the randomization distribution, leading to performance degradation upon deployment. We propose a framework that moves beyond static domain randomization by adapting a learned dynamics model to the deployed target conditions, with a concurrent teacher-student paradigm applied to both the policy and dynamics model. This framework integrates the dynamics model into an on-policy reinforcement learning pipeline, letting the performance of the policy align with the empirical target dynamics. Experimental validations on bipedal locomotion tasks demonstrate competitive adaptability under extreme physical variations, including a payload reaching 80% of self-weight and an oil-lubricated low-friction surface.

items.title: A Bi-level Co-design Framework for Lunar Monoped with 2D Jump and Landing Control
items.summary: Legged robots for lunar exploration must be designed for low gravity, where reduced contact forces and long flight phases make leg morphology and controller choice interdependent. We study this for a planar monoped in lunar gravity (1.625 m/s^2) using a bi-level co-design framework: a differential evolution outer loop searches over link lengths, and each candidate is evaluated on a vertical jump by either a quadratic program based task-space controller (QP-TSC) or a direct-collocation based trajectory optimization. The two controllers yield different optimal link lengths, and trajectory optimization outperforms the QP-TSC across most of the design space, with 17% lower Cost of Transport (COT) at their respective optima. We then extend to a 2D jump, where trajectory optimization with centroidal angular momentum regulation produces stable in-place and forward jumps, and an LQR controller absorbs impact and stabilizes the robot after touchdown. This is demonstrated on a baseline morphology with both links 0.3 m long.

items.title: LiveAudio: From Bidirectional to Autoregressive Diffusion for Real-Time Streaming Video-to-Audio Generation
items.summary: Video-to-audio generation synthesizes sound that matches a video in content and timing, with applications ranging from film post-production to live streaming, games and interactive world models. Interactive applications receive video continuously and need the sound to follow it in real time, yet most existing video-to-audio models are bidirectional and must observe an entire clip before producing any sound. We propose LiveAudio, a streaming video-to-audio framework that generates high-quality and synchronized audio in real time while the video is playing. In contrast to prior streaming models trained from scratch, LiveAudio converts a bidirectional model into a streaming generator so as to build on its audio quality and synchronization. LiveAudio generates audio block by block, and each block depends only on the video that has already been played. The streaming generator is obtained from the bidirectional model through progressive causal fine-tuning and distillation, so that each block needs only a few sampling steps. Experiments on VGGSound show that LiveAudio outperforms existing streaming models in audio quality and synchronization, and surpasses the bidirectional model it starts from in synchronization. On a single A100 GPU, it runs in real time with a real-time factor of 0.79 and a time to first frame of 143 ms. Audio samples are available at https://streamaudio.github.io.

items.title: Hierarchical Multi-Timescale Deep Reinforcement Learning for QoS-Aware AI-RAN Configuration
items.summary: Configuring radio access networks (RANs) for heterogeneous services requires coordinating radio parameters whose effects on throughput, delay, and reliability are closely coupled and evolve over different timescales. This paper presents a hierarchical deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework for joint, QoS-aware RAN configuration that aligns the learning structure with the real-time, near-real-time, and non-real-time control loops of O-RAN that are also adopted by AI-RAN. Three proximal policy optimization agents jointly select per-user modulation and coding schemes, user-to-bandwidth-part (BWP) assignments, per-BWP transmit power, numerology, and BWP bandwidth weights, at three timescales. The agents share a QoS-aware objective combining throughput demand satisfaction with delay and reliability penalties. We extend ns-3 5G-LENA and integrate it with Ray RLlib through ns3-ai to support the required radio controls, network observations, and hierarchical policy execution. We evaluate the agents' performance in a nine-cell downlink network with inter-cell interference, varying user populations, and mixed URLLC, gaming, conversational-video, and video-streaming traffic. Compared with the baseline 5G-NR RAN, our trained hierarchical DRL agents substantially reduce URLLC and conversational-video delays, lower the residual block error rate, and prevent the near-starvation of the weakest flows, trading off slightly lower throughput for high-rate video streaming under capacity-limited conditions.

items.title: Power-Swing Blocking and Out-of-Step Tripping Scheme Using the Swing Center Voltage in Systems With Inverter-Based Resources
items.summary: Misoperation of power-swing blocking (PSB) and out-of-step tripping (OST) schemes in distance relays is a critical concern in power systems with increasing penetration levels of inverter-based resources (IBRs). Recently, several papers have studied the impact of IBRs on conventional dual-blinder PSB/OST schemes. They highlight interoperability issues concerning fast power swings and unconventional impedance trajectories, and propose revised relay settings in attempts to deal with the problems. However, the blinder-based PSB methodology suffers from being dependent on the speed of the apparent impedance just as it crosses between the blinders. It is therefore important to consider alternative methods. This paper thoroughly analyzes the characteristics of the swing center voltage (SCV) and the impacts of grid-forming (GFM) and grid-following (GFL) inverters on its local estimation. Then, an SCV-based PSB/OST scheme is proposed, where the main PSB criterion can be tuned from simple system parameters. This is made possible by a separate PSB activation function. The OST scheme uses only one setting and is motivated from the analytical analysis of the SCV with IBRs. Extensive PSCAD/EMTDC simulations verify the performance of the proposed SCV-based PSB/OST scheme and how it overcomes limitations of blinder-based schemes with GFM and GFL inverters.

items.title: The generalized method of moments is (almost) statistically efficient in low-SNR Gaussian latent-variable models
items.summary: We study estimation in the low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) regime for a broad class of Gaussian latent-variable models, including Gaussian mixtures and orbit-recovery problems. We show that, in this regime, the generalized method-of-moments (GMoM) matches the first-order asymptotic efficiency of maximum likelihood. In particular, if the moment features are chosen up to the minimal local order required for identification and are weighted optimally, then the resulting GMoM estimator has the same leading asymptotic covariance as the maximum-likelihood estimator. We further show that this efficiency can be achieved using practical, data-driven weighting schemes and is preserved under a broad class of simpler weighting choices, including the commonly used identity-weighted method of moments, although these may incur larger higher-order efficiency losses. On the other hand, inappropriate weighting or discarding moment entries can lead to persistent efficiency losses even as SNR tends to zero, despite preserving identifiability. These results distinguish the moments required for identifiability from those needed for statistical efficiency, and characterize when moment-based estimation can match the performance of maximum likelihood.

items.title: Fidelity-Based Robustness Margins for Quantum Control
items.summary: We develop certified lower bounds on structure-specific fidelity-threshold robustness margins for finite-dimensional closed quantum systems under piecewise-constant coherent control. A scalar physical parameter may perturb the drift, a control Hamiltonian, or another declared Hamiltonian component across the control horizon. A differential sensitivity bound for the trace-amplitude gate fidelity yields a threshold-dependent Lipschitz constant on the nominal connected safe parameter component and hence a certified finite perturbation radius. Recentering this certificate produces an iterative one-dimensional method whose finite runs return lower bounds on the distance to the first threshold contact. The fidelity may touch the threshold without falling below it. A three-qubit gate-control example shows that the returned bounds vary by up to a factor of three across controllers of comparable nominal fidelity and contain structure-dependent information not captured by nominal differential sensitivity alone.

items.title: A Proposal for Multiplierless RLS Adaptive Filters with Implementation Complexity Constraint
items.summary: The so-called sum-of-powers-of-two arithmetic has the advantage of using simple shift and thus avoiding multiplications operations. In this work, we provide a feasible RLS adaptive filter algorithm employing the SOPOT representation. This reduces the computational burden of the RLS algorithm. Therefore, leading to a reduction in the power consumption from a hardware implementation point of view, which is an important feature in the developing of smaller, lighter and more power-efficient portable devices.

items.title: Optimal Window Design for Intercarrier and Intersymbol Interference Power Minimization in w-OFDM
items.summary: Block transceivers are essential for modern communication systems, and they are vastly implemented in many day-to-day devices, especially the orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) technique. The application of a pulseshaping technique in the OFDM generates the so-called windowed OFDM (w-OFDM). This letter proposes an optimization of the window shape, obtaining minimal intercarrier and intersymbol interference power, ICI, and ISI, respectively. A communication system is simulated by implementing the optimized w-OFDM, and its performance is compared with a non-optimized system using a raised-cosine window.

items.title: Fault Detection in Solar Thermal Systems using Probabilistic Reconstructions
items.summary: Solar thermal systems (STS) present a promising avenue for low-carbon heat generation, with a well-running system providing heat at minimal cost and carbon emissions. However, STS can exhibit faults due to improper installation, maintenance, or operation, often resulting in a substantial reduction in efficiency or even damage to the system. As monitoring at the individual level is economically prohibitive for small-scale systems, automated monitoring and fault detection should be used to address such issues. Recent advances in data-driven anomaly detection, particularly in time series analysis, offer a cost-effective solution by leveraging existing sensors to identify abnormal system states. Here, we apply probabilistic reconstruction-based anomaly detection to the publicly available PaSTS dataset of operational domestic STS, which features real-world complexities and diverse fault types. We combine an LSTM-based Variational Autoencoder with heteroscedastic uncertainty estimation and evaluate it exclusively on systems unseen during training. Our experiments show that reconstruction-based methods detect faults in domestic STS both qualitatively and quantitatively. Our model achieves the best generalisation to unseen systems among all evaluated methods, while a rescaled PCA reconstruction baseline remains competitive on pooled threshold-free metrics. An ablation shows that heteroscedastic uncertainty estimation drives the gain in cross-system generalisation. Finally, we discuss the engineering overhead required to unlock these improvements and make a case for simple deep learning models.

items.title: Timestep Selection in Diffusion-Based OTFS Channel Estimation
items.summary: Diffusion-based channel estimators are run with a few deterministic sampling steps, and their step count is treated as a knob that trades accuracy against latency. We show that for the mean squared error this trade-off mainly comes from the default leading timestep spacing, whose first timestep indicates an intermediate noise level although the initial state is pure noise. In a multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal time frequency space receiver with ray-traced paths and per-path Doppler shifts, moving only the first timestep of the default spacing to the pure-noise end recovers the gain of trailing spacing, completely for our anchored residual estimator and mostly for a published diffusion estimator. With trailing spacing one to three steps give the most accurate single trajectory of our estimator at every signal-to-noise ratio we test, and longer trajectories raise the error, by 0.34~dB over one step at a signal-to-noise ratio of 20~dB after 50 steps. This is the direction predicted by an idealized analysis in which a long deterministic trajectory turns the posterior mean into a posterior sample. With three trailing steps, the published estimator reaches 0.8 to 1.8~dB lower normalized mean squared error than with its original five leading steps, on its own trained network and test set. A start rule that places the first timestep from the error power of the linear anchor of the estimator, with one threshold per network, recovers trailing spacing for our estimator and matches start timesteps tuned separately for every signal-to-noise ratio on a noise-prediction network. A regression network with the same architecture and data reaches 0.23 to 1.36~dB lower normalized mean squared error than the best diffusion configuration we evaluate. The step count of a diffusion channel estimator should therefore be judged only after its first timestep is fixed.

items.title: Enhancing Diabetic Retinopathy Detection with CNN-Based Models: A Comparative Study of UNET and Stacked UNET Architectures
items.summary: Diabetic Retinopathy DR is a severe complication of diabetes. Damaged or abnormal blood vessels can cause loss of vision. The need for massive screening of a large population of diabetic patients has generated an interest in a computer-aided fully automatic diagnosis of DR. In the realm of Deep learning frameworks, particularly convolutional neural networks CNNs, have shown great interest and promise in detecting DR by analyzing retinal images. However, several challenges have been faced in the application of deep learning in this domain. High-quality, annotated datasets are scarce, and the variations in image quality and class imbalances pose significant hurdles in developing a dependable model. In this paper, we demonstrate the proficiency of two Convolutional Neural Networks CNNs based models, UNET and Stacked UNET utilizing the APTOS Asia Pacific Tele-Ophthalmology Society Dataset. This system achieves an accuracy of 92.81% for the UNET and 93.32% for the stacked UNET architecture. The architecture classifies the images into five categories ranging from 0 to 4, where 0 is no DR and 4 is proliferative DR.

items.title: Boundary Stabilization of Mixed Traffic Flow With Connected Automated Vehicles
items.summary: This paper addresses boundary stabilization of stop-and-go oscillations in mixed traffic containing human-driven vehicles (HVs) and connected automated vehicles (CAVs). A penetration-dependent fundamental diagram is constructed from vehicle-class headways and effective spacing and embedded in an Aw--Rascle--Zhang (ARZ) model. Backstepping yields full-state and output-feedback controllers for the nominal linearized system. Exponential stability and finite-time convergence are established for the linearized system. Closed-loop simulations over CAV penetration rates from 0 to 1 show that increasing penetration raises the equilibrium speed and flow and reduces the convergence time for both the state-feedback and output-feedback controllers. A proportional-integral (PI) controller benchmark, input magnitude and rate constraints, physical sensor noise, and a sensitivity analysis are also considered to assess the performance of the controllers. We further illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed control methods and the simulation framework through a fundamental diagram calibration using the TGSIM dataset. These results quantify the traffic performance changes and identify the limits of the proposed method.

items.title: Asynchronous Uplink Multi-UE Networked Sensing via Multipath Correlation
items.summary: Multiuser uplink sensing offers a promising paradigm for networked sensing by leveraging signals from multiple user equipment (UEs) to enhance sensing coverage and performance. This paper investigates asynchronous multiuser uplink orthogonal frequency-division multiple access sensing by exploiting correlated multipath structures across UEs. A common frontend first mitigates the dominant timing offsets (TOs), carrier-frequency offsets (CFOs), and phase offsets (POs) through LoS-referencing and constructs a reduced delay-angle-of-arrival (AoA) search space. Two alternative multiuser sensing estimators are then proposed, with different mechanisms of explicitly and implicitly exploiting UE correlation, respectively. The first explicitly adopts a latent-group shared-private sparse Bayesian learning (Group-SBL) model to exploit group-shared propagation structures while accommodating UE-specific components. The second combines calibrated multiuser observations for joint multiple signal classification (MUSIC) processing, recovering a global delay-AoA pool that can be further associated with individual UEs. Residual-TO refinement is conducted with both estimator updates, followed by local-grid delay-AoA refinement and residual common-phase compensation before Doppler estimation. Simulations under a 5G New Radio-compatible uplink configuration show that both multiuser schemes outperform their corresponding per-UE baselines, with larger gains as cross-UE propagation correlation increases.

items.title: Identax: A Toolbox for Efficient Learning of Linear, Parameter-Varying, and Nonlinear Systems in JAX
items.summary: Accurate data-driven modelling of dynamical systems is increasingly important across engineering disciplines, yet state-of-the-art identification methods are often computationally demanding, opaque, or poorly scalable. We present Identax, a JAX toolbox for identifying linear, Linear Parameter-Varying (LPV) and nonlinear systems, designed as an extensible foundation for system identification research. Its modular design allows model structures, identification criteria and optimization methods to be extended independently. The first release provides state-space and Linear Fractional Representation (LFR) models, multiple-shooting criteria for parallel training, and a transparent optimization pipeline. On the Silverbox benchmark, an LPV-LFR model outperforms all previous black-box results while training in under three minutes on a CPU. On a control moment gyroscope, Identax matches state-of-the-art accuracy.

items.title: Passivity-Based Decentralized Stability Criterion and Active-Damping Design for DC Microgrids
items.summary: Interactions among converter-interfaced devices can destabilize DC microgrids (DCMGs). In practice, detailed device models often cannot be disclosed to the system operator for centralized stability analysis, and only some device controllers can be redesigned. This paper develops an output-feedback passivity (OFP)-based decentralized small-signal stability criterion for DCMGs with both fixed-controller and tunable-controller devices. By incorporating the certified OFP indices of fixed-controller devices into an equivalent network, the criterion quantifies a locally verifiable OFP requirement for each tunable-controller device. Full-order analysis further reveals that the finite current-loop bandwidth imposes upper bounds on the OFP indices of droop-controlled converters, which can remain negative for any PI gains despite positive predictions based on reduced-order analysis. Guided by the criterion and these bounds, an OFP-oriented active damping (OFP-AD) strategy is proposed for these converters. The proposed strategy improves the OFP index toward the required value while preserving the cascaded PI control and droop characteristics, using output-capacitor-current feedback. Case studies on a 39-node DCMG validate the proposed criterion and OFP-AD.

items.title: Autonomous UAV Navigation in an Unknown Environment via Multi-Trajectory Model Predictive Control
items.summary: A novel model predictive control (MPC) formulation, named multi-trajectory MPC (mt-MPC), is presented and applied to the problem of autonomous navigation of an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) in an unknown environment. The UAV is equipped with a LiDAR sensor, providing only a partial description of the surroundings and resulting in time-varying constraints as the vehicle navigates among the obstacles. The control system layout is hierarchical: the low-level loops stabilize the vehicle's trajectories and track the set-points commanded by the high-level, mt-MPC controller. The latter is required to plan the UAV trajectory trading off safety, i.e. to avoid collisions with the uncertain obstacles, and exploitation, i.e. to reach an assigned target location. To achieve this goal, mt-MPC considers different future state trajectories in the same Finite Horizon Optimal Control Problem (FHOCP), enabling a partial decoupling between constraint satisfaction (safety) and cost function minimization (exploitation). Recursive feasibility and, consequently, persistent obstacle avoidance guarantees are derived under the assumption of a time invariant environment. The performance of the approach is studied in simulation and compared with that of a standard MPC, showing good improvement.

items.title: Implicit Neural Representation for 3D Radio Map Compression in Low-Altitude Environments
items.summary: Low-altitude wireless networks require accurate 3D radio maps (RMs) to support environment-aware communication. However, due to the extensive spatial coverage and multi-modal channel representations, 3D RMs usually incur prohibitive storage and transmission overhead, making efficient compression highly desirable. In this paper, we propose NeRM3D, an implicit neural representation (INR)-based framework for compact 3D RM compression. Specifically, NeRM3D represents the entire 3D RM as a lightweight neural network that maps discrete height values to corresponding RM slices, thereby encoding the RM into a compact neural network. To effectively model the volumetric spatial structure of 3D RMs, NeRM3D jointly integrates horizontal embeddings with height-aware modulation, enabling efficient extraction and fusion of spatial correlations across different vertical layers and channel modalities. Experimental results demonstrate that NeRM3D achieves competitive compression performance with low complexity and decoding latency, making it suitable for resource-constrained devices.

items.title: Angular characteristics of attenuation and temporal dispersion introduced by single deciduous bush in winter conditions at FR2 band
items.summary: Vegetation-induced attenuation and temporal dispersion remain important impairments in millimeter-wave radio propagation, particularly in the frequency range 2 (FR2) band, where highly directional links are employed. Existing vegetation attenuation models, including ITU-R P.833, predominantly address scenarios involving trees or vegetation clusters and are typically derived for the main radiation direction of the transmitting antenna. This paper presents an experimental study of angular-dependent attenuation and temporal dispersion introduced by a single deciduous bush under winter conditions. Measurements were conducted on a university campus at 28 GHz and 38 GHz using a wideband channel-sounding testbed operating from 1 MHz to 44 GHz. The bush, approximately 3 m in height, was located at the center of a circular measurement trajectory with a radius of 10 m, along which the receiver was positioned at angular intervals of approximately 8 deg. Directional antennas with 7-9 deg half-power beamwidth were employed, and reception angles from 0 to 200 deg relative to the transmitter-bush axis were investigated. The results demonstrate significant angular variability in both excess attenuation and temporal dispersion, indicating substantial contributions from scattering outside the main propagation direction. Differences between the two carrier frequencies are analyzed, highlighting frequency-dependent attenuation mechanisms even in leaf-off conditions. The presented findings extend existing single-vegetation models by incorporating angular characteristics and temporal effects, providing valuable insights for the design and modeling of FR2 wireless links in sparse-vegetation environments.

items.title: Combining Physical Layer Security and Symmetric Encryption to Secure Rate-Splitting Multiple Access
items.summary: The demand for increased spectral efficiency (SE) in downlink multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) systems has led to the development of various multiple access techniques. Among these, rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) can improve SE over space division multiple access (SDMA) and non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) by splitting each user's data into common and private parts. The common parts from all users are then encoded into a single common message, which is transmitted alongside the private messages using an RSMA-specific precoder. Recent results showed that the precoder can be modified to enable physical layer security (PLS) by integrating secrecy rate constraints into the design. However, this approach only secures the private messages, while the common part of each user remains unprotected. To address this limitation, we propose a hybrid-PLS RSMA scheme that symmetrically encrypts all user data and embeds key information within the PLS-secured private messages. Additionally, the RSMA precoder is adapted to ensure that the private messages are sufficiently sized to carry the key information. The precoder design is formulated as a non-convex SE maximization problem and solved using successive convex approximation (SCA). Analytical and numerical evaluations demonstrate that the proposed hybrid-PLS RSMA can significantly improve SE compared to partially secure RSMA and secure SDMA, when complete user data security is required.

items.title: Safety-Tiered ISAC Scheduling with History-Aware Value of Information for V2X Networks
items.summary: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) assisted vehicle-to-everything (V2X) networks prioritize safety-critical radar sensing over communication. However, existing scheduling methods overlook the varying criticality of vehicles, long-term fairness in service quality, and information staleness. Considering this, we propose a low-complexity sensing-prioritized allocation for radar and communication (SPARC-V) to maximize the value of information (VoI) in V2X networks. SPARC-V addresses these challenges with a two-stage hierarchical resource scheduling framework. For sensing, vehicles are first categorized into safety tiers based on a risk metric. Safety-critical vehicles receive orthogonal resources, while others can reuse resources under specific constraints. Sensing resources are allocated based on a sensing priority metric that balances safety significance and long-term fairness. In the next stage, communication resources are allocated to vehicles with the most outdated information. Performance is measured using a unified VoI metric that considers sensing quality, safety relevance, and information freshness. Monte Carlo simulations show that SPARC-V achieves the highest network VoI of 26.5 among all baselines, with its advantage over baselines widening as vehicle density increases.

items.title: IP-GNO: An Inductive Physics-Informed Graph Neural Operator for Automated Distribution System State Estimation
items.summary: Distribution System State Estimation (DSSE) is a crucial tool for real-time monitoring, operation, and control of the new-age distribution systems (DSs) due to intensified voltage fluctuations and operational uncertainties introduced by volatile power injection at the nodes. Existing GNN-based approaches generally exhibit limited generalization across networks with different sizes and topologies, making zero-shot cross-grid transfer to unseen DSs a significant challenge. To overcome the aforementioned challenges, this article proposes an Inductive Physics-Informed Graph Neural Operator (IP-GNO) for scalable and transferable DSSE. The proposed framework frames complex bus voltage estimation as an operator-learning problem inspired by the Neumann series expansion of the inverse bus admittance matrix. An admittance-parameterized kernel, incorporating a self-admittance gate in the zeroth-order term and a persistent source-injection skip connection across network layers, captures the underlying electrical dependencies. Additionally, a Physics-Embedded Tree Encoding (PETE) scheme introduces five grid-size-invariant positional features derived from path impedance and a DC-linearized phase-angle prior. A sine-cosine output formulation is further employed to address phase-angle periodicity and ensure stable training. The proposed IP-GNO module is evaluated on two small (IEEE 33- and 69-bus), two medium (IEEE 123- and 136-bus), and one large (2522-bus) sized DSs. Particularly, its zero-shot cross-grid generalization capability is investigated by training the model exclusively on the IEEE 33-bus system and directly evaluating it on four unseen distribution networks of different sizes without retraining or fine-tuning. A detailed comparative analysis with the existing state-of-the-art DSSE tools proves the superiority of IP-GNO, enabling scalable DSSE across heterogeneous DSs.

items.title: Distributed Constraint-coupled Resource Allocation: Anytime Feasibility and Violation Robustness
items.summary: This paper considers distributed resource allocation problems (DRAPs) with a coupled constraint for real-time systems. Based on primal-dual methods, we adopt a control perspective for optimization algorithm design by synthesizing a safe feedback controller using control barrier functions to enforce constraint satisfaction. On this basis, a distributed anytime-feasible resource allocation (DanyRA) algorithm is proposed. It is shown that the DanyRA algorithm converges to the exact optimal solution of DRAPs while preserving feasibility of the coupled inequality constraint from a feasible initialization. To address constraint violations caused by external disturbances, we develop a recover-after-violation mechanism using a virtual queue with a minimum buffer, enabling feasibility recovery within a prescribed number of iterations. We characterize the trade-off between convergence accuracy and violation robustness for a fixed positive buffer and establish exact convergence with a suitably decaying buffer. DanyRA is further specialized to coupled equality constraints, with constraint preservation and an explicit linear convergence rate established. Finally, a numerical example is provided for verification.

items.title: Robust Lateral String Stability and Error Attenuation for Heterogeneous Vehicle Platoons
items.summary: Keeping an entire vehicle platoon close to its planned path is essential for navigating road boundaries and obstacles safely. Followers may rely on predecessor information for lateral guidance, which couples their lateral dynamics and allows errors to propagate downstream. This paper develops a robust lateral string stability framework to study this propagation and achieve downstream error attenuation in heterogeneous platoons under varying longitudinal motion and local perturbations. Arc-length-based feedback linearization gives each vehicle the same nominal lateral error dynamics, with parameter uncertainty and external disturbances represented as local perturbations. We define robust $\mathcal L_2$ lateral string stability in terms of platoon-length-uniform error bounds and derive a sufficient condition for achieving it. Furthermore, we show that the same condition guarantees platoon-length-uniform $\mathcal L_\infty$ error bounds. For the considered control formulations, predecessor tracking (PT) can accumulate lateral errors, whereas desired-path tracking (DT) prevents this accumulation. We propose a learn-from-predecessor (LFP) strategy with explicit gains for downstream error attenuation and characterize how intervehicle perturbation differences limit this attenuation. Simulations validate the theoretical findings under vehicle heterogeneity, varying longitudinal motion, and local perturbations.

items.title: Probabilistic Risk Sensitivity and Loss Aversion in Cumulative Prospect Theory
items.summary: This paper develops a binary-gamble framework for characterizing risk sensitivity and loss aversion in Cumulative Prospect Theory (CPT). The proposed probabilistic risk-sensitivity metric is defined as a probability-threshold ratio that determines acceptance and preference thresholds in choice problems involving either a certain outcome and a binary gamble or two binary gambles. We show how standard notions of symmetric and non-symmetric bet aversion can be recovered within this framework, and we compare the resulting threshold-based conditions with utility premia, probability premia, and Arrow-Pratt curvature measures. The analysis clarifies when these criteria coincide and when they diverge, particularly for increasing aversion conditions, binary gambles with unequal probability distributions, and settings involving probability weighting functions. We also identify technical restrictions that arise when CPT-utility functions are used to represent loss aversion at the reference point. The resulting framework provides a decision-theoretic interpretation of risk sensitivity that is directly tied to probability thresholds and complements existing premium-based approaches.

items.title: Dynamic Channel Gain Map Reconstruction via Object-Attached Gaussian Propagation
items.summary: Channel gain maps describe location-dependent propagation, but moving vehicles can change reception beyond their physical footprints. Reconstructing these changes requires connecting local object states to regional power. We consider a fixed transmitter and predefined receiver areas, with historical static and dynamic radio supervision and continuing delayed, noisy vehicle-state messages. We propose OA-GS, an object-attached Gaussian propagation model with a shared area correction. Each vehicle carries anisotropic kernels whose effective attributes are supplied by offline-calibrated templates and affine condition generators. Closed-form Gaussian integrals along finite propagation segments evaluate an effective attenuation model, while directional scattering terms account for additional power. These interactions modulate a learned static reference and contribute to regional channel gain. A shared multilayer perceptron then uses object, propagation, and receiver-area features to predict a bounded path-loss residual that compensates for errors in the compact propagation model. All learned parameters remain fixed during deployment, and reconstruction uses arrived vehicle messages without current-traffic radio measurements. In a fixed-scene ray-tracing study over four development traffic sequences and three initializations, OA-GS reduces map and strong-event dynamic-response root-mean-square errors (RMSEs) from 2.503 to 1.272 dB and from 5.965 to 3.563 dB, respectively, relative to a task-adapted GS-CG baseline receiving eight initial radio reports. The shared correction reduces strong-event dynamic-response error from 3.962 to 3.563 dB under the same propagation backbone, demonstrating the benefit of combining explicit propagation structure with learned regional correction.

items.title: Deep-Learning-Based Classiffcation of Relay-Surface Scattering Regimes for NLOS Millimeter-Wave Sensing
items.summary: In non-line-of-sight (NLOS) millimeter-wave sensing, relay-surface scattering alters target echoes and can cause propagation-model mismatch, angle-estimation errors, and ghost targets. DEKL, a deep-learning framework, identifies the dominant scattering regime from radar echoes without measuring surface roughness. Multipath echo models describe specular reflection, structured multipath reflection, and diffuse scattering. These models and a no-target hypothesis define a model-selection problem with unknown parameters. The Kullback-Leibler information criterion yields an adaptive decision rule for selecting among these hypotheses. A lightweight network, KLNet, learns covariance-domain features and combines attention with confidence-gated iterative decoding to avoid repeated likelihood evaluation. Analytical simulations, independent electromagnetic simulations, and radar measurements show that DEKL improves discrimination over the evaluated information-criterion-based rules. Ablations show how attention, confidence supervision, and gated decoding contribute to selective prediction and robustness under controlled covariance perturbations. The predicted regime guides propagation-model selection for radio-environment repre-sentations in wireless-network digital twins and informs NLOS localization and imaging.

items.title: Dynamic Constraint Reconstruction Based Control Barrier Functions for Safety-Critical Control of High-Dimensional Manipulators
items.summary: Control barrier functions (CBFs) provide formal safety guarantees for constrained nonlinear systems, but their effectiveness relies on accurate system dynamics. In high-dimensional manipulators subject to unknown disturbances and model uncertainties, fixed safety constraints constructed from nominal dynamics may become inconsistent with the actual system behavior, leading to safety degradation or excessive conservatism. This paper proposes a dynamic constraint reconstruction based control barrier function (DCR-CBF) framework for safety-critical control of disturbed robotic manipulators. An extended state observer is employed to estimate lumped disturbances online, and the estimated disturbance is incorporated into high-order control barrier functions to reconstruct safety constraints according to the estimated true dynamics. To address estimation inaccuracies, a safety margin is introduced, and a sufficient condition is derived to guarantee forward invariance under bounded estimation errors. Simulation studies on a 4-DOF excavation manipulator demonstrate that the proposed DCR-CBF method achieves zero safety violation under strong unknown disturbances while significantly improving trajectory-tracking performance compared with standard and robust CBF methods.

items.title: Stability and Safety of Grid-Following Inverters in Weak Grids via Barrier Function Control
items.summary: This paper proposes a barrier control approach for the safe regulation of grid-following voltage-source converters (VSC), operating in weak grid conditions. The proposed controller aims to enhance the transient performance and synchronization properties of the VSC, providing frequency and current limiting guarantees by employing smooth control barrier functions. First, a dynamic model is derived that includes the dynamic state interactions that are omitted in quasi-steady-state approaches, revealing the destabilizing elements both during transient and steady-state performance. Then, it is analytically proven that the proposed control law guarantees frequency limitation and inner current evolution in prescribed safety regions, while counteracting the destabilizing strong coupling between PCC voltage and injected current. In addition, sufficient conditions are formulated that guarantee the stability of the closed-loop system with respect to desired operating points. The theoretic results are verified in simulations of case studies operating in varying grid strength.

items.title: Neural 3D Object Reconstruction with Small-Scale Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
items.summary: Miniaturized Uncrewed Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) can access indoor and hard-to-reach spaces, but severe constraints on payload and autonomy have limited their use in demanding tasks such as high-quality 3D reconstruction. We introduce a novel system architecture that enables autonomous, high-fidelity 3D scanning of static objects with sub-100 gram UAVs. Our core innovation lies in a closed-loop active viewpoint selection framework specifically tailored for ultra-constrained micro-platforms, advancing beyond standard static or offline active reconstruction methods. The framework establishes a dual-reconstruction pipeline that creates a real-time (RT) feedback loop between data capture and flight control. A near-RT process uses Structure-from-Motion (SfM) to generate an instantaneous point-cloud of the object. A systematic trajectory adaptation algorithm analyzes the model quality on the fly and dynamically adapts the UAV's trajectory based on parameterized spatial partitioning to intelligently capture new images of poorly covered areas, ensuring comprehensive acquisition. For the final, high-fidelity output, a non-RT pipeline employs a Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF)-based Neural 3D Reconstruction (N3DR) approach, fusing SfM-derived camera poses with precise external location data, evaluated across both radio-based Ultra Wideband (UWB) and visual motion-capture setups, to correct sensor noise and achieve superior accuracy. We implemented and validated this architecture using Crazyflie 2.1 UAVs. Our experiments, conducted in both single- and multi-UAV configurations show that algorithmic dynamic trajectory adaptation consistently improves reconstruction quality over static flight paths. This work demonstrates a scalable and autonomous solution that unlocks the potential of miniaturized UAVs for fine-grained 3D reconstruction, a capability previously reserved for much larger platforms.

items.title: Stable and Fair Benefit Allocation in Mixed-Energy Truck Platooning: A Coalitional Game Approach
items.summary: This paper addresses the benefit allocation in a mixed-energy truck platoon composed of fuel-powered and electric trucks. The interactions among trucks during platoon formation are modeled as a coalitional game with transferable utility. We first design a stable payoff allocation scheme that accounts for truck heterogeneity in energy savings and platoon roles (leader or follower), establishing core-stability conditions to ensure that no subset of trucks has an incentive to deviate for greater benefit. To enhance payoff fairness, we then propose a closed-form, Shapley value-based allocation approach that is computationally efficient and independent of the platoon size. Sufficient conditions under which the allocation is both fair and core-stable are provided. In scenarios where the Shapley value falls outside the core, we develop an alternative allocation based on the stable payoff that minimizes the mean relative deviation from the Shapley value while preserving core stability. This deviation is further proved to be upper-bounded by $1$, showing a favorable trade-off between stability and fairness. Finally, extensive numerical studies validate the theoretical results and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in facilitating stable, equitable, and sustainable cooperation in mixed-energy truck platooning.

items.title: Predictive Safety Filter for Multi-Modal Learned Policies
items.summary: This paper presents a predictive safety filter (PSF) for learned policies with multi-modal outputs. We represent the multi-modal output as a Gaussian mixture model (GMM) and seek a trajectory that remains in a high-likelihood region while satisfying state and input constraints for nonlinear systems. The resulting problem is formulated as a Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence minimization between the filter output and the GMM. By modeling the filter output as a Gaussian with vanishing covariance, this objective reduces in the zero-variance limit to a log-sum-exp cost, yielding a tractable nonlinear program (NLP) solved once per time step. We show that the performance degradation due to safety enforcement is bounded by a function of the worst-case KL divergence. The proposed method is validated in autonomous parking scenarios and compared with two predictive safety filter baselines: one that filters only the maximum-likelihood mode and one that filters all candidate modes and selects the best filtered one according to the finite-horizon discounted return. The proposed method achieves higher aggregate goal-reaching success than both baselines while requiring only a single NLP per step and achieving lower wall-clock time than Parallel SF in the full-mixture comparison.

items.title: Reciprocal Range-Doppler Estimation with Partial Path Association for Asynchronous Bistatic OFDM-ISAC
items.summary: In bistatic integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), clock asynchronism shifts the delay and Doppler measured from orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) echoes. The two stations may see different reflectors, so the receiver must identify which echoes belong to the same path before combining the two views. For partial path association, PreVote finds a common displacement in the directional delay and Doppler differences. One-to-one assignment at this displacement accepts compatible pairs and allows other paths to remain unmatched. Each station uses coherent compression to form a subcarrier vector and a slow-time vector per path. For range-Doppler estimation in reciprocal sensing, the center multiplies paired vectors without conjugation. The opposite constant clock terms cancel, and a correct pair yields twice the physical phase slopes of one path. A Cramer-Rao bound (CRB) for fixed identities and phase branches quantifies the shared clock uncertainty. At the higher signal-to-noise ratios tested, reciprocal fusion yields lower range and Doppler errors than both receivers using calibrated echoes. Under partial visibility, displacement-based matching recovers more targets with correct identities and prescribed accuracy than separate centering with the same fusion stage. Balancing directional energy and extending the common aperture improve Doppler accuracy, while carrier frequency variation increases error.

items.title: Two Heads Are Better Than One: Audio-Visual Speech Error Correction with Dual Hypotheses
items.summary: This paper introduces a new paradigm for generative error correction (GER) framework in audio-visual speech recognition (AVSR) that reasons over modality-specific evidences directly in the language space. Our framework, DualHyp, empowers a large language model (LLM) to compose independent N-best hypotheses from separate automatic speech recognition (ASR) and visual speech recognition (VSR) models. To maximize the effectiveness of DualHyp, we further introduce RelPrompt, a noise-aware guidance mechanism that provides modality-grounded prompts to the LLM. RelPrompt offers the temporal reliability of each modality stream, guiding the model to dynamically switch its focus between ASR and VSR hypotheses for an accurate correction. Under various corruption scenarios, our framework attains up to 57.7% error rate gain on the LRS2 benchmark over standard ASR baseline, contrary to single-stream GER approaches that achieve only 10% gain. To facilitate research within our DualHyp framework, we release the code and the dataset comprising ASR and VSR hypotheses at https://github.com/sungnyun/dualhyp.

items.title: Value function based Reward shaping for safety in quadrupeds
items.summary: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has progressed from simple control tasks to complex real-world challenges with large state spaces. While RL excels in these tasks, training time remains a limitation. Reward shaping is a popular solution, but existing methods often rely on value functions, which face scalability issues. This paper presents a novel safety-oriented reward-shaping framework inspired by barrier functions, offering simplicity and ease of implementation across various environments and tasks. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed reward formulations, we conduct simulation experiments on the Unitree Go1 quadruped robot in Isaacgym. The policy was better than the existing baselines and reduced safety violations from 27% to 0.1% without almost any compromise on the performance.

items.title: UV3CP: Universal ViT-Based 3D Channel Predictor for MIMO-OFDM Systems
items.summary: Channel aging in time-division duplex multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) systems causes a mismatch between uplink-based channel state information and the downlink channel at the transmission instant. Although vision transformers (ViTs) are effective for channel prediction, their performance is highly sensitive to the patch size, whose optimum depends on the channel coherence region. Moreover, changing the patch size typically requires retraining because it alters the token grid and patch embedding operator. In this paper, we propose a universal ViT-based 3D channel prediction framework, called UV3CP, for MIMO-OFDM systems. The proposed UV3CP employs an efficient 3D ViT backbone to capture frequency, time, and spatial channel dependencies. First, based on second-order channel statistics, we derive a statistics-aware patch-size selection rule that selects axis-wise patch lengths using a mean-squared-error-based criterion, thereby matching the tokenization granularity to the dominant channel coherence while controlling token length and complexity. Second, we develop a statistics-aware patch-embedding resizing method that enables a single shared UV3CP to operate across different patch sizes without patch-size-specific retraining. Simulation results show that the proposed method improves robustness under various scenarios and patch-size mismatch while reducing the need to train and store multiple patch-size-specific ViT models.

items.title: Prescribed Time Higher Order Control Lyapunov-Barrier Functions
items.summary: We propose a framework based on Repeated-Root Prescribed Time Higher-Order Control Lyapunov- Barrier Functions (RR-Pxt-HOCL-BF) that guarantees convergence to a safe set/ goal set within user-specified time. Unlike conventional Higher-Order Control Barrier Functions, which does not provide any guarantee on reaching the safe set if the system is initially not in safe set, the proposed method enforces convergence within a prescribed time horizon. This is achieved through a structured differential constraint derived from repeated roots of the characteristic polynomial, leading to closed-form polynomial solutions that ensure convergence at the desired time. Analytical conditions for forward invariance and prescribed-time reachability are derived, with explicit formulations for second-order systems. The approach is validated on an acceleration-controlled unicycle and an inverted pendulum and compared with existing HOCBF methods. Simulation results demonstrate reliable convergence within the desired time horizon, even in scenarios where conventional approaches fail.

items.title: When to Move: Online Repositioning of Movable Antenna Arrays Under a Long-Term Actuation Energy Budget
items.summary: Movable antenna (MA) arrays improve multiuser throughput by repositioning their elements, but mechanical movement reduces transmission time and consumes actuation energy. Changes in user configurations create nonuniform demand for repositioning over time, while each movement determines which positions are reachable in subsequent slots. Thus, online control must decide when to spend a limited actuation-energy budget, not only where to position the antennas. We formulate causal effective-throughput maximization under displacement-dependent movement delay, inter-slot reachability, and a long-term average actuation-energy constraint. We propose Lyapunov-based online movable-antenna repositioning (LOMA), which adjusts the price of movement through a virtual queue and solves the resulting nonconvex position problem via proximal minorization--maximization, accounting for nonsmooth movement delay and promoting sparse antenna updates. We establish monotone ascent of the smoothed per-slot objective, a finite-horizon sample-path energy bound, almost-sure long-term budget feasibility under a Gaussian fading model with bounded large-scale gains, and a state-matched throughput comparison separating temporal energy allocation from per-slot optimization error. Simulations show that LOMA concentrates actuation after intermittent user changes and improves effective throughput over optimized fixed arrays and a per-slot-budget counterpart, while continuous channel drift favors more frequent incremental repositioning. Additional simulations with pilot-based channel estimates in sparse millimeter-wave channels show that LOMA retains most of the throughput benefits of online repositioning while operating near its prescribed long-term actuation-energy budget.

items.title: MIMO Integrated Sensing and Communications: A Fisher-based Local Mutual Information Approach
items.summary: Integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) beamforming requires a sensing utility that is compatible with the communication rate and aligned with per-target angle estimation. Fisher information (FI)/Cramér--Rao bound (CRB) criteria depend on the angular units and generally involve coupled multi-target matrices, whereas sensing mutual information (SMI) is typically defined on aggregate response variables. This paper proposes Fisher-based local mutual information (F-LMI), a prior-aware bit-domain utility for multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) ISAC. F-LMI linearizes each target-specific range-compressed statistic around the angular prior mean and yields a closed-form local information gain. In the single-target case, it admits a Bayesian CRB (BCRB) log-ratio interpretation and is a locally consistent surrogate for the nonlinear parameter MI. For multiple targets, the prior-induced variations of the non-intended targets are marginalized into a beamformer-dependent interference-plus-noise covariance in each branch. We derive a fractional-programming algorithm with linear-system updates and scalar bisection. Monte Carlo simulations with nonlinear target-wise posterior-mean receivers show that F-LMI reduces the root-mean-square error (RMSE) by 5.0--14.7\% relative to a target-indexed Bayesian-bound baseline at two matched rates in a closely spaced layout. Under a common basis-selection protocol, it also attains lower branch RMSE than aggregate and joint criteria.

items.title: One UWB Radar, Many Views: Comparing and Fusing Signal Representations for Human Activity Recognition
items.summary: IEEE 802.15.4z-compliant impulse-radio ultra-wideband (IR-UWB) transceivers are increasingly built into consumer devices, enabling contactless, privacy-preserving human activity recognition (HAR) in healthcare. Before activity classification, the signal is typically converted into range-time, range-Doppler, or time-Doppler maps, each exposing different spatial and motion cues. Existing comparisons often apply shared processing across representations, leaving it unclear whether their rankings hold after independent tuning. It is also unknown whether rankings and fusion gains generalize across environments and activities, and at what computational cost. Consequently, practitioners lack guidance on which representation and processing suit a given HAR deployment. We release an open dataset of raw IR-UWB measurements collected by a ceiling-mounted radar from 44 participants during scripted activity sequences in 12 layouts across two bedrooms. Using a statistically guided, staged search, we independently tune each representation across five processing and deployment settings. We then compare individual and fused performance under layout and room shifts and quantify computational cost. Across over 1{,}000 cross-validated models, independent tuning proves essential, as optimal processing differs per representation and processing choices shift macro-F1 by up to 26 points, four times the gap between representations. Once tuned, the range-Doppler map leads for unseen layouts (85.1\% macro-F1), while time-Doppler map does for unseen rooms (72.7\%). Fusing all three maps raises these scores to 89.1\% and 80.0\%, respectively. Lower sampling rates and narrower Doppler bands reduce latency by 38--51\% with at most a 1.5-point macro-F1 loss. The best representation for UWB HAR is therefore a deployment decision, not a fixed property.

items.title: Automated Neural Network Auditing (ANNA) for Energy Market Settlements: A Machine and Reinforcement Learning-Based Approach
items.summary: The integration of segmented energy markets into Independent System Operators (ISOs) like CAISO and MISO has increased settlement complexity. Automated transaction processing creates challenges for evaluating accuracy, compliance, and financial integrity. Traditional rule-based manual auditing is inefficient, error-prone, and cannot handle the data volume from automated markets.This research proposes Automated Neural Network Auditing (ANNA), a machine and reinforcement learning framework for settlement auditing via anomaly prioritization. ANNA integrates statistical anomaly detection, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), clustering, and Deep Q-Network (DQN) reinforcement learning to flag potentially anomalous transactions from historical market data. The approach is evaluated as an analyst-support tool for prioritizing transactions needing further audit review.ANNA was tested against traditional statistical methods, clustering-based techniques, and supervised/reinforcement learning models. The study used three years of CAISO settlement data over 63 million source records across 32 charge codes and multiple counterparties. After preprocessing, approximately 2.9 million labeled transactions formed the working dataset, with model-specific subsets used for training and evaluation. Performance was assessed using precision, recall, computational efficiency, and false-negative detection.ANNA outperforms traditional methods by identifying hidden relationships in settlement data, while standard deviation thresholds, K-Means, KNN, and Q-Learning performed poorly across key metrics. The result is a scalable solution integrating machine and reinforcement learning for automated auditing of energy market settlements, contributing computationally efficient anomaly prioritization to settlement-auditing workflows.

items.title: Optimization of a Solar-Grid Water Supply System with Hydraulic Energy Storage: A Case Study
items.summary: Given the high cost of grid-scale batteries, other energy storage approaches are needed for developing and low-income regions. Elevated volumes of water are often more economically feasible energy storage options than batteries in these contexts. This paper presents a dual-framework modeling approach for one such energy storage setup: a solar-grid hybrid water supply system in the arid Afar region of Ethiopia. By utilizing an elevated 1,900 m3 water reservoir as a "hydraulic battery," the system replaces traditional electrochemical storage, significantly reducing capital expenditures. Using Python for high-resolution technical simulation and Xendee for economic optimization, the study shows a 55.1% solar fraction and a 10% Internal Rate of Return (IRR). The results confirm that hybrid systems with hydraulic storage offer a financially viable and reliable solution for water access in energy-constrained regions.

items.title: SA-GLRT-D: Sidelobe-Aware GLRT-Based Detector for FMCW Radar
items.summary: This paper investigates adaptive detection for frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar in multi-target complex scenarios, where reference-cell contamination, spectral leakage from the cell under test (CUT), and the resulting sidelobe interference severely degrade detection performance. A sidelobe-aware detector based on the generalized likelihood ratio test (GLRT), termed SA-GLRT-D, is proposed. Unlike conventional filtering-then-constant false alarm rate (CFAR) schemes, the proposed method explicitly accounts for the non-ideal frequency-domain energy spreading of the CUT induced by the finite-window effect. Accordingly, conventional single-cell target detection is extended to local-region detection, and decision statistic construction, CUT-related parameter estimation, and sidelobe interference suppression are jointly accomplished within a unified hypothesis-testing framework. Furthermore, to reduce computational complexity, a fast implementation of SA-GLRT-D is developed, together with a dedicated parameter initialization strategy to enhance the stability of numerical optimization. Simulation and real-measurement results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high-accuracy target detection while maintaining a constant false alarm rate, with favorable computational efficiency.

items.title: Motion-Sickness-Aware Vehicle Control via DKUC-Based Inverse Design and Iterative Feedback Tuning
items.summary: Tuning existing vehicle controllers for motion-sickness reduction requires a desired vehicle response that reflects physiological comfort. The six-degree-of-freedom subjective vertical conflict (6DoF-SVC) model can evaluate sensory conflict induced by vehicle motion, but it does not directly provide a target motion for controller design. This paper proposes a 2-step framework to construct such a reference. First, a target SVC trajectory is generated from the baseline response by limiting conflict peaks while imposing a minimum activity level. Second, a lifted linear model identified using Deep KoopmanU with Control (DKUC) is inverted to map the target SVC trajectory to a regularized reference expressed in vehicle-acceleration and angular-velocity coordinates. The resulting motion reference is then used in an Iterative Feedback Tuning (IFT)-style procedure for fixed-structure PI and LQR controllers. In the considered simulation scenario, the selected SVC target reduces the sequence norm by 6.95% relative to the baseline. Controller tuning with reduced response models decreases the regularized PI and LQR objectives by 49.5% and 32.3%, respectively. These results show that a nonlinear physiological comfort objective can be converted into a practical motion reference for tuning fixed-structure vehicle controllers.

items.title: Trade-off Between Airspace and Channel Capacity for Low-altitude Wireless Network
items.summary: Communication-serviceable capacity for low-altitude unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) networks depends on both spatial occupancy and wireless quality of service (QoS). This paper formulates a communication-feasible occupancy-planning model that maps candidate-grid assignments to concurrent beam loads and per-user rates under fixed-stream and fixed-beam power. With fixed effective noise, per-beam QoS screening determines maximum admission, and an exact dynamic program maximizes aggregate spectral efficiency at that fixed admission. Signal-level simulations validate the SINR expressions, while an explicit-array model examines load-dependent inter-beam leakage. The dynamic program is globally optimal for the separable integer problem, but that guarantee does not extend to the coupled problem. Equal-time orthogonal multiple access (OMA) and ideal-SIC non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) are evaluated through the same local beam reduction under fixed effective noise and fixed per-beam power.

items.title: Time-Window Noise2Noise: Self-Supervised Blind Denoising of Mechanical Vibration and Impact Signals
items.summary: Vibration and impact measurements in mechanical systems are invariably corrupted by noise, which degrades every quantity derived from them, such as modal parameters and contact forces. Classical filters rely on assumptions about the noise or the signal, and linear filters cannot remove the noise that shares the frequency band of the structural response. This work presents Time-Window Noise2Noise (TWN2N), a self-supervised method for blind denoising of signals produced by deterministic mechanical systems. The method requires neither a clean reference signal nor paired noisy observations, nor a measured noise variance or distribution: by reconstructing each time instant from its temporal neighborhood while masking the instant itself, a compact autoencoder-based network is encouraged to exploit the coherent temporal and multichannel structure of the measurement rather than the noise. The formulation requires no model of the system and is assessed on two benchmarks with exactly known ground truth: the impulse response of a linear 3-degree-of-freedom system and a nonlinear Hunt-Crossley impact. Over repeated realizations, TWN2N exceeds a zero-phase low-pass filter at low and moderate input signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and gives the largest gain inside the structural band, which a linear filter largely preserves, among the Savitzky-Golay and wavelet references; the advantage vanishes at high input SNR and under brown noise. The benefit propagates to identification: the damping ratio of the weakest mode, overestimated several-fold on the raw signals, is recovered close to its reference value after denoising.

items.title: Algebraic Diversity: Group-Theoretic Spectral Estimation from Single Observations
items.summary: We establish that temporal averaging over multiple observations is the degenerate case of algebraic group action with the trivial group $G=\{e\}$. A General Replacement Theorem proves that, under signal equivariance and noise ergodicity, a group-averaged estimator from one snapshot achieves equivalent subspace decomposition to multi-snapshot covariance estimation. The Trivial Group Embedding Theorem proves that the sample covariance is the accumulation of trivial-group estimates, with variance governed by a $(G,L)$ continuum as $1/(d_{\mathrm{eff}}\cdot L)$, where $d_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the effective dimension of the group average. For group-matched signals the processing gain is up to $10\log_{10}(M)$ dB, the classical beamforming gain, showing that this gain is set by the matched group and not by sensor count. The DFT, DCT, and KLT are unified as group-matched special cases. We conjecture a General Algebraic Averaging Theorem extending these results to arbitrary statistics, with variance governed by $d_{\mathrm{eff}}$. Monte Carlo experiments on the first four sample moments are consistent with the conjecture in the scalar case. The framework exploits the structure of information (representation-theoretic symmetry of the data object) rather than the content, complementing Shannon's theory. Four applications are demonstrated: single-snapshot MUSIC, massive MIMO, single-pulse waveform classification, and graph signal processing. Earlier quantitative claims on transformer LLMs are retracted. Techniques for blind group matching are described.

items.title: Training-Free Continuous Bitrate Control for Scalable Image Coding for Humans and Machines
items.summary: Continuous variable-rate compression is highly demanded in real-world applications, but remains underexplored in scalable image coding for humans and machines. In this paper, we propose a training-free variable-rate scalable image coding framework. By adaptively adjusting quantization step sizes based on predicted scale values, the proposed method enables independent and continuous bitrate control for the machine and enhancement layers while preserving important latent information in each layer. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method and highlight the importance of bitrate allocation between the two layers.

items.title: Generalizable Variable-Rate Adaptation for Image Coding for Machines
items.summary: Image Coding for Machines (ICM) aims to preserve task-relevant information for machine vision under limited bitrates. However, most ICM models are trained for a fixed operating point, and extending them to variable-rate compression is challenging because their training objectives differ across tasks and model designs. In this paper, we propose a loss-agnostic distillation framework for variable-rate ICM. A pretrained fixed-rate ICM model is used as a frozen teacher, while a student model learns variable-rate behavior through importance-adaptive quantization and distillation-based optimization. This enables continuous bitrate control with a single model while preserving task-relevant latent components, without requiring the original task-specific loss or downstream task labels. Experiments based on existing ICM models demonstrate that the proposed method provides continuous bitrate control and achieves competitive recognition performance compared with the fixed-rate models.

items.title: Data-Driven Domain of Attraction Estimation via Convergent Koopman-Zubov Approximation
